Dear Donald,
You hand-picked Michael Whatley for the U.S. Senate and we all know he'll do anything you tell him if he's elected. He's about to get crushed, and you should see the loss for what it is: a direct repudiation of your failed leadership in the White House. When he loses on November 3rd, that loss is yours too, buddy.
I want to tell you why it's going to happen, because none of the sycophants around you will.
Here's the short version. You told North Carolinians you'd fight for working families. Then you governed for your billionaire donors, your family and yourself. North Carolinians have been totally screwed by high costs and they're pissed off. Now here's the long version.
#### **Reason one: You can 't gerrymander a Senate race.**
I used to serve in Congress. Your MAGA buddies in the NC General Assembly drew me out of my seat. Then they did it again for Don Davis' district last year, after you told them to. You can gerrymander a House district but you can't gerrymander the borders of our state. Every voter in North Carolina gets the same ballot and an equal say in this race.
#### **Reason two: Western North Carolina remembers Helene.**
You stood in Swannanoa and promised to help. Then you walked away. Your FEMA turned down Governor Stein's request to keep covering all of the debris removal and emergency costs, calling it "not warranted," and never explained why. This summer you sent Congress an $88 billion war funding request with zero dollars for Helene. Even Republican Sen. Ted Budd told Congress in July that too many projects in western North Carolina have stalled for lack of money. And last month in Gastonia, you told the crowd that if Whatley loses, you're not sending the money.
#### **Reason three: You slashed our health care to cut taxes for the rich.**
You can't claim to fight for working people when you cut their hospitals and health care. You can't claim to fight for working people when your bill puts health coverage at risk for 680,000 North Carolinians. And you definitely can't claim to fight for working people when you do it all to pay for tax breaks for the richest people in America. Your big ugly bill cut nearly $1 trillion from Medicaid. Our hospitals could lose $32 billion over the next decade, putting the rural hospitals that serve 80 of our 100 counties at risk. Even Thom Tillis warned you. You called him a "talker and complainer" and said he was "screwing the Republican party." He was telling you the truth.
#### **Reason four: You work for the billionaires. Period.**
During the last campaign you said, "when I win, I will immediately bring prices down, starting on day one." Here's what your big ugly bill actually does. The top 1% get an average tax cut of about $66,000 next year. Altogether, that's $117 billion for the richest 1% in a single year. The bottom 20% get a tax cut worth less than 1% of their income, and then lose more than that in health care and food assistance cuts. The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office found that an earlier version of your bill would cost the poorest 10% of households about $1,600 a year. It's a big ugly bill written by and for the ultra-rich.
#### **Reason five: Our farmers are paying for your tariffs.**
Ask [Brandon Batten](https://substack.com/redirect/5d4956b0-900c-41df-a29a-dfae29ac2dc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). His family farms soybeans at Triple B Farms in Four Oaks. Last fall, China stopped buying American soybeans because of your trade war, and he was left wondering who would take their place. "We need all the markets we can get," he said. A report from the conservative John Locke Foundation estimates your tariffs could [cost North Carolina farmers about $695 million](https://substack.com/redirect/2d33445d-c052-4cc6-a03a-406724820c79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), roughly a third of average net farm income. That's not a liberal talking point. That's your own side's think tank. The head of the state's soybean growers [put it plainly](https://substack.com/redirect/0dbcbff1-77a1-4f9d-8f8c-c16e91d29d6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "We're losing good farmers."
#### **Reason six: You made everything cost more.**
The day before you started your war with Iran, gas in North Carolina averaged about $2.75. Diesel shot up 71%, from $3.39 in January to a record $5.81 in April, and then broke that record again in September, topping $6. Just ask the Byrd family, who farm tobacco, corn, wheat and soybeans in Harnett County. In September, R.H. Byrd Jr. said diesel was running about $6.20 a gallon, roughly $2.75 more than a year earlier. "The cost of diesel is one of our biggest challenges," he said. Gas was still around $4 a gallon in Wendell earlier this month. Food prices are through the roof. Diesel moves our food, our lumber and just about everything on a store shelf. When it spikes, everything costs more. And your answer was that high energy costs are a "very small price to pay." Not for billionaires like you. For farmers in Harnett County, for the trucker in Kinston and for the mom in Garner filling up her minivan, it's a choice between gas and food.
#### **Reason seven: You took us into a war with Iran with no plan and no end in sight.**
You chose this war against Iran. You launched it on February 28th without coming to Congress. Nearly eight months later, the Pentagon counts 21 American service members dead and 865 wounded. A Fort Bragg soldier, 1st Lt. Tyler Feehan, was one of two killed in an Iranian attack on a base in Jordan. Our 82nd Airborne paratroopers are still over there, and their deployment has been extended into next year. There's still no plan to bring our people home. Every one of those costs is on you. Your own Pentagon says this war has already cost over $45 billion, and that doesn't count rebuilding all of the damaged bases. Moody's chief economist says it's [cost the average American household nearly $2,000](https://substack.com/redirect/46b7dd21-4bc9-4046-9b9b-b8b2afa48d11?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and counting. What happened to no more forever wars?
#### **Reason eight: DOGE gutted the Triangle.**
When DOGE started cutting grants, North Carolina's 4th District was the hardest hit in the country, losing 186 federal grants. RTI lost about $1 billion and laid off a third of its workforce. Our state health department lost more than $100 million in grants and cut more than 80 jobs, including work on immunizations and addiction treatment.
#### **Reason nine: You sent ICE raids into North Carolina.**
North Carolinians want a secure border. We also believe every person deserves to be treated with dignity. Last November, you sent the federal agents from your Charlotte operation into Raleigh and Cary.
You said you were going after the "worst of the worst." The numbers say otherwise. Of the more than 1,100 people arrested in North Carolina during and right after your Charlotte operation, just 30% had ever been convicted of a crime. Nationally, it's worse. Leaked federal data analyzed by the [libertarian Cato Institute](https://substack.com/redirect/6ff0c78c-386b-449a-925f-757800d78468?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) shows 73% of people booked into ICE detention had no criminal convictions at all. Only 5% had a violent conviction. That's not public safety. That's theater. And it's dangerous theater. In Minneapolis, an ICE officer shot and killed Renee Good, a 37-year-old mother. Weeks later, federal agents shot and killed Alex Pretti, an ICU nurse who cared for veterans. Deaths in ICE custody in 2025 were the highest in more than 20 years, and this year has already broken the all-time record.
I'm about to be Wake County's top prosecutor. I know what actually makes a community safer: going after violent criminals. That's not what you're doing.
#### **Reason ten: Your pardons are totally indefensible.**
I take the rule of law very seriously. You pardoned roughly 1,500 people charged in connection with the January 6th attack on the Capitol. Police officers were beaten that day. Their convicted attackers walked. Then you pardoned Changpeng Zhao, the Binance founder who pleaded guilty to money laundering, after Binance helped your family's crypto company land a $2 billion deal. When reporters asked, you said you didn't know who he was. In your America, if you're rich, connected or useful to the Trump family, the law just doesn't apply.
#### **Reason eleven: You 're cashing in while we pay more.**
While North Carolina families cut back, Forbes estimates your family nearly doubled its fortune to about $10 billion since the 2024 election. Your own financial disclosure reports at least [$1.4 billion in 2025 from your crypto](https://substack.com/redirect/3ad3c636-1c5c-4fdb-998d-a38e3f779c60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and memecoin businesses. One of them, World Liberty Financial, you co-founded with your sons and Steven Witkoff, who's now one of your top diplomats. Then there's the plane. Qatar's royal family handed over a $400 million Boeing 747, and you promised it would go to your presidential library. North Carolinians can't accept a free car from a lobbyist. You accepted a jumbo jet from a foreign government. You're running the most corrupt White House ever, and it isn't even close.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6fb2c455-abd5-49db-ab7e-9926e1ca3c56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### **And the last reason: Roy Cooper.**
You've thrown everything you've got at [Roy Cooper](https://substack.com/redirect/4fcf1312-7701-4a28-898c-996fe4fd279a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). You called him "radical left" and blamed him for the slow Helene recovery your own administration dragged out. You compared him to Michael Dukakis and Willie Horton and said he "DISGRACED North Carolina" and "disqualified himself from Public Office!" Now you're telling people our cities are "blood-soaked killing fields." North Carolinians know better. Roy Cooper has never lost an election. Voters have trusted him statewide again and again. They're about to do it one more time.
Here's the thing you'll never understand, Donald. The power of the presidency is real. But it's nothing compared to the power of North Carolinians standing in line at a polling place with a ballot in their hands. You can redraw maps. You can pardon your friends. You can take a jet from Qatar, but you can't stop what's coming on Tuesday, November 3rd.
So enjoy your breakfast on November 4th. Then start preparing to blame everyone but yourself for the upcoming blowout.
And if you're reading this and you're not Donald Trump: [NC early voting is open now](https://substack.com/redirect/17e24de5-ae0f-463f-941b-4974fd6e670e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) through October 31st. [Go vote for Roy Cooper](https://substack.com/redirect/4fcf1312-7701-4a28-898c-996fe4fd279a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Let's send a message so loud they hear it all the way in Mar-a-Lago.
Wiley

PS: Want to meet the guy leading the fight to flip the NC House? Robert Reives, the Democratic Leader in the House, is coming to my home in Cary on Thursday, October 22nd. The head of the state's soybean growers : "We're losing good farmers." Reason six: You made everything cost more. The day before you started your war with Iran, gas in North Carolina averaged about $2.75. Diesel shot up 71%, from $3.39 in January to a record $5.81 in April, and then broke that record again in September, topping $6. Just ask the Byrd family, who farm tobacco, corn, wheat and soybeans in Harnett County. In September, R.H. Byrd Jr. said diesel was running about $6.20 a gallon, roughly $2.75 more than a year earlier. "The cost of diesel is one of our biggest challenges," he said. For farmers in Harnett County, for the trucker in Kinston and for the mom in Garner filling up her minivan, it's a choice between gas and food. Tyler Feehan, was one of two killed in an Iranian attack on a base in Jordan. Our 82nd Airborne paratroopers are still over there, and their deployment has been extended into next year. Your own Pentagon says this war has already cost over $45 billion, and that doesn't count rebuilding all of the damaged bases. Moody's chief economist says it's and counting. body:
The Houston Chronicle recently endorsed me, and what they wrote about Abbott says everything you need to know.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
**Last week, the Houston Chronicle, the paper of record in Texas’s largest city, endorsed me for governor.**
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261020_1_houston.L8GOwV&refcode=em20261020-2480&t=1&akid=2480%2E299639%2E5yiNxm)
I want to be honest about something: when I met with their editorial board in February, they didn’t think Greg Abbott had much to worry about. They said so right in the endorsement. I was a state rep with little name recognition outside Austin, running against a three-term incumbent with a $106 million war chest.
Eight months later, they’ve endorsed me.
**But what stuck with me most in their endorsement wasn’t what they said about me. It was what they said about how much Greg Abbott has changed.**
Texans first met Abbott in the ’90s, when he ran for judge in Houston. Back then he came across as a moderate, Bush-era Republican who even picked up Democratic votes. Three decades later, the Chronicle calls him a “relentless, hardcore MAGA standard-bearer.”
Look at what he’s done with the power he’s been given:
* Texas currently has the most people without health insurance, the most people being disconnected from their electricity, and the most bankruptcies of any state.
* He stripped Texas communities of local control.
* And he’s taken care of the billionaires who fund him:
* A $1 million check from a gas tycoon whose company cashed in during Winter Storm Uri.
* $12 million from a Pennsylvania billionaire while Abbott pushed vouchers that drain money from rural public schools.
* A billion dollars a year in tax breaks for data centers.

**That’s the question at the heart of this race: which Texans does Greg Abbott serve? It isn’t working families.**
When I left that editorial board meeting, I told them I think people are tired of fighting. Tired of a government that works for the powerful instead of for them. **After 30 years of one-party rule, Texans are ready for change.**
Early voting is going on _right now_. Abbott still has $17 million to spend, and he’ll use every dollar to keep things exactly the way they are.
If you’ve been waiting to make your first contribution, let this be the moment. [**Will you chip in $15 to help us bring our message to every Texan throughout early voting?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1374?c0=em_ms_gh_20261020_1_houston.gDh357&refcode=em20261020-2480&t=3&akid=2480%2E299639%2E5yiNxm)

Thank you,
Gina

body:

Right now, we're facing a significant budget gap -- and it means we're at risk of having to pull the plug on some of our TV ads, just 14 days before the election...

And over and over throughout American history, Georgia — the cradle of the Civil Rights Movement — has been a place where courageous people on the right side of history have made a transformative impact.
So, not for the sake of my career ... and not for the sake of the Democratic Party ... but for the sake of our country: These final 2 weeks in Georgia matter an awful lot.
If that’s all you need to hear, use this link to chip in to my reelection campaign today: [**https://act.electjon.com/go/Georgia**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261020-1-f&utm_campaign=em261020-1-f&t=2&akid=3130%2E5691347%2EN3U3dw)

Trump and his big money MAGA machine will do whatever it takes to replace me with his puppet, who is pro-war, pro-tariff, and pro-cutting your health care.
Before my election to the U.S. Senate, I led a team that investigated and exposed war crimes, human rights abuses, official corruption and organized crime for international news organizations.
We helped courageous journalists smuggle the truth out of repressive societies with authoritarian governments.
And more and more, the United States under Donald Trump reminds me of those places.
That’s why we need to send a massive message this fall — a message so clear and a rebuke so decisive this fall that no president — of any party! — will dare anything like this again ... for centuries.
_That's_ the opportunity that we have this November.
And that will be a great service to our Republic.

Republicans are planning a
court takeover after the midterms.

Judiciary Chair Chuck Grassley has crammed two judicial nomination
hearings into November’s short session, with more on deck for December.
It’s his last stretch as chair, and he wants every seat he can get.

The timing is deliberate. Under Senate rules, any nomination still pending
when this Congress ends gets sent back to the White House, and the nominee
has to go through hearings and votes all over again. So Republicans are
racing to confirm Trump’s picks before then.

While the country’s attention is on the election results, Republicans will
be putting Trump’s cronies on the bench for life.

This is nothing new. The Senate has confirmed 56 of his judges this
Congress, including 10 to the appeals courts. District nominees are
getting through in a third of the time they took in Trump’s first term.^1

Trump hand-picked every one of them. They’ll be ruling on our fundamental
rights and enabling his abuses of power for decades.

So we have one message for every Democrat in the Senate right now: no
votes for Trump’s judges. Not in November and not in December.

Grassley is counting on these confirmations sliding through. Every

**Save the Date: Army-Navy Policy Conference | December 11, 2026**
---
|
---
| | |
---
|
---
Friends, Please save the date for the fifth annual Army-Navy Warrior Policy Conference on Friday, December 11, 2026, at Fordham University in New York City, on the eve of one of America’s most storied traditions: the Army-Navy Football Game. Hosted by Secretary Patrick J. Murphy, Genine Fallon, Dan Kunze, and SitReps, the conference brings together leaders from the military, government, business, sports, technology, and academia for an afternoon of meaningful conversations about the future of American leadership, national security, innovation, and service. What began as a small gathering at the University of Pennsylvania has grown into a national convening, with previous conferences hosted at MIT, Georgetown, and Johns Hopkins. Along the way, our mission has remained the same: to bring together established leaders and the next generation of changemakers, creating connections that extend well beyond Army-Navy weekend. At its heart, this conference is about more than celebrating the values of service, teamwork, and leadership. It is about putting those values to work. From emerging defense technologies and public-private partnerships to veteran entrepreneurship and the evolving demands of national security, our conversations focus on the challenges and opportunities shaping America’s future. Event Details Date: Friday, December 11, 2026Time: 12:00–5:00 PMLocation: Fordham University, New York CityRegistration: 🔗 [REGISTRATION LINK](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141774698/654730194/673837616?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS8xMDYyMjAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMmRiNDQ2M2QtODZjYy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=gDpNh26rOKuFf_GuQFoGUV3sQwh6OE7lAG-0xuoHvgc=&emci=92dab933-bfcb-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=2db4463d-86cc-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=10957263) We look forward to welcoming an exceptional community of leaders, veterans, cadets, midshipmen, students, entrepreneurs, and innovators for an afternoon of ideas, connections, and collaboration. Please mark your calendars. We will be sharing additional announcements about our speakers, partners, and programming in the coming weeks. The Army-Navy Game reminds us what it means to serve something greater than ourselves. Our conference is about what we can accomplish together because of it. ### Are conventions archaic and does every voter deserves a say in the primary?

Somewhere in a red state this year, a donor-funded group will tell you party conventions are archaic and that every voter deserves a say in the primary. Count My Vote -- the Utah outfit that has run this campaign twice -- has already said the quiet part out loud. Here's executive director Taylor Morgan, on record in 2023: "If we do have to run a new initiative, it will be for direct primary elections only. The caucus convention path will no longer be a path to the public primary ballot." Not reform. Abolition. Caucuses may survive as a social club, but the convention would never again name a nominee. Utah is the test case, and it's a mistake -- the proof is a fifty-point swing.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/78127460-bca5-47e1-8ed5-826ae6d8dcb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The swing.** On April 27, 2024, nearly 4,000 Utah GOP delegates filed into the Salt Palace. Gov. Spencer Cox was booed. State Rep. Phil Lyman beat him at the convention 67.54% to 32.46%. Trent Staggs, endorsed by Trump that morning, took about 70% of the Senate delegate vote. Delegates looked past John Curtis, Brad Moore, and Celeste Maloy entirely. Then came the June 25 primary: Cox beat Lyman by about ten points, and Curtis -- who had skipped the convention and bought his way onto the ballot with signatures -- swamped Staggs roughly 49% to 32%. Count the swing: a thirty-five-point convention win flipped to a ten-point loss, and a 70% delegate candidate fell to 32% with actual voters. Call it _fifty points_ of separation between the two electorates.
That gap is the whole point. The delegates are the people who showed up to a school gymnasium in March, elected a neighbor, and spent months vetting candidates face to face. They are, statistically, the Republican Party's conservative core. The June primary is a mail-ballot electorate where name ID and ad dollars rule. Under the current law, SB54, the convention's verdict is merely advisory. Before 2014, a candidate who hit 70% at convention was the nominee -- no primary at all. Run that system today and Cox and Curtis types never survive the floor. Curtis, remember, was eliminated at a 2017 special convention and only reached Congress through the signature path. That's the track record the donor class is trying to bury.
**The filter that can 't be bought. **In 2010, Utah delegates dumped three-term Sen. Bob Bennett with 26.59% of the vote after his TARP vote -- a sustained cheer echoed through the hall as his defeat was announced. Mike Lee emerged from that convention. That's what the institution is for: a room where a schoolteacher with a pickup truck and three minutes at a microphone can end a thirty-year career, and where no A/B-tested ad buy can reach. A signature drive cannot be won that way. Signatures are bought -- paid circulators at per-name rates, six figures for a statewide race -- and the 2026 cycle already shows the rot: in Davis County, Utah, only thirteen candidates are going convention-only. Everyone else takes the money road, because it's the safe road. Signature-only makes the establishment's ballot line a subscription the party never cancels.
**The ratchet.** Count My Vote's history tells you what the compromise was always for. 2013: threaten an initiative. 2014: cut a deal -- SB54, dual path. 2017: relaunch the initiative anyway, signature-only, needing 113,000 signatures (polling split evenly by October). 2023: threaten again. Meanwhile the GOP spent a decade in court trying to restore its convention rights: the Tenth Circuit upheld SB54 two-to-one in 2018, the Supreme Court declined to hear it in March 2019, a second challenge died in the en banc process in 2024, and the Supreme Court has again declined to intervene. Every round, the ask shrinks in one direction only. Keep My Voice's pro-caucus counter-initiative didn't even collect signatures in 2018. Shoe leather can't outspend the donor class, and the ratchet only turns one way.
**One direction.** This isn't just Utah. In Colorado, DaVita's former CEO Kent Thiry bankrolled an initiative to make primaries open, add ranked-choice general elections, and do away with the caucus, assembly, and vacancy committees outright -- the machine's next target list. Virginia's GOP, a convention party for decades, resorted to a primary for its 2025 statewide slate. The drift always runs the same way: toward the primary the institutional money can win and away from the convention it can't.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0c6dfa2c-924f-4672-a8c9-b17ac2494980?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The honest caveat.** Convention picks lost their 2024 primaries -- Lyman by ten, Staggs by seventeen. Delegates can misread the broader electorate; defenders of the convention system should own that. But it's an argument for party rules -- restoring the 70% threshold, or at least binding the endorsement -- not for deleting the institution with a bankrolled ballot initiative. Delegates answer to their neighbors at the next caucus. A signature-gathering firm answers to whoever pays the invoice.
A party is the people who show up. Red-state volunteers have watched the signature path produce the exact nominees their conventions rejected, then watched courts and initiatives ensure it can never be undone. If the price of losing the delegate fight is abolishing the delegate fight, every activist in every red state will learn the same lesson: the rules only bind them. Keep the convention. It's the last room where fifty points of separation still means something.

Then came the June 25 primary: Cox beat Lyman by about ten points, and Curtis -- who had skipped the convention and bought his way onto the ballot with signatures -- swamped Staggs roughly 49% to 32%. Count the swing: a thirty-five-point convention win flipped to a ten-point loss, and a 70% delegate candidate fell to 32% with actual voters. Call it fifty points of separation between the two electorates. That gap is the whole point. The delegates are the people who showed up to a school gymnasium in March, elected a neighbor, and spent months vetting candidates face to face. They are, statistically, the Republican Party's conservative core. The June primary is a mail-ballot electorate where name ID and ad dollars rule. Under the current law, SB54, the convention's verdict is merely advisory. Before 2014, a candidate who hit 70% at convention was the nominee -- no primary at all. Run that system today and Cox and Curtis types never survive the floor. Curtis, remember, was eliminated at a 2017 special convention and only reached Congress through the signature path. That's the track record the donor class is trying to bury. The filter that can 't be bought. In 2010, Utah delegates dumped three-term Sen. Bob Bennett with 26.59% of the vote after his TARP vote -- a sustained cheer echoed through the hall as his defeat was announced. Mike Lee emerged from that convention. That's what the institution is for: a room where a schoolteacher with a pickup truck and three minutes at a microphone can end a thirty-year career, and where no A/B-tested ad buy can reach. A signature drive cannot be won that way. Signatures are bought -- paid circulators at per-name rates, six figures for a statewide race -- and the 2026 cycle already shows the rot: in Davis County, Utah, only thirteen candidates are going convention-only. Everyone else takes the money road, because it's the safe road. Signature-only makes the establishment's ballot line a subscription the party never cancels. The ratchet. Count My Vote's history tells you what the compromise was always for. 2013: threaten an initiative. 2014: cut a deal -- SB54, dual path. 2017: relaunch the initiative anyway, signature-only, needing 113,000 signatures (polling split evenly by October). 2023: threaten again. Meanwhile the GOP spent a decade in court trying to restore its convention rights: the Tenth Circuit upheld SB54 two-to-one in 2018, the Supreme Court declined to hear it in March 2019, a second challenge died in the en banc process in 2024, and the Supreme Court has again declined to intervene. Every round, the ask shrinks in one direction only. Keep My Voice's pro-caucus counter-initiative didn't even collect signatures in 2018. Shoe leather can't outspend the donor class, and the ratchet only turns one way. One direction. This isn't just Utah. In Colorado, DaVita's former CEO Kent Thiry bankrolled an initiative to make primaries open, add ranked-choice general elections, and do away with the caucus, assembly, and vacancy committees outright -- the machine's next target list. Virginia's GOP, a convention party for decades, resorted to a primary for its 2025 statewide slate. The drift always runs the same way: toward the primary the institutional money can win and away from the convention it can't. | | ---|---|--- The honest caveat. Convention picks lost their 2024 primaries -- Lyman by ten, Staggs by seventeen. Delegates can misread the broader electorate; defenders of the convention system should own that. But it's an argument for party rules -- restoring the 70% threshold, or at least binding the endorsement -- not for deleting the institution with a bankrolled ballot initiative. Delegates answer to their neighbors at the next caucus. A signature-gathering firm answers to whoever pays the invoice. A party is the people who show up. Red-state volunteers have watched the signature path produce the exact nominees their conventions rejected, then watched courts and initiatives ensure it can never be undone. If the price of losing the delegate fight is abolishing the delegate fight, every activist in every red state will learn the same lesson: the rules only bind them. Keep the convention. It's the last room where fifty points of separation still means something. Thanks for reading! This post is public so feel free to share it. You're currently a free subscriber to . Somewhere in a red state this year, a donor-funded group will tell you party conventions are archaic and that every voter deserves a say in the primary. Count My Vote -- the Utah outfit that has run this campaign twice -- has already said the quiet part out loud. Here's executive director Taylor Morgan, on record in 2023: "If we do have to run a new initiative, it will be for direct primary elections only. The caucus convention path will no longer be a path to the public primary ballot." Not reform. Abolition. Caucuses may survive as a social club, but the convention would never again name a nominee. Utah is the test case, and it's a mistake -- the proof is a fifty-point swing.

Introducing LinkUp: Text Your Friends to Get Out the Vote

We're excited to launch LinkUp, a new Right Insight feature that lets you personally text your friends and contacts. A message
from someone they know and trust is one of the most powerful ways to get people to the polls.

How to get started:

1. Log in to Right Insight and tap LinkUp at the bottom of your screen.

2. Tap Sync in the top right corner to upload your contacts. Give it a moment to load.

3. You'll now see your contacts, along with their voter registration status and how they're voting.

4. Tap a contact you'd like to message.

5. If you have more than one number for that person, select the right phone number.

6. Set your organization to Minnesota Republican Party.

7. Choose a pre-written message template, or type your own, then tap Send Message.

Texts go out directly from your phone, so your friends see a message from you, just like any other text.

At the Westport Library, I joined Congressman Jim Himes and Independent Party candidate Ben Wesley for a debate hosted by the League of Women Voters.
I appreciate the opportunity to discuss the issues that matter to residents of Fairfield County.
But several exchanges deserve further attention because they revealed fundamental differences in how Congressman Himes and I approach healthcare, Social Security, immigration enforcement, government spending, and public safety.
As a physician and attorney, I believe public policy should be evaluated by its actual results--not simply by the intentions behind it.
**Healthcare: Himes Agreed With Much of My Diagnosis. But What About the Cure?**
When I discussed the rising cost of healthcare, Congressman Himes acknowledged many of the problems I identified.
The American healthcare system has become enormously expensive. Physicians face increasing administrative requirements. Independent practices struggle to compete with large healthcare organizations. Insurance companies and hospital systems exercise tremendous influence over the care patients receive.
For more than forty years, I have practiced medicine. I have seen the effects of these changes firsthand.
I believe the healthcare system needs fundamental structural reform.
We must reduce unnecessary administrative burdens, restore competition, improve access to preventive medicine, and give patients greater negotiating power.
Congressman Himes emphasized the importance of Medicare negotiating prescription drug prices. That is an important policy tool, but it does not address every source of healthcare inflation.
**Lowering the price of selected medications is not the same as fixing the healthcare delivery system.**
We also disagreed over competition.
Congressman Himes expressed concern that healthcare cannot operate like an ordinary consumer marketplace because patients must have access to essential treatment regardless of income.
I agree with the importance of access. But competition and access are not opposites.
We can protect patients while allowing independent physicians, competing hospitals, community-based purchasing groups, and innovative healthcare providers to offer better care at lower costs.
My proposal includes community-based healthcare purchasing arrangements that could give large groups of patients greater bargaining power.
It also emphasizes preventive care. Properly managing diabetes, for example, can reduce the risk of serious complications, including kidney disease, cardiovascular disease, and vision loss.
As I previously explained in _[Stop Complaining. Start Voting.](https://substack.com/redirect/14f7eb1b-dc17-4439-807b-6a588e4340db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , healthcare should be centered on patients rather than bureaucracy.
The important question is how Congress will make care more affordable while preserving quality and access.
**Social Security: Himes Dismissed the Investment Question**
One of our most substantial disagreements involved Social Security.
Congressman Himes correctly identified demographic pressures on the program. Americans are living longer, and the ratio of workers to beneficiaries has declined.
But demographics are only one part of Social Security's financial structure.
I raised the issue of how Social Security Trust Fund reserves are invested.
Under federal law, these reserves are invested in special U.S. Treasury securities. They earn interest but are not diversified into equities or other assets as many traditional pension funds are.
My question was straightforward:
**Should Congress examine whether a carefully designed, diversified investment structure could improve long-term returns while protecting beneficiaries?**
Congressman Himes responded by referencing the 2008 financial crisis and the risks of stock market investment.
Market risk is real. It cannot be dismissed.
But neither can the potential effects of investment policy over multiple decades.
A responsible examination would consider investment returns, volatility, inflation, liquidity, the timing of benefit payments, and the guarantees that Social Security beneficiaries depend upon.
I am not proposing that retirees' monthly checks be exposed to uncontrolled market speculation.
Social Security Trust Fund money should be invested in a similar way that employee pension funds of governments and private industry are invested. There needs to be a balance between generating significant income from the investment and protecting against risk and market downturns.
I am proposing that Congress evaluate the alternatives before concluding that the only solutions are higher taxes, reduced benefits, or a later retirement age.
Social Security faces a significant financing shortfall. Investment diversification is not a proven stand-alone solution, and any proposal must be tested against actuarial projections.
Nevertheless, the question deserves serious examination.
**Our seniors deserve a system that protects the benefits they earned and is managed with long-term financial discipline.**
For background on my broader approach to retirement security, healthcare, and affordability, readers can visit [The Goldstein Substack](https://substack.com/redirect/69658584-971f-4be8-885f-54028d770f2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
**Violence Against Women: The Votes and the Due-Process Debate**
During the immigration discussion, I challenged Congressman Himes about his September 18, 2024 vote against H.R. 7909, the _Violence Against Women by Illegal Aliens Act_.
The bill proposed additional immigration consequences for specified domestic violence, sexual offenses, stalking, child abuse, and related conduct.
Congressman Himes voted against the measure.
During the debate, he explained his opposition in terms of constitutional due process.
I agree that constitutional protections are essential. Noncitizens are entitled to applicable due-process protections, and criminal allegations must be treated carefully.
However, the legislation's deportability provisions addressed specified criminal convictions, while other provisions addressed certain admissions of criminal conduct.
The legislation was not simply a proposal to deport individuals based on unsupported accusations.
Critics raised concerns about the breadth of its definitions and possible unintended consequences for survivors of domestic abuse. Those objections deserve to be understood rather than ignored.
There is also a subsequent development that voters should know: Congressman Himes voted for H.R. 30, a successor bill addressing these offenses, in January 2025.
That raises an important question about the difference between the two bills and whether his earlier concerns were resolved.
I believe we should protect women and children from violent offenders while preserving constitutional safeguards.
**Protecting victims and respecting due process should be complementary responsibilities, not competing political slogans.**
Voters can review the [September 2024 House vote on H.R. 7909](https://substack.com/redirect/026c2482-247a-4887-b279-c5a7d3fc3a4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and examine the legislation themselves.
**Government Benefits Fraud: What Should the Consequences Be?**
I also raised the issue of immigration-related fraud involving government programs.
On March 18, 2026, Congressman Himes voted against H.R. 1958, the _Deporting Fraudsters Act_.
The legislation proposed additional immigration consequences for certain noncitizens convicted of defrauding the federal government or unlawfully obtaining public benefits.
I believe deliberate fraud against taxpayer-funded programs should carry meaningful legal consequences.
At the same time, we must distinguish among undocumented immigrants, lawfully present noncitizens, eligible benefit recipients, and people convicted of fraud.
These are not interchangeable categories.
Federal benefit programs have different eligibility requirements, and undocumented immigrants are generally ineligible for many major federal benefits, subject to specific exceptions.
The central issue is whether existing enforcement mechanisms adequately deter fraud, recover public funds, and hold offenders accountable.
Congressman Himes opposed the proposed legislation. I believe the public deserves a clear explanation of the legal and policy reasons for that vote.
The [House roll call on H.R. 1958](https://substack.com/redirect/187ce4d0-50b3-428c-a91c-7b8d852b14a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) provides the voting record.
**Government must protect both the integrity of taxpayer-funded programs and the rights of people accused of wrongdoing.**
**Connecticut 's Affordability Crisis Extends Beyond Washington**
The debate also addressed energy, education, housing, and infrastructure.
I discussed Connecticut's high energy costs and the need to improve energy supply and infrastructure throughout New England.
Electricity and natural gas prices affect more than household utility bills.
They affect manufacturing, transportation, grocery prices, healthcare facilities, and the ability of businesses to expand.
I have previously discussed these issues in _[Stop Complaining. Start Voting.](https://substack.com/redirect/14f7eb1b-dc17-4439-807b-6a588e4340db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ and in my article about [the energy and economic challenges shared by New York and Connecticut](https://substack.com/redirect/425ba941-de4b-470f-8ddd-d875cafcc36a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
We also discussed the importance of protecting the Long Island Sound.
Development, stormwater runoff, sewage-treatment capacity are a greater issue than rising sea levels and development has taken away marshes and wetlands that serve as buffers to rising tides.
Early Voting is going on Now Through November 1st and Election Day is November 3rd.

clean_body: It is Time to Put This Doctor in the House | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The Goldstein Substack - A Father-Son Publication Dr. Goldstein is Running for Congress and his page can be found It is Time to Put This Doctor in the House | | | Oct 20 | | | | | | | | | | | | Eighteen years in Washington. Connecticut families still face rising costs, strained infrastructure, and difficult questions about the future. | | ---|---|--- At the Westport Library, I joined Congressman Jim Himes and Independent Party candidate Ben Wesley for a debate hosted by the League of Women Voters. I appreciate the opportunity to discuss the issues that matter to residents of Fairfield County. But several exchanges deserve further attention because they revealed fundamental differences in how Congressman Himes and I approach healthcare, Social Security, immigration enforcement, government spending, and public safety. As a physician and attorney, I believe public policy should be evaluated by its actual results--not simply by the intentions behind it. Healthcare: Himes Agreed With Much of My Diagnosis. But What About the Cure? When I discussed the rising cost of healthcare, Congressman Himes acknowledged many of the problems I identified. The American healthcare system has become enormously expensive. Physicians face increasing administrative requirements. Independent practices struggle to compete with large healthcare organizations. Insurance companies and hospital systems exercise tremendous influence over the care patients receive. For more than forty years, I have practiced medicine. I have seen the effects of these changes firsthand. I believe the healthcare system needs fundamental structural reform. We must reduce unnecessary administrative burdens, restore competition, improve access to preventive medicine, and give patients greater negotiating power. Congressman Himes emphasized the importance of Medicare negotiating prescription drug prices. That is an important policy tool, but it does not address every source of healthcare inflation. Lowering the price of selected medications is not the same as fixing the healthcare delivery system. We also disagreed over competition. Congressman Himes expressed concern that healthcare cannot operate like an ordinary consumer marketplace because patients must have access to essential treatment regardless of income. I agree with the importance of access. But competition and access are not opposites. We can protect patients while allowing independent physicians, competing hospitals, community-based purchasing groups, and innovative healthcare providers to offer better care at lower costs. My proposal includes community-based healthcare purchasing arrangements that could give large groups of patients greater bargaining power. It also emphasizes preventive care. Properly managing diabetes, for example, can reduce the risk of serious complications, including kidney disease, cardiovascular disease, and vision loss. As I previously explained in , healthcare should be centered on patients rather than bureaucracy. The important question is how Congress will make care more affordable while preserving quality and access. Social Security: Himes Dismissed the Investment Question One of our most substantial disagreements involved Social Security. Congressman Himes correctly identified demographic pressures on the program. Americans are living longer, and the ratio of workers to beneficiaries has declined. But demographics are only one part of Social Security's financial structure. I raised the issue of how Social Security Trust Fund reserves are invested. Under federal law, these reserves are invested in special U.S. Treasury securities. They earn interest but are not diversified into equities or other assets as many traditional pension funds are. My question was straightforward: Should Congress examine whether a carefully designed, diversified investment structure could improve long-term returns while protecting beneficiaries? Congressman Himes responded by referencing the 2008 financial crisis and the risks of stock market investment. Market risk is real. It cannot be dismissed. But neither can the potential effects of investment policy over multiple decades. A responsible examination would consider investment returns, volatility, inflation, liquidity, the timing of benefit payments, and the guarantees that Social Security beneficiaries depend upon. I am not proposing that retirees' monthly checks be exposed to uncontrolled market speculation. Social Security Trust Fund money should be invested in a similar way that employee pension funds of governments and private industry are invested. There needs to be a balance between generating significant income from the investment and protecting against risk and market downturns. I am proposing that Congress evaluate the alternatives before concluding that the only solutions are higher taxes, reduced benefits, or a later retirement age. Social Security faces a significant financing shortfall. Investment diversification is not a proven stand-alone solution, and any proposal must be tested against actuarial projections. Nevertheless, the question deserves serious examination. Our seniors deserve a system that protects the benefits they earned and is managed with long-term financial discipline. For background on my broader approach to retirement security, healthcare, and affordability, readers can visit . Violence Against Women: The Votes and the Due-Process Debate During the immigration discussion, I challenged Congressman Himes about his September 18, 2024 vote against H.R. 7909, the Violence Against Women by Illegal Aliens Act. The bill proposed additional immigration consequences for specified domestic violence, sexual offenses, stalking, child abuse, and related conduct. Congressman Himes voted against the measure. During the debate, he explained his opposition in terms of constitutional due process. I agree that constitutional protections are essential. Noncitizens are entitled to applicable due-process protections, and criminal allegations must be treated carefully. However, the legislation's deportability provisions addressed specified criminal convictions, while other provisions addressed certain admissions of criminal conduct. The legislation was not simply a proposal to deport individuals based on unsupported accusations. Critics raised concerns about the breadth of its definitions and possible unintended consequences for survivors of domestic abuse. Those objections deserve to be understood rather than ignored. There is also a subsequent development that voters should know: Congressman Himes voted for H.R. 30, a successor bill addressing these offenses, in January 2025. That raises an important question about the difference between the two bills and whether his earlier concerns were resolved. I believe we should protect women and children from violent offenders while preserving constitutional safeguards. Protecting victims and respecting due process should be complementary responsibilities, not competing political slogans. Voters can review the and examine the legislation themselves. Government Benefits Fraud: What Should the Consequences Be? I also raised the issue of immigration-related fraud involving government programs. On March 18, 2026, Congressman Himes voted against H.R. 1958, the Deporting Fraudsters Act. The legislation proposed additional immigration consequences for certain noncitizens convicted of defrauding the federal government or unlawfully obtaining public benefits. I believe deliberate fraud against taxpayer-funded programs should carry meaningful legal consequences. At the same time, we must distinguish among undocumented immigrants, lawfully present noncitizens, eligible benefit recipients, and people convicted of fraud. These are not interchangeable categories. Federal benefit programs have different eligibility requirements, and undocumented immigrants are generally ineligible for many major federal benefits, subject to specific exceptions. The central issue is whether existing enforcement mechanisms adequately deter fraud, recover public funds, and hold offenders accountable. Congressman Himes opposed the proposed legislation. I believe the public deserves a clear explanation of the legal and policy reasons for that vote. The provides the voting record. Government must protect both the integrity of taxpayer-funded programs and the rights of people accused of wrongdoing. Connecticut 's Affordability Crisis Extends Beyond Washington** The debate also addressed energy, education, housing, and infrastructure. I discussed Connecticut's high energy costs and the need to improve energy supply and infrastructure throughout New England. Electricity and natural gas prices affect more than household utility bills. They affect manufacturing, transportation, grocery prices, healthcare facilities, and the ability of businesses to expand. I have previously discussed these issues in and in my article about . We also discussed the importance of protecting the Long Island Sound. Development, stormwater runoff, sewage-treatment capacity are a greater issue than rising sea levels and development has taken away marshes and wetlands that serve as buffers to rising tides. ---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

Here are **10 reasons** why neighbors and families across CD2 are backing Eric Pratt:

1. **30 years in banking and risk management.** Eric led teams that prevented fraud and managed risk. He knows how to manage real budgets and protect your hard-earned money.
2. **Proven local track record.** On the Prior Lake–Savage School Board, Eric helped eliminate debt, build a budget surplus, lower property taxes, and improve local schools.
3. **Stopping fraud before it starts.** In the private sector, Eric caught financial scams. He’ll bring that same risk-management mindset to Washington to protect taxpayers from waste.
4. **Real financial accountability.** Eric doesn't ignore tough questions or gloss over bad balance sheets. He demands transparency and real accountability at every level of government.
5. **D1 gridiron discipline.** Playing Division I football under Hall of Fame Coach Bill McCartney taught Eric that execution, teamwork, and accountability matter far more than talk.
6. **Independent-minded leadership.** Eric isn't afraid to stand up to anyone in D.C. when federal policies hurt working families in Minnesota.
7. **Backed by grassroots support.** Eric raised his kids in the Second District and relies on neighbors in Dakota, Scott, Rice, Washington, and Le Sueur counties, not outsider money.
8. **He’s actually accessible.** Town halls, local coffee shops, and community events. No velvet ropes, no closed doors, and no handler-speak.
9. **Empowering small businesses.** Having worked in leadership at U.S. Bank and Target, Eric focuses on cutting red tape so local businesses can grow and hire.
10. **One simple standard before every vote.** Before casting a single vote, Eric asks one question: _"What is best for Minnesota families?"_

You might notice that NY-17 is squarely within that yellow region on the East Coast. That’s the New York media market. It’s the most populous media market in the country. It also doesn’t squarely map onto state lines. The New York media market stretches into New Jersey, Connecticut, and Pennsylvania. And you can’t just cut those states out when you place a buy. I’ve said over and over again that New York is the single most expensive place in the country to run a political campaign. And a huge chunk of the reason for it is just how difficult it is to run a robust and targeted ad program in this media market. To get around that, our campaign has heavily invested in other ways to reach voters. We’ve built a historic field program that has knocked on tens of thousands of doors. * **Christina Hines (MI-10)** — A prosecutor and mom on a mission, Christina is running to flip Michigan’s open 10th Congressional District, currently represented by MAGA loyalist John James.
* **Cait Conley (NY-17)** — A decorated combat veteran and national security expert, Cait is no stranger to tough fights. Now, she’s running to defeat Trump ally Rep. Mike Lawler and flip New York’s 17th Congressional District.
* **Paige Cognetti (PA-08)** — As mayor of Scranton, Paige has helped lead the city through financial recovery and community renewal. She’s bringing that same grit to the race for Pennsylvania’s 8th Congressional District, currently held by corrupt Republican Rep. Rob Bresnahan Jr.
* **Janelle Stelson (PA-10)** — An Emmy Award-winning broadcast journalist, Janelle came within about one point of defeating Rep. Scott Perry last cycle. With the right resources, she can cross the finish line this November and flip this seat.

| Friend,
---
I’m going to admit something to you that’s deeply personal...
---
**_I’m about to confront the hardest battle I’ve ever faced in my 82 years on this earth, and the price of failure could be the _REST OF MY LIFE_._**
---
**You see, Democrats are on the brink of taking back the House, IMPEACHING President Trump __again__ , and resuming their LAWFARE against his political allies and confidantes like me.**
---
To make matters even worse, the radical Democrat Attorney General who is forcing me to stand in yet another RIGGED trial for bogus state-level crimes – _since President Trump can’t save me with a federal pardon_ – is currently in the process of _WINNING_ reelection – and she’s made her LAWFARE against me a key part of her campaign:
---
**"Trump, politics and _lawfare_ take center stage in Arizona's attorney general race" (KJZZ Phoenix)**
---
If (God forbid) she does indeed win reelection on November 3rd, she’s going to use her victory as a mandate to escalate her vicious crusade to throw me in prison as an innocent man.
---
_How did we get to the point where Democrat candidates can run – and potentially win – on a platform that includes JAILING their political opponents? We’re about to hit the point of no return..._
---
But I want to be perfectly clear, Friend: **__This isn’t just about MY freedom.__**
---
I’m 82 years old. In May, I was taken to the hospital, fell into a coma, placed on a ventilator, and read my last rites. I’ve already faced far worse than anything the Democrats can throw at me.
---
**No – this is about the freedom of every American. Because if I lose this battle, this same injustice will happen to another innocent patriot who stands up for what he knows to be right and true.**
---
_This is about making sure that my trial (and possibly, my subsequent imprisonment) doesn’t go down in history as the moment that our country collapsed into full-blown Marxist tyranny._
---
_This is about SAVING the United States of America and our _FREE_ Republic._
---
That’s why no matter what the Democrats do to me; I will NEVER back down.
---
They can strip me of all my earthly possessions. They can drag me through a RIGGED trial. They can threaten me with LIFE in prison.
---
I’d rather face all that – **_and if it comes down to it, spend the rest of my life in a prison cell as an innocent man_** – than throw in the towel and surrender to the Democrats.
---
Trust me, I don’t scare easily.
---
I fought the Mafia, I fought violent criminals, I fought corruption, and I fought the Deep State agents who tried to frame and destroy my client and friend – President Trump.
---
But I’m humble enough to know that my spirit and resolve alone won’t be enough to win this legal battle for my freedom. It’s going to require a top-notch legal defense team.
---
That’s why I'm humbly asking generous conservatives like _YOU_ for help as I fight the toughest battle of my life to defeat this vicious Democrat LAWFARE.
---
_With Election Day right around the corner, I understand that you’re probably being bombarded with tons of spam right now. So I want to thank you for taking the time to read this message. And if you can’t afford to donate to help me in this fight, I get it – I really do. Don’t think twice about deleting this email._
---
However, if you can help me, I truly need it more than ever before.

People often ask...how did I get that name?

| [](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMjBfQVQtU0kuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDY0MzI1LTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDIwX0FULVNJLjExMDExN190MjA2NDMyNS0yMDY4In0/uU3r7qouj_J0kQNSYbMyLA)
---
That’s a picture of me from when I flew H-46 and H-3 helicopters in the U.S. Navy. If you look to my left, you can see my call sign...**Blossom.**
People often ask...how did I get that name?
Well, my roommate in flight school and I went on a bit of a “girl power” kick one day and bought old bathtub non-skid flower stickers from the store, cut out that flower shape in reflective tape from our squadron, and stuck those reflective flowers on our helmets.
There is very little room for making a Navy flight suit more “feminine,” but on cruise we were able to be a little more creative and came to love those girly flowers on our helmets.
Although the helicopter community doesn’t use call signs as much as some of the fixed wing squadrons, the “Blossom” stuck and was painted on the side of a CH-46 for part of my first cruise. Made for a great photo and story!
It was my experience in the Navy that helped instill in me the importance of service.
Far too often, our elected officials today forget that their job is to SERVE. They think it is their job to tell everyone what to do and why everyone else is wrong....but that’s not service.
As a Navy veteran and nurse practitioner, I got so frustrated and decided to run for Congress because I wanted to actually SERVE my country and my community.
**While for some it is all about power, for me it is all about service.**
Sadly, this has made me some enemies in Washington.
No one is going to buy me off or tell me what to do...I’m going to keep serving the people I represent, not serve some “master” in Washington, D.C.
If you are also tired of leaders who care more about power than service, [I’m asking you to send me some help today.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMjBfQVQtU0kuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDY0MzI1LTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDIwX0FULVNJLjExMDExN190MjA2NDMyNS0yMDY4In0/Sv_8eKrrbFxjyd4tApCmOg)
Because I’m a veteran and not a career politician, I need all the help I can get to support my fight against the Democrats.
---
| [RUSH SUPPORT TO JEN](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMjBfQVQtU0kuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDY0MzI1LTIwNjgmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDIwX0FULVNJLjExMDExN190MjA2NDMyNS0yMDY4In0/cUMP_TYb4Lbixt1LTE9pWg)

It’s time we support leaders who truly want to serve our country, and that’s what I promise to always do...are you with me, Peter?
With the courage to fight,

#### **Troy Jackson Tweaks on Firefighters After Losing Endorsement**
Democratic candidate Troy Jackson is spending the final weeks of his U.S. Senate campaign showing off his temper. After telling Sen. Susan Collins to "shut up" during a debate, Jackson went on CNN visibly irritated with Dana Bash and refused to apologize. Last night, the ex-Senate President was raging on Facebook against the fire fighters union, which has endorsed his opponent, and the Maine Wire.
Under a Professional Fire Fighters of Maine post on Facebook, the union noted that Sen. Collins sponsored a bill giving collective bargaining rights to firefighters in right-to-work states. Troy Jackson replied, "I passed that bill twice in Maine." When one commenter chided Jackson, suggesting that he was going to claim taxpayer-funded reimbursements for his Facebook posting, Jackson fired back, "so the Maine Liar is your information source." To another Facebook commenter, Jackson unleashed his legendary Allagash wit: "yeah and the MAGA movement is helping the working class so much."
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.._AfiyTKNc6xOsnMNOtqB0SwfSWfJXh6aUPg8VFRpuls?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=221301940)
The exchange refers to the Maine Wire's investigative reporting, which shows that when Jackson was in the state legislature, he hauled in more than $160,000 in reimbursements for meals, lodging, and mileage -- more than any lawmaker in the history of the state. That's tax free, too. Jackson has never responded to our questions about his FHA mortgage, his reimbursements, or the legislation and public spending he backed that appears to have benefitted his family financially. Although he has taken to calling the Maine Wire "the Maine liar" (admittedly, devastatingly clever on his part), Jackson has never identified which part of our reporting is not accurate.

#### **[Suspicious Letters Sent to Two Collins Offices as Federal Authorities Investigate Nationwide Mailings](https://substack.com/redirect/d6e944a3-c647-4eab-aac0-b612d1d39f1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Pingree wasn't first. Two of Susan Collins' offices were sent suspicious letters containing an unknown white powder, Jon reports, and authorities intercepted both. Portland police and firefighters, a hazardous materials team and the FBI responded at her Portland office. The FBI wouldn't confirm specific letters, but said it and the Postal Inspection Service are investigating "a series of suspicious mailings" nationwide, including to secretaries of state and election offices. ABC News has reported more than 100 such letters in at least 19 states, and offices belonging to Ted Cruz, Kirsten Gillibrand and Raphael Warnock are among those reporting them. Collins' chief of staff, Katie Brown, said the mailings followed other recent threats aimed at the senator's offices or her home. Nobody has said publicly what the powder in Collins' letters is.
#### **[Car Reported Stolen From Auburn Ends Up in Sabattus Pond](https://substack.com/redirect/8e6cef80-630c-4491-8472-c2bee733a114?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Sabattus police started getting calls early Sunday about a car driving recklessly with its lights off. Officers say they watched it run the red light at Pleasant Hill Road and Route 126, lose control and go into Sabattus Pond. Inside were seven juveniles, some as young as 13. Two ran for the woods and were caught with help from a K9; the other five stayed put and cooperated. Police learned the car had been reported stolen from Auburn. Charges are pending, and it isn't clear whether anyone went to Long Creek or just home to their parents.
#### **[Man Stabbed Near Lewiston Dunkin' as City Confronts Youth Violence](https://substack.com/redirect/3733db35-ffa0-4ca1-b3f5-dd787102859b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
A 20-year-old was stabbed in the back and hit with brass knuckles in a fight near the Main Street Dunkin' on Saturday afternoon. Police arrested 18-year-old Alexander Keith at the scene, according to the Portland Press Herald, and say the two knew each other. The victim's injuries are serious but not life-threatening. The city's own numbers: 19 gun-violence incidents in the first six months of 2026, 12 of them involving juveniles. City officials have answered with $200,000 more in police overtime and a push to change how the state handles repeat violent juvenile offenders.
#### **[Man Charged With Robbery and Assault in Bangor, Police Say](https://substack.com/redirect/d33c14e6-2d12-40a6-b38e-2aefa87f36e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Bangor police say a man with blood on his hands, clothes and face flagged down an officer on Ohio Street around 5 p.m. Wednesday. He told her Justin Moulton, 43, listed as homeless, had demanded his money inside an Ohio Street apartment, hit him in the face and made him hand over his cash. Officers found Moulton and charged him with robbery and assault. Whose apartment it was is still unclear. Moulton was arrested in 2021 over an alleged attempt to steal a catalytic converter from a commercial truck.

**President Trump is in North Carolina today.**
The GOP has poured tens of millions into baseless attack ads against me - and now, Trump is here to double down on all of the lies and smears he uses against me at rallies and on his Truth Social. He's doing whatever he can to save Michael Whatley's campaign in the final two weeks of this election.
Where Trump goes, MAGA money follows, so I need your urgent support. **[We've set a rapid-response goal to raise $1 million to fight back against Trump, and I'm asking you to chip in $5 to help me hit it. Will you rush a donation before Trump takes the stage?](https://substack.com/redirect/c251f67a-4c0a-4b30-ac54-a30feaa23a31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/c251f67a-4c0a-4b30-ac54-a30feaa23a31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Trump can't stop ranting and raving about me. He says I'm part of the "radical left." He's called me a "total fraud." He's accused me of turning North Carolina's cities into "blood-soaked killing fields."
He's coming after me so hard because he knows this: If we fail to flip North Carolina from red to blue, Democrats will lose our chance at taking back the Senate.
We need to show Trump and the GOP the sheer strength of our grassroots movement, but we can't do that without hitting our $1 million goal. **[So please, will you chip in $5 or more right now to help me close the gap on this goal, flip North Carolina and take back the Senate for Democrats?](https://substack.com/redirect/c251f67a-4c0a-4b30-ac54-a30feaa23a31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

With just two weeks to go until the election, this can't wait.
Thank you,
Roy Cooper

---|---|---
Andy Biggs is running for governor of Arizona.
Let me tell you what Andy Biggs did.
On January 6th, 2021, while a mob was attacking my colleagues and me at the United States Capitol. Andy Biggs was one of the members of Congress who had spent weeks telling his constituents that the election was stolen. That their government was being taken from them. That what they were feeling. the rage, the urgency, the sense that something had to be done. was justified.
He fed that lie. Over and over. And then the people who believed him showed up.
I was there. I know what happened when they showed up. I held the line while they came at us with flagpoles and bear spray and their bare hands. I watched my colleagues get hurt. I watched people I worked alongside every day of my career take beatings for doing their jobs.
And Andy Biggs never had to answer for his part in it.
So I went to Arizona.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..DJjj11GB0VgaeY32sIRzki9YBpGNDcqX8f2q6lQ3Bmo?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=221324121)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4105d0bd-2629-437b-8503-e9e5b8221367?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Trump came to Arizona too. Showed up on October 14th to rally for Biggs, repeating the same lies about stolen elections that he's been telling since 2020. Still claiming Katie Hobbs rigged the 2022 governor's race. Six years later and they cannot let it go. Six years later and they are still telling the same story that got people killed and got people hurt and got my colleagues traumatized in ways they will carry for the rest of their lives.
Andy Biggs challenged the electoral results on January 6th. He voted against certifying a free and fair election. He helped build the lie and he has never walked it back. And now he wants to be the governor of Arizona. He wants to control how elections are run in one of the most contested states in the country.
That cannot happen.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/843b9008-797b-4fc2-a9ed-bb6ade2eb81b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I went to Arizona because accountability looks different now than it did five years ago. The people who physically attacked us got pardons. The Supreme Court gave the president immunity. The DOJ is running interference. The courts keep telling me I have no standing.
But I can show up. I can knock doors. I can look people in Arizona in the eye and say: I was there on January 6th. I know what this man helped cause. And I need you to vote him out.
Katie Hobbs is fighting for her second term against one of the architects of the biggest lie in American political history. That's not a policy debate. That's not Republicans versus Democrats. That's about whether we let the people who attacked our democracy get rewarded for it.
I'm not letting that happen without a fight.
I went to Arizona. I'll go back if I have to.
-Harry

clean_body: Andy Biggs is running for governor of Arizona. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more | | | Oct 20 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Andy Biggs is running for governor of Arizona. Let me tell you what Andy Biggs did. On January 6th, 2021, while a mob was attacking my colleagues and me at the United States Capitol. Andy Biggs was one of the members of Congress who had spent weeks telling his constituents that the election was stolen. That their government was being taken from them. That what they were feeling. the rage, the urgency, the sense that something had to be done. was justified. He fed that lie. Over and over. And then the people who believed him showed up. I was there. I know what happened when they showed up. I held the line while they came at us with flagpoles and bear spray and their bare hands. I watched my colleagues get hurt. I watched people I worked alongside every day of my career take beatings for doing their jobs. And Andy Biggs never had to answer for his part in it. So I went to Arizona. Trump came to Arizona too. Showed up on October 14th to rally for Biggs, repeating the same lies about stolen elections that he's been telling since 2020. Still claiming Katie Hobbs rigged the 2022 governor's race. Six years later and they cannot let it go. Six years later and they are still telling the same story that got people killed and got people hurt and got my colleagues traumatized in ways they will carry for the rest of their lives. Andy Biggs challenged the electoral results on January 6th. He voted against certifying a free and fair election. He helped build the lie and he has never walked it back. And now he wants to be the governor of Arizona. He wants to control how elections are run in one of the most contested states in the country. That cannot happen. | | ---|---|--- I went to Arizona because accountability looks different now than it did five years ago. The people who physically attacked us got pardons. The Supreme Court gave the president immunity. The DOJ is running interference. The courts keep telling me I have no standing. But I can show up. I can knock doors. I can look people in Arizona in the eye and say: I was there on January 6th. I know what this man helped cause. And I need you to vote him out. Katie Hobbs is fighting for her second term against one of the architects of the biggest lie in American political history. That's not a policy debate. That's not Republicans versus Democrats. That's about whether we let the people who attacked our democracy get rewarded for it. I'm not letting that happen without a fight. I went to Arizona. I'll go back if I have to. -Harry You're currently a free subscriber to . Every vote really does matter this year. Here’s how to cast yours early.

Friends,

Early voting starts TODAY across Wisconsin, and I ask you to make a plan to get your ballot in. We need you to bank your vote. I won't sugarcoat it. Control of Congress is at risk this year. The House majority could come down to a handful of seats and a few thousand votes, and Wisconsin is right in the middle of it. **Every vote really does matter.** It doesn't stop there. The races for Governor, Attorney General, and the State Legislature are all on the ballot, and each one will shape the future of Wisconsin for years to come. **Please vote the whole Republican ballot, top to bottom.** You can vote early in person at your local clerk's office or voting site now through Sunday, November 1. Hours and locations vary by community, so check yours at MyVote.wi.gov. It only takes a few minutes, and once your ballot is in, you're done. Remember to take your photo ID. When you go, I ask you to bring someone with you. Remind a friend, a neighbor, or a family member to vote too. That's how we win. We have just two weeks left.[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/T3I6v9xKOoX?e=561a28864e&c2id=c7ba3a2bb578965816da09c04ea0f7a1)[**If you're able, a contribution of any amount today helps us reach more voters before Election Day.**](https://us.list-manage.com/iDLYjdif1qG?e=561a28864e&c2id=c7ba3a2bb578965816da09c04ea0f7a1)
Thank you for standing with me. Let's get it done! Scott Fitzgerald

**TUESDAY, OCTOBER 20, 2026**
If truth be told, there were days when I would gladly have handed off the baton to anyone willing to take it. It was the faces of Benjamin, Daniel, Emily, Luis, and David that drove me to seek action from state and federal agencies and nonprofits. Still, I sometimes wonder whether my longing for personal relief drove me, too.
Then came a response from former Senator Marco Rubio's office. They forwarded my correspondence about Northeast Florida State Hospital to then Governor Rick Scott's office and asked for a response. Rubio's office later followed up to ask whether the matter had been addressed.
"If your neighbor comes to you for a cup of sugar," my grandmother would say, "give her the cup and another, if you have it to give. But when you need sugar, do not seek even a grain. Better spent is your time understanding why you have no sugar in your cupboard."
The cup of sugar may ease the moment. Understanding the scarcity begins the reckoning. Taking responsibility for what happens next--that is social reckoning.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper. **
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

We're debating whether the test is too hard. Or if math is racist.
Meanwhile, our children will compete with those who can do the math.
Artificial intelligence is changing how work gets done. But reading, reasoning, and communicating remain essential. A child who cannot evaluate an answer is poorly equipped to know when a machine gets it wrong.
**The age of abundance is not a participation trophy.**
Opportunity requires preparation. Preparation requires adults willing to tell the truth--and act on it.
[RESERVE YOUR SEAT TODAY](https://substack.com/redirect/32243784-52a0-4ea5-b66c-91b4948b2f65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
That's why we're bringing parents, educators, faith leaders, and community voices together for our **[2nd annual Faith, Family& Future Forum](https://substack.com/redirect/32243784-52a0-4ea5-b66c-91b4948b2f65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this Saturday, October 24, in Germantown, Philadelphia.**
After the forum, a limited number of attendees will have the opportunity to tour a historic Underground Railroad station. A reminder of the courage it took to move America closer to its founding promise that all men are created equal--and our responsibility to carry that work forward.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/32243784-52a0-4ea5-b66c-91b4948b2f65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
