This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Netanyahu tells Trump they have a "job to finish" in Iran: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu suggested that Israel and the United States could resume bombing Iran soon. The comments came in a call with President Donald Trump on Monday that Netanyahu posted a of on Monday. Netanyahu thanked Trump for his endorsement in the upcoming Israeli elections and said on Iran: "Donald, we have a job to finish. You said it, and we'll finish it together. We'll finish it, and no one else will do it." Axios: Hegseth meets Netanyahu at Israeli air base amid talks of renewed war with Iran: U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth Netanyahu at Ovda Air Base in southern Israel on Monday, where American fighter jets and refueling aircraft are deployed, according to Axios. The unannounced visit came eight days before Israel's elections and amid U.S.-Israeli discussions about potentially resuming major combat operations against Iran. Hegseth also met American troops stationed at the base. Iran warned Tuesday that any renewed U.S. military attack would be met with retaliation. "The era of 'hit-and-run' is over," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei , dismissing reports suggesting Washington could strike Iran's Pickax Mountain facility without provoking a response. "We have proven in practice that we absolutely do not leave attacks unanswered," he added. Baghaei also said Tehran had not entered negotiations with Washington, adding that diplomacy remained part of Iran's broader defense strategy. His remarks came as Pakistan's army chief, Asim Munir, was expected in Tehran on Tuesday for talks with Iranian officials, including discussions of negotiations between Iran and the U.S.. Oil hits five-month high: Oil prices Tuesday, with Brent crude reaching a five-month high of $111.75 a barrel, as traders weighed Ansarallah attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of attacks on commercial vessels near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps that renewed U.S. military action against Tehran would trigger a global energy crisis. "If America takes a new action--even a limited one--the world will face a serious energy crisis," IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi told the Tehran Times. He said Iran had not yet used its full capacity to close the Strait of Hormuz and warned that Tehran could draw on additional regional capabilities involving the Bab al-Mandab Strait and Suez Canal. "Our response this time will be far more severe and will land America in far bigger trouble," he said, adding that disruptions to energy supplies could become particularly damaging as Europe approaches winter. Iran and Russia have "never worked as closely as now," Araghchi says after Lavrov talks in Tehran: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tuesday that cooperation between Tehran and Moscow had reached an unprecedented level following talks with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Tehran. "Never in our history have Iran and Russia worked as closely as now," Araghchi on X, saying the two discussed developments in Lebanon, Palestine, Ukraine, and Yemen, alongside expanding economic and nuclear cooperation. Lavrov the talks as "highly fruitful, transparent and frank." Meanwhile, Trump said Washington continued to hit Iran hard, "economically and militarily," while praising Russia for taking a "very positive" stance in the conflict. Iran claims to have shot down 54th U.S. MQ-9 drone over Hormuz: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Tuesday that its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a U.S. MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz in the early hours of the morning, the 54th U.S. MQ-9 drone destroyed since the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran began on February 28. Iran says mines struck two tankers near Strait of Hormuz: Two tankers and were stopped after striking naval mines laid along an "illegal route" south of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said. The IRGC warned that vessels crossing the mined route risk being set ablaze and that oil companies would "pay a bigger price" if U.S. military operations continued. Separately, Iran's Strait of Hormuz Management Authority said it had added 122 vessels to a list of ships allegedly violating its maritime regulations and had taken action against more than 40 others. The authority claimed it was negotiating with 19 vessels, two of which had agreed to meet its requirements to be removed from the list, while approximately 30 others had received warnings and faced possible inclusion. Tanker involved in incident with military forces off Oman 's coast: A tanker was involved in an incident with unidentified military forces approximately 121 nautical miles east of Oman's coast on Tuesday, the UK Maritime Trade Operations reported. The agency did not report any details on casualties or damage. Palestine Israeli attacks kill five Palestinians, including two children, in Gaza: Israeli forces two Palestinians and wounded several others in a strike on a residential apartment in western Gaza City on Tuesday, WAFA reported. In southern Gaza, Israeli forces shot and killed a child in Khan Younis, while another child was killed by Israeli gunfire in Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza. UN teams 50 Israeli airstrikes and attacks a day across Gaza over the past week, despite the ceasefire, AP reported. Israeli forces and settlers attack Palestinian olive harvesters, impose siege on occupied West Bank village: Salfit: Israeli settlers olive trees and stole agricultural equipment in the Al-Wad Al-Ahmar area, east of Marda village, on Tuesday, according to WAFA. Ramallah: Settlers to a welcome monument at the entrance to Burqa village, causing extensive damage. Residents extinguished the blaze and began repairs. Nablus: Israeli forces a complete blockade of Madama village for a tenth consecutive day, restricting the movement of more than 2,500 residents and obstructing access to food, medicine, and ambulances. A resident suffering chest pains had to be carried on foot through the mountains after an ambulance was unable to reach him. The village council head said Israeli forces also fired toward residents attempting to bring in medicine. Settlers electricity to the home of a Palestinian family in Beita for a third consecutive day. The family reportedly faces near-daily harassment and fears leaving the house because settlers might seize it. Israel to gradually resume commercial goods entry into Gaza: Israeli authorities they would gradually resume coordination of private-sector goods entering Gaza after several days of suspension over claims that merchants had halted shipments because Hamas demanded payments of approximately 10,000 shekels ($3,000) per truck and required them to sell goods in cash. The claims were denied by the head of Gaza's private truckers union at the time, who told AP: "The merchants are not the ones who stopped the shipments. The Israeli coordinator is claiming that Gaza's merchants are responsible, but the truth is that the Israelis are the ones who imposed the restrictions." Israeli military agency COGAT on Monday claimed merchants had reported that Hamas withdrew the demands and said it was now requiring merchants to conduct all transactions through bank transfers. It warned that any merchant found to have "made payments to Hamas" would lose authorization to bring goods into Gaza. Amnesty condemns "state-driven" Israeli settler violence, calls for sanctions: Amnesty International escalating Israeli settler attacks across the occupied West Bank on Tuesday, accusing Israel of using violence to forcibly displace Palestinians and calling on governments to impose sanctions, halt settlement trade, and end cooperation sustaining the occupation. "Settler attacks are not isolated acts, but a central policy of the Israeli state," Heba Morayef, Amnesty's regional director for the Middle East and North Africa, said, accusing the international community of enabling abuses through inaction. Amnesty urged governments to impose an arms embargo on Israel, sanction officials implicated in serious violations, and support International Criminal Court investigations. New polls show Israeli opposition poised for win: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu got no immediate bump from Trump's recent endorsement, new surveys show. released Monday found Netanyahu 13 seats short of a majority. A at the same time found the pro-Netanyahu bloc with 51 seats, ten short of the 61 needed to form a majority. Polls have historically been fairly accurate this late in the race. Palestinian parties are expected to get roughly 15 seats, making them a difference-maker in the forming of a coalition for the opposition. Yemen UK announces additional military support for Saudi Arabia: The UK additional military support to Saudi Arabia following a request from Riyadh, including RAF Typhoon fighter jets, the British Defense Ministry announced Tuesday. The ministry said Britain would take a "defensive role and will not conduct offensive strikes," against Ansarallah. However, the support will include an RAF Voyager refueling aircraft to assist Saudi air operations, including operations aimed at degrading Ansarallah military targets in Yemen deemed a threat. The deployment builds on existing British military assistance, including air defense equipment and personnel stationed in Saudi Arabia to help counter missile and drone attacks. The ministry defended the expanded military role as necessary to protect regional stability, energy supplies, and trade, warning that escalating violence could drive up prices and costs for British businesses. UN: More than 250,000 displaced in Yemen since August, with Taiz hardest hit: More than 250,000 people have been across Yemen between August 1 and October 17 amid escalating hostilities, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) said Tuesday. Taiz accounted for 76% of departures and hosted 52% of those newly displaced, followed by Lahj, which hosted 23%, and Aden with 13%. Death toll from Ansarallah strike in Shabwa rises to 73: The death toll from an Ansarallah ballistic missile attack on the Al-Alam military training camp in Yemen's southern Shabwa governorate has risen to 73, local officials said Tuesday. More than 200 recruits were wounded, many critically. Yemen's Saudi-backed forces claimed their airstrikes in Taiz governorate killed 129 Ansarallah fighters and wounded 176 others over the past 48 hours. The figures could not be independently verified. Saudi-led coalition claims interception of weapons shipment off Yemen and missile over Riyadh: The Saudi-led military coalition Tuesday it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by Yemen's Ansarallah toward Riyadh. The coalition also said it had intercepted and destroyed a shipment of smuggled weapons off Yemen's coast. Coalition spokesperson said its forces had also destroyed 127 Ansarallah weapons depots and missile launch platforms, releasing footage purportedly showing strikes on boats and maritime shipments allegedly used to transport weapons. Saudi Arabia postpones "Davos in the Desert" summit: Saudi Arabia its flagship Future Investment Initiative (FII) conference, known as "Davos in the Desert," until 2027 amid escalating Ansarallah attacks on the kingdom. The annual gathering, scheduled for October 26-29 in Riyadh, was expected to bring together leading global financial executives, including JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon, Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser, Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon, and BlackRock CEO Larry Fink. The FII Institute announced the postponement Tuesday, saying a new date would be announced soon. This follows the cancellation or postponement of several international events in Saudi Arabia, including the EU-GCC summit, Riyadh Fashion Week, and the Saudi International golf tournament. Lebanon Israel blocks UN peacekeeper convoy in southern Lebanon: Israeli tanks blocked a UN peacekeeping logistics convoy near Al-Bayyadah in southern Lebanon on October 16, preventing supplies from reaching UN Interim Force in Lebanon positions, UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said Monday. "Roadblocks and obstacles on several routes have forced the cancellation of planned patrol and logistics convoys," he said, amid continued Israeli violations in the area. U.S. News Early votes signal major Democratic wave:, polls showing a Democratic blowout have merit. Voting patterns in Democratic areas suggest voters there are outpacing 2022 and 2018 midterm levels, though a shift in Democratic voter habits appears to be confounding the data. The Trump administration has aggressively sought to stifle mail-in voting, relying on its control of the U.S. Postal Service to make moves aimed at choking turnout, including new regulations largely blocked by the Supreme Court. That effort has eroded Democratic trust in using the USPS to turn in ballots, resulting in a surge of Democrats hand-delivering ballots to in-person locations, where they can have more certainty the vote will be counted. Much remains up in the air, but Republican seats across the country that went for Trump by 15-20 points in 2024 are consistently in play. Mexican man who died in Texas ICE facility was a lawful permanent resident: Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias , 56, was a green-card holder, ICE on Monday. On Saturday, Covarrubias was found unconscious in his bed at the ICE Rio Grande Processing Center, and declared dead about 20 minutes later. His cause of death is unknown; an autopsy is being conducted by the Webb County Medical Examiner. Officers detained him at a Laredo port of entry in June, accusing him of fraudulently obtaining legal status by failing to disclose a 2004 arrest for theft. He was scheduled to stand before an immigration judge in November. His daughter, Estefani Andrade , said he disclosed his criminal record when he applied for a green card. Vance stays neutral on Netanyahu following Trump endorsement : Vice President JD Vance Monday that he would not endorse Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. "I endorse American candidates, and that's where I'm focused on in the midterms. So I'm not getting involved in Israeli elections," he said. President Donald Trump** Netanyahu on Sunday, calling him "Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself." U.S. stalls transfer of Patriot interceptor to Ukraine; envoys head to Oslo Tuesday for negotiations: The Trump administration has not transfers of Patriot interceptors to Ukraine, Ukrainian officials said Monday. A U.S. official and three others told the Washington Post that Secretary of War Pete Hegseth neither rejected the transfers nor approved them. A Ukrainian official told the Post last week that "only a couple" of interceptors remain in Ukraine's stockpile. Trump envoy Steve Witkoff will Oslo on Tuesday for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and European leaders, with Jared Kushner expected to participate virtually, Axios reported. Witkoff is also planning to travel to Russia after the talks to present proposals developed with Ukraine and European allies. U.S. grants Ukrainians and Sudanese protection from deportation "for now": About 100,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese will keep their Temporary Protected Status, which was set to expire Monday, the Department of Homeland Security on Sunday. An announcement on the future of TPS will be "made at the appropriate time," according to the DHS. Last month, the Trump administration announced that it would grant Salvadoran immigrants to keep their TPS protections for the time being. DOJ charges 28 green-card holders in California with voting crimes; authorities quickly begin arrests: Twenty-eight green-card holders in California were charged with violating federal voting laws on Monday, the New York Times . Eleven have been arrested. The 28 people charged were among the 20,000 names of "likely noncitizens" the Trump administration flagged to California officials last week. The DOJ warned state officials not to count those ballots, or risk investigation for aiding voter fraud. Trump said authorities would "jail" officials who did not comply. Over the last two months, the DOJ has charged 113 people in 20 states with voting violations. Federal judge lets North Carolina 's strict mail-in ballot rules stand for midterms: North Carolina's rigid mail-in ballot rules must remain in place, U.S. District Judge Thomas Schroeder ruled. The voting regulations were passed by the Republican-led State Board of Elections just hours before ballots were sent to voters last month. Schroeder, a George W. Bush appointee, said it was too late to overturn the rules. The rules require that voters sign their name and seal their ballot in a county-provided envelope. They also direct counties to "spoil" ballots if the inner envelope isn't perfectly sealed, or if the signature does not clearly match the name on the return envelope, such as if a voter uses a nickname, a maiden name, or their initials. Supreme Court declines to hear case of fired NLRB member: The Supreme Court to consider reinstating Gwynne Wilcox , a Democratic member of the National Labor Relations Board. The move maintains an appeals court ruling that Congress violated the Constitution by trying to limit the president's power to remove NLRB members. In a recent Supreme Court case, the court approved the presidential power to fire leaders of any executive-branch agency for any reason. Watchdog groups file Hatch Act complaint over Alaska rally: Democracy Defenders Fund and Reporters Without Borders the Office of Special Counsel to investigate remarks by Federal Communications Commission Chair Brendan Carr , Interior Secretary Doug Burgum , and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick at Sen. Dan Sullivan 's rally earlier this month, alleging violations of the Hatch Act's ban on executive-branch political activity while on duty. Although the complaint acknowledges that Carr said he was speaking personally, it says he focused his remarks on the FCC's past and pending work. Neither Burgum nor Lutnick said they spoke in a personal capacity. The complaint also says Trump introduced both of them by their official titles, and that they failed to "correct the impression that each was speaking officially." The FCC has an upcoming vote on an Alaskan broadband deal, which Carr discussed the day after the rally on X, writing, "I look forward to working with @SenDanSullivan to get the job done." White House counsel probes pay-for-access allegations : White House Counsel Will Scharf is reportedly possible corruption stemming from a text message that Ric Grenell , then the head of the Kennedy Center and the Venezuela envoy, sent to the Turkish businessman Turhan Mildon , the husband of a Trump ally, Axios reported on Monday. In May 2025, Grennel texted Mildon: "Once the money comes to the company here, I will arrange the donation to Kennedy Centre [sic], and you'll be joining the VIP events and get close with the administration, even with POTUS." Grenell denies sending the text and says he never received a payment from Mildon. Mildon's attorneys gave the White House the text, an email, and a 2025 record of a $17.6 million wire to the Houston defense firm Texas Armament & Technology. Mildon says the money was split between a software deal in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Kennedy Center, which allegedly never received its $6 million share. Mildon's wife, the Trump ally Alina Habba, has accused Grenell of misdirecting the money. Mississippi attorney general says police shooting of 1-year-old "was justified": Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch 's office Monday that it completed its review of a June 14 police shooting and found it justified. Kohen Wiley , a 1-year-old child, was killed while sitting on the lap of his mother Vellesiya Wiley in a Walmart parking lot after officers responded to a call that she andLatoya Ferrell had stolen a pack of diapers. As the women drove off, officers drew weapons, Wiley lifted her son to show a child was in the car, and an officer fired into the vehicle, killing the baby and wounding Ferrell. Officers claimed, without evidence, that the women drove toward the police before they shot into it. Video footage recorded by a bystander does not corroborate the police claim. Neither Wiley nor Ferrell has been charged with a crime, and officials have not released any evidence that they engaged in shoplifting. The officer who shot the one-year-old Wiley, Hunter Foster, is white, and Wiley and both women are Black. The local news outlet Mississippi Today reported in July that Foster faced internal complaints over a racist remark days before the shooting, and that he had faced two allegations of misconduct. Mahmoud Khalil asks Supreme Court to halt his deportation : Mahmoud Khalil , the Columbia University graduate student and legal permanent resident detained by ICE in March 2025, an appeal Monday after the Third Circuit cleared the way for arrest and potential deportation. The Trump administration detained him under a rarely used statute that allows the Secretary of State to deport individuals whose presence "undercuts the national interest." A district judge found the law likely unconstitutional and ordered his release, but a closely divided appeals court said the petition belonged first in immigration court, which is run by the executive branch. The justices will decide whether to accept the case, which could take months. If they do, arguments would likely come in the spring with a ruling by early July. Mike Rogers received nearly $725,000 from IronNet before the controversial cybersecurity firm went bankrupt, filings indicate: The cybersecurity firm IronNet, founded by former NSA Director Keith Alexander , Michigan's GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers $724,887 prior to declaring bankruptcy, The American Prospect reported on Monday. His December 2023 disclosure also shows a $250,000 to $500,000 secured promissory note from the company, and $100,000 to $1,000,000 in capital gains from IronNet stock. Rogers joined the board right after leaving the House in January 2015 and sat on its Audit Committee until July 2023. From the 2021 reverse merger to his departure, the stock fell 99%, from $14 to $0.14. An investor group alleged inflated revenue, and the bankrupt firm settled for $6.6 million in 2024. Rogers failed to disclose the promissory note in his July 2026 financial statement. If he sold stock before leaving the board, mandatory SEC disclosures would apply, and none were filed. ProPublica: Trump 's FBI purge ended a bribery probe touching Lindsey Graham, James Clyburn, and Joe Wilson: In early 2025, the FBI opened a corruption investigation built on confessions from Martin Kao , CEO of the defense contractor Navatek, who told agents that his business model was bribing officials for government contracts, according to a new from ProPublica. He said he struck cash-for-contracts deals with Sen.Lindsey Graham , Rep. James Clyburn and Rep. Joe Wilson of South Carolina, and with Sen. Susan Collins of Maine. Agents found that much of Kao's account matched company records seized in the investigation. After Trump returned to the White House, the DOJ's anti-corruption section lost authority to file new cases, the career prosecutor quit, and agents assigned to the case were fired or pushed out. The case is now dead. The living lawmakers involved (Clyburn, Wilson, and Collins) have denied any wrongdoing. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Sudan drone attacks kill 160+, including 80 in single strike: Drone strikes since Friday have killed more than 160 people in western Sudan, Al Jazeera . Among the deadliest attacks was a strike near a market in RSF-controlled al-Dabba, West Kordofan, where a drone hit a transport hub and instantaneously killed 80 people. Forty-seven others were wounded in the attack; 30 of them later died of their injuries. The rights group Emergency Lawyers accused the Sudanese army of the attack, as did the RSF. On Monday, a drone strike on the RSF stronghold of Nyala killed 17 people, including seven RSF officers, and wounded 23 others. Meanwhile, a drone strike on Friday blamed on the RSF hit a gathering of displaced people in Sudan's Blue Nile state on the border with Ethiopia, killing 41 people, Emergency Lawyers said. On Monday, a drone struck a house near central Khartoum, three children between the ages of two and six. The children's mother was critically injured. Attack in Nigeria kills at least 15, including 10 soldiers: A convoy of Nigerian troops on patrol in the Nigerian state of Borno a landmine, likely planted by Boko Haram, and were ambushed Saturday, according to Reuters, which could not independently verify the casualties. A pickup truck detonated the mine, killing eight soldiers instantly. Gunmen then opened fire on a second vehicle, killing two more soldiers and five members of the Civilian Joint Task Force. Kenyan court convicts cult leader and others of murder of 190 children: The cult leader Paul Mackenzie and 28 others murdered 190 children and one adult, a Kenyan court on Monday. Prosecutors said his Good News International Church ran a doomsday sect that ordered followers to starve themselves and their children to reach heaven. More than 400 bodies have been recovered from the incident. Only 26 children's bodies have been identified. Mackenzie, who was arrested in 2023, also faces terrorism-related charges over the deaths. In a separate case, prosecutors allege that while he was in detention, he directed the deaths of 52 people. He has pleaded not guilty. Three killed, four injured in India clashes: Armed militants fire on villagers in the Indian state of Manipur on Monday, killing three people and injuring four, Reuters reported. The perpetrators were unidentified. The victims belonged to the mostly Hindu Meitei community, which has sporadically fought the predominantly Christian Kuki community since May 2023 over economic benefits and job quotas. Meitei groups blame Kuki "militants" for Monday's violence, which Kuki groups deny. The attack prompted protests in the state capital of Imphal; locals placed the bodies of two victims outside the chief minister's residence. Indian court extends detention of Cockroach Janta Party leaders, jailed for protesting : An Indian court prolonged the jailing of two leaders of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, Indian media reported. Police had requested more time to question them, and their detention was then extended two days. Ranka and Das were among 14 protesters who climbed barricades last week to enter a Delhi observatory the day after officials removed it from a list of approved protest sites. For more on the Indian protests, read Drop Site 's Biplob Kumar Das and Fatima Khan . Serbian opposition leaders surveilled by Israeli spyware on eve of election: Just days before Serbia's October 25 parliamentary election, two leaders of the country's political opposition, Vladan Djokic and Rade Bajic, were targeted by the Israeli firm NSO Group's Pegasus spyware, watchdog group Citizen Lab Monday. Both men have conflicted with Serbia's ruling party, which has faced two years of student-led anti-corruption protests. Djokic, rector of the University of Belgrade, has stood with students during youth-led anti-corruption protests against Serbia's ruling party. Bajic, a former lawyer, said he believed he was hacked because of his role in prosecuting senior officials who allegedly assisted Jared Kushner's firm in its property development plans. Russian drone strike kills six, including three children: A Russian drone attack six people, including three children, in a village near Kharkiv on Monday, Reuters reported. Fifteen people were injured. The drone strike hit a park where families were playing with their children, according to the interior minister of Ukraine, Ivan Vyhivskyi. Belarus bans entry of Latvian goods: Belarus a range of Latvian products, including canned fish and various industrial goods, on Monday, citing Latvia's "unconstructive approach and unfriendly rhetoric." Migrants trying to enter the European Union have found a new passage in Belarus in recent years. Latvia closed its border with Belarus in July. Finland to buy one million anti-personnel mines : Finland to spend 100 million euros ($112 million) on one million anti-personnel mines, AFP reported. Finland joined the anti-landmine Ottawa Convention in 2012, and withdrew from it in 2025. France imposes partial curfews in several cities, bans nighttime protests: French authorities announced overnight curfews on the Place de la Republique and the Les Halles areas of Paris on Monday, and banned other gatherings and demonstrations anywhere in the city after 8 p.m. Other cities imposed similar curfews, some of which only applied to minors. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu Monday he asked prefects to impose "partial" and "localized" curfews to protect businesses after weekend demonstrations turned into some of the worst street violence in recent years. He said "it is out of the question to put all of Paris under curfew," that a state of emergency could be declared if needed, and that he is "fully resolved to restoring public order." Haitian gangs ambush international security force; Salvadoran troops missing: Heavily armed gangs a UN-backed Gang Suppression Force vehicle with explosives near Port-au-Prince, officials told the UN Security Council on Monday. The four El Salvador air force members aboard the vehicle fled and are currently missing, Reuters reported. A spokesperson for the Gang Suppression Force said it was searching for the missing troops. Cuba says U.S. lets terrorists operate freely on U.S. soil : Cuban law enforcement officials accused the U.S. of granting terrorists freedom of movement in U.S. territory, citing a Cuban investigation into a February speedboat infiltration the Florida Keys, which led to a gun battle at sea. The February operation, according to Cuban law enforcement, was conducted by 10 Cuban exiles carrying about 13,000 rounds of ammunition, 11 rifles, 15 handguns, Molotov cocktails, and Starlink equipment. Five were killed; the survivors were detained and now face terrorism charges. Some individuals who trained the group remain at large in the U.S. For more on this story, see Reed Lindsay 's from Cuba. China accuses U.S. of "illegally" approaching disputed shoal: China accused the USS Charleston of "illegally" entering waters adjacent to Sabina Shoal in the Spratly Islands on Tuesday and sent naval forces to track and monitor the ship, Reuters . A Philippine military spokesperson said the U.S. ship "did not trespass into 'Chinese territory'" and that no nation can require prior permission for lawful transit of international waters. Taiwan accuses China of entering its territorial waters: Taiwan said a Chinese Coast Guard ship entered restricted waters near the Pratas Islands and was confronted by Taiwan's Coast Guard. During the encounter, the Chinese and Taiwanese vessels exchanged messages over broadcast. But a strong debate only matters if we turn it into votes. Kelly Ayotte will spend the next two weeks trying to drown out this message, and we need the resources to make sure every voter hears it.

## **Candidate Spotlight: Congressman Andy Biggs & Why Arizona is Closer Than You Think**
If you listen to corporate pollsters and mainstream media outlets, they'll try to convince you that key races in Arizona are out of reach or beyond the margin of error. But if you look under the hood at voter sentiment, turnout trends, and grassroots energy on the ground, the numbers tell a completely different story.
The mainstream narrative simply doesn't hold up.
On last night's episode of _The Sean Spicer Show_ , Congressman Andy Biggs -- the Republican nominee for governor - joined us to pull back the curtain on what's really happening in Arizona. Andy broke down why public polling models are systematically misjudging independent voters, undercounting conservative enthusiasm, and missing the ground game movement happening across the state.

Hey folks,
Pete Hegseth apparently thinks he could be President of the United States.
Yes. Seriously.
New reporting says people in Hegseth's orbit are encouraging him to consider a 2028 run. Meanwhile, he's dealing with the fallout from his attempt to livestream a military execution, defending the disastrous war in Iran, and giving Trump more reasons to eventually make him the scapegoat for everything going wrong.
* [**00:01:05**] We dig into the wild new reporting that Pete Hegseth is considering a political future, including a possible run for president in 2028.
* [**00:04:08**] J.D. Vance gets asked about his own presidential ambitions, and I explain why a MAGA primary without Trump could become an absolute bloodbath.
* [**00:07:55**] Hegseth's push to livestream a military execution reportedly overlaps with his political ambitions, and completely misreads what the American public actually wants.
* [**00:10:46**] Why I think Trump could eventually turn on Hegseth and make him the scapegoat for the war, the political fallout, and a disastrous midterm election.
* [**00:14:38**] We get to the part that isn't funny: reporting that the Pentagon plans to delay an internal report about a deadly school strike in Iran until after the midterms.

A Pete Hegseth presidential campaign sounds absurd. But the bigger story is what his ambition tells us about the people Trump has elevated, and how quickly they're already positioning themselves for whatever comes next. We have an election in two weeks. Democrats need to win, start demanding accountability, and make sure this movement doesn't simply reinvent itself with a new face in 2028. **If you value independent media that keeps exposing the corruption, incompetence, and chaos, help me keep doing it.**

Here’s what I want you to know: **nothing coming out of Washington has changed how you can vote in California. ** We secured a U.S. Supreme Court order protecting your ability to vote by mail, so you can vote exactly as you have in past elections: by mail, ballot drop box, early, or in person on Election Day. _Your vote is safe. And we’re going to keep it that way._ → We’ve been in close contact with law enforcement, the Governor, the Secretary of State, and local registrars across the state. Protecting your right to vote is a team effort in California, and we are prepared for any possibility. → We’ve also taken new steps to strengthen those protections. California just passed new laws that make it a crime to unlawfully seize ballots, and that if a seizure is attempted, my office must be notified immediately so we can act to stop it. **To put it simply: If you can imagine it, we’re ready for it. ** When it comes to protecting your fundamental right to vote — from the President, a law-breaking sheriff, or anyone else who tries to interfere — I’ll never stop fighting for your rights and our shared democracy. **[I’m up for re-election this November, and I could use your support in these final two weeks. name: Chad Bianco
subject: The fight for California continues
body:
Our fight is far from over. And I need you by my side.

| | | | | |
---
| |

Friends,
**The fight for California continues.**
Every day, I think about the state of distress California is in. Our once-beautiful state, once known for low crime, families moving in, and patriotism, has taken a wrong turn.

I have come to tell you that California's future is not inevitable. **California will be what you make of it** —what we make of it, together—and it can once again have very beautiful times.
**I speak to all of California** , not just Riverside, because every day I am fighting the corrupt Sacramento elite and standing up for your rights, which are being taken away. I have seen it firsthand.
---
| | | | | [Join Team Bianco](https://us.list-manage.com/Uk46q282abS?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
---
| |
**Click above — important message**

**Sacramento doesn’t want you to own a legal firearm.** They don’t want fair elections or lawful investigations into where there may be fraud. They give sanctuary to criminals, including criminal migrants and refuse to fund Prop 36, which voters in every California county supported. And the list goes on
**My re-election campaign for sheriff won’t be an easy battle.** The Democrats will do everything in their power to ensure we lose. That is why I humbly ask for your support. Now more than ever, in these difficult times, California needs a strong voice for law and order—one that stands up for the people when Sacramento refuses to listen.
I am asking each and every one of you to **contribute just $5** today to my re-election campaign as Riverside County Sheriff. If you could **make it a recurring contribution** , it would make all the difference in this fight.
**I will never give up on this state.** I ask you to join me.
Sheriff Chad Bianco
Riverside County

body:
My opponent sat down with the Seattle Times. Here's what he said about me.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/e9CQPo8pqQS?e=a7b299e420&c2id=1b040b68f1d062d0c966c24dae99fcb4)
| | | | | | | | | | | |
The Seattle Times ran a long story on our race: **"Amid potential blue wave, Spokane Republican vies to stay in Congress."**
My opponent sat down for an hour-long interview and somehow all he talked about was the temporary reduction in taxes on overtime and tips.
He didn’t say a word about:
* Voting for the drastic cuts to Medicaid
* Surrendering Congressional power over tariffs and war
* Letting former AG Pam Bondi off the hook for continuing to shield unindicted co-conspirators in the Epstein child trafficking ring

He did find time to criticize me, saying I “don’t have the experience” to do the job.
_He has plenty of experience — as a career politician._
**I have almost 30 years of real world, non-partisan public service: in the U.S. Foreign Service, with postings in Pakistan, Japan and New Zealand, and as a Spokane County deputy prosecuting attorney. I’ll bring the problem-solving skills of a negotiator and a prosecutor to Congress.**
This Seattle Times story also called out that by the end of September, he had more than $800K in the bank compared to our $154,000.
**We are on the national radar of both parties and we’re this close to flipping this seat but we have to keep up our momentum all the way across the finish line.**
[**Can I count on you to chip in just $5 or $10 so we can talk to voters in every corner of the district before Election Day? WA-05 is bigger than 9 US states - we have a lot of ground to cover and not much time left.**](https://us.list-manage.com/rQVAwtyf3Qs?e=a7b299e420&c2id=1b040b68f1d062d0c966c24dae99fcb4)

Friend,

When I was a kid in Louisville's West End, my mom skipped meals so I could eat. She never complained. She just did it, the way millions of parents still do.

In 2021, Michael Bennet helped change that for a lot of families. The expanded Child Tax Credit, which he had championed for years, put money in parents' pockets every month and cut child poverty in America nearly in half.

Then it expired. Democrats were one vote short in the Senate to extend it, and the next year, millions of children were pushed back into poverty.

I think about that a lot. _One vote._

I also think about this: My opponent, Congressman Andy Barr, voted against the bill that made those monthly payments possible. Every House Republican did.

My name is Charles Booker. I'm running for Mitch McConnell's open Senate seat in Kentucky, and our latest poll has this race tied, 43 to 43.

Republicans hold 53 seats. Democrats need to flip four to win the majority back, and the last few years have shown exactly what a _single seat_ is worth.

Kentucky can be one of the four.

Barr's campaign has the money: millions from the coal, crypto, and AI industries.

But we have something they can't buy: Kentuckians who are tired of being ignored and ready for a senator who has lived through the struggles they're living.

I've been homeless. I've rationed my insulin. I know what it's like to choose between groceries and prescriptions. That's why I'm running.

Yesterday I turned 53.
It's hard to believe that 20 years have passed since I ran for Congress. I remember those days vividly, knocking on doors trying to convince the people of Bucks County that a young guy who had just come home from war deserved a chance to represent them in Washington.
Birthdays have a funny way of putting things in perspective.
At 23, I was beginning my military career.
At 33, I was running for Congress.
At 43, I was preparing for another chapter of leadership in the U.S. Army.
And now, at 53, I'm thinking more about my own kids growing up and the next generation of Americans who will carry this country forward.
In 2006, I was an unlikely underdog who believed public service was one of the best ways to make this country better. I still do.
That's why, with the midterm elections just two weeks away, I'm back on the campaign trail, knocking on doors and supporting Democratic candidates I believe in. Only this time, I have my son Jack by my side.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/34e79d7d-64e1-461f-84fb-b77974bc419f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### **Why I Still Believe Good People Should Run**
One way I got involved early this election season was by hosting a meet-and-greet in Philadelphia for [Rebecca Bennett](https://substack.com/redirect/43abcec3-5257-488e-9412-f55a6e530cf9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a fellow veteran running for Congress in New Jersey's 7th District against incumbent Republican Tom Kean Jr. Out Taking the Hill federal PAC endorsed her, and we've written her a check.
Rebecca spent more than a decade as a Navy helicopter pilot, earned her MBA from Wharton, and went on to become a leader in healthcare. She's also a mother of two.
Having run for Congress myself, I know how much you're asking of yourself and your family when you put your name on the ballot. It's not an easy decision, especially these days.
I've long believed that the next chapter of veterans' service isn't just about what America can do for them, but what they can continue doing for America. Running for public office is one way to do that, and it's encouraging to see veterans taking that step.
* * *
Another highlight of the week was hitting the campaign trail for [Bryan Allen](https://substack.com/redirect/ae11e64e-6364-4c2e-abaa-95feb608885f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who's running for the PA State House in Bucks County, with my son Jack. Bryan is a graduate of Conwell Egan Catholic, where Jack is a Junior. Our Kennedy Democrats state PAC wrote him a $96K check.
I've knocked on thousands of doors over the years, but doing it alongside my son was something special. Politics has changed quite a bit since I ran in 2006, but there's still nothing quite like meeting voters face-to-face.
Now instead of asking people to believe in me, I'm thinking about the values I want to instill in my own children and what I want them to believe about our country.
I want Jack to understand that democracy isn't a spectator sport. It requires participation and a willingness to listen to people who see the world differently. Public service is a duty we all share, even if that simply means showing up to vote on Election Day.
Earlier this week, I spoke at the national PWW conference with leaders from across the country in the emergency medical services community. It was a good reminder that public service comes in many forms. Our EMS professionals who report for duty at 3 a.m. are our local heroes, and as I said to them, nobody calls 9-1-1 because they're having a good day. There are over one million of them: 623K EMS professionals (who conducted over 150 education hours) and 268K paramedics (who conducted over 1500 education hours). Last year, according to NEMSIS, they answered over 63 million activations.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a7b58b3d-f68e-4de7-8a45-64d4e46bc3e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2cb619de-eac8-411d-8bbd-1c69ef19cb7c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
With two weeks until Election Day, everyone will be focused on who will win and who will lose. But the day after matters too.
Because the need for service doesn't disappear when the ballots are counted. The emergencies keep coming. The challenges facing our communities remain. And the next generation is watching how we respond.
I've been fortunate to serve this country in a lot of different ways, from West Point to Baghdad, from Congress to the Pentagon. And twenty years after my first campaign, I still believe public service is one of the best things we can do with our lives.
I can't tell you what my son Jack will decide to do when he grows up. But I hope he'll remember knocking on those doors with me and understand why it was so important.
The next generation won't learn the meaning of service simply by hearing us talk about it. They'll learn it by watching our actions - especially when we show up to help others.

At 43, I was preparing for another chapter of leadership in the U.S. Army. And now, at 53, I'm thinking more about my own kids growing up and the next generation of Americans who will carry this country forward. In 2006, I was an unlikely underdog who believed public service was one of the best ways to make this country better. I still do. That's why, with the midterm elections just two weeks away, I'm back on the campaign trail, knocking on doors and supporting Democratic candidates I believe in. Only this time, I have my son Jack by my side. | | ---|---|--- Why I Still Believe Good People Should Run One way I got involved early this election season was by hosting a meet-and-greet in Philadelphia for , a fellow veteran running for Congress in New Jersey's 7th District against incumbent Republican Tom Kean Jr. Out Taking the Hill federal PAC endorsed her, and we've written her a check. Rebecca spent more than a decade as a Navy helicopter pilot, earned her MBA from Wharton, and went on to become a leader in healthcare. She's also a mother of two. Having run for Congress myself, I know how much you're asking of yourself and your family when you put your name on the ballot. It's not an easy decision, especially these days. I've long believed that the next chapter of veterans' service isn't just about what America can do for them, but what they can continue doing for America. Running for public office is one way to do that, and it's encouraging to see veterans taking that step. Another highlight of the week was hitting the campaign trail for , who's running for the PA State House in Bucks County, with my son Jack. Bryan is a graduate of Conwell Egan Catholic, where Jack is a Junior. Our Kennedy Democrats state PAC wrote him a $96K check. I've knocked on thousands of doors over the years, but doing it alongside my son was something special. Politics has changed quite a bit since I ran in 2006, but there's still nothing quite like meeting voters face-to-face. Now instead of asking people to believe in me, I'm thinking about the values I want to instill in my own children and what I want them to believe about our country. I want Jack to understand that democracy isn't a spectator sport. It requires participation and a willingness to listen to people who see the world differently. Public service is a duty we all share, even if that simply means showing up to vote on Election Day. Earlier this week, I spoke at the national PWW conference with leaders from across the country in the emergency medical services community. It was a good reminder that public service comes in many forms. Our EMS professionals who report for duty at 3 a.m. are our local heroes, and as I said to them, nobody calls 9-1-1 because they're having a good day. There are over one million of them: 623K EMS professionals (who conducted over 150 education hours) and 268K paramedics (who conducted over 1500 education hours). Last year, according to NEMSIS, they answered over 63 million activations. | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- With two weeks until Election Day, everyone will be focused on who will win and who will lose. But the day after matters too. Because the need for service doesn't disappear when the ballots are counted. The emergencies keep coming. The challenges facing our communities remain. And the next generation is watching how we respond. I've been fortunate to serve this country in a lot of different ways, from West Point to Baghdad, from Congress to the Pentagon. And twenty years after my first campaign, I still believe public service is one of the best things we can do with our lives. I can't tell you what my son Jack will decide to do when he grows up. But I hope he'll remember knocking on those doors with me and understand why it was so important. The next generation won't learn the meaning of service simply by hearing us talk about it. They'll learn it by watching our actions - especially when we show up to help others. The Secretary's SitRep is a reader-supported publication. I'm proud to call her a dear friend, and I fully believe in the work of her climate PAC — especially now, when the very fabric of our democracy and our planet is being tested every single day. You’ve seen it for yourself. Donald Trump is doing everything in his power to prop up corporate polluters who don’t give a damn about you, me, or the very people who voted for him. He’s cut taxes for his fossil fuel buddies, opened millions of acres of public lands to drilling, gutted protections for our air and water, and fired scientists who dare speak the truth. These aren’t abstract decisions — they hurt real people, real communities, and real families. But when I start to lose hope, I look to Jane and to the work her team is doing at JanePAC, and it reminds me that change is still possible. They aren't waiting around for Washington to do the right thing. They're building power from the ground up by electing climate champions at every level of government in races that rarely make headlines but change lives and shape the policy that protects us from Trump's attacks. Since 2022, Jane and her team have helped elect over 250 climate leaders nationwide. Now, with critical races in Texas, Pennsylvania, Georgia, and beyond coming down to the wire, we have a historic opportunity to help them elect dozens more this November. That's why I'm reaching out today. Hi Peter, it’s Carole King 🎶, and I personally wrote this email.
I first met Jon Ossoff in 2020 before he was elected to the U.S. Senate, when he was an investigative journalist. He brought that background to the Senate, where he exposed the abuse and sexual trafficking of children in foster care — and he brought to light the mistreatment of military families by private housing contractors.
That’s why I am asking now: [**Will you join me in supporting Jon’s reelection?**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261020-2-f&utm_campaign=em261020-2-f&t=3&akid=3133%2E5691347%2EKn-bn2)
The Republican Senate majority has refused to use their power to end the war or stop the grift and corruption at the highest levels of our government.
Senator Ossoff has used his voice against the greedy and powerful on behalf of hardworking Georgians, from Sky Valley to St. George, who can no longer afford basic needs.

****
Jon has been hearing from an unprecedented number of Georgians who are now having to rely on food banks.
A man in a company uniform: “I’m working my jobs, but we couldn’t eat without the food pantry.”
A mom holding a toddler: “I can’t afford gas, rent, groceries, insurance premiums...I don’t know how we can make it through this.”
A postal worker on a break: “People saying they can’t afford to eat out? I can’t afford to eat in!”
[**If you agree that this is unacceptable in Georgia and the United States of America, please donate whatever you can afford right now.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261020-2-f&utm_campaign=em261020-2-f&t=28&akid=3133%2E5691347%2EKn-bn2)
When we spoke, Jon said that the well-being of children and families is what matters most. He’s seeking reelection to work for them, not to enrich billionaires. And that’s why super-rich Republican donors have poured MILLIONS of dollars into a barrage of ads with dire predictions, dark music, and ominous voiceovers to turn voters against him.
Imagine how much GOOD could be done with a Democratic majority with a moral conscience.
Senator Ossoff has a moral conscience, and he can bring together a broad coalition to make things better for hardworking Georgians and Americans.
[**Let’s make sure Jon Ossoff can continue to stand up for hardworking Georgians and Americans in the U.S. Senate.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261020-2-f&utm_campaign=em261020-2-f&t=29&akid=3133%2E5691347%2EKn-bn2)
If you can’t spare a dollar, or even if you can donate more, here are two actions you can take for free:
1. [Vote.](https://act.electjon.com/go/71?t=30&akid=3133%2E5691347%2EKn-bn2)

2. [Volunteer.](https://act.electjon.com/go/5125?t=31&akid=3133%2E5691347%2EKn-bn2)

Peter, thank you so much for participating. Stay strong. We’ll get through this.
My best wishes to you and your family,
-Carole

Well they finally went and looked.

28 providers got hit with enforcement and 16 got kicked out of the program entirely, mostly because investigators kept showing up and found no kids, or nobody answered the door.

One Boise daycare was licensed for 12 kids and had up to 42 enrolled on your dime. Averaging more than $21,000 a month.

At least 7 of them were flagged back in 2024 and early 2025 but they stayed in the program anyway.

In April, Brad wrote that Idaho's child care fraud rate is "among the lowest in the nation." Yesterday he tweeted that "we must hold fraudsters accountable."

Before payments go out the door, huh.

---|---|---
Then there's illegal labor...

Contractors hire illegals and undercut Idaho guys who play by the rules.

The Idaho Home Builders Association fought the E-Verify bill and Rick Naerebout from the Idaho Dairymen's Association, said his members depend on unauthorized workers to run their farms (If we get rid of the slaves who will pick the cotton?).

Those workers get hired on fake papers and somebody else's Social Security number. That IS fraud, and it's the exact thing this pledge is supposedly about.

The House passed a bill making it a state crime to hire illegals and another requiring E-Verify.

Both died in the Idaho Senate on purpose.

14 immigration bills this session and zero made it to Brad's desk. He told reporters E-Verify is "not black and white."

All hat and no cattle as they say.
Cheers,
Brian

Two weeks until Sherrod's race decides Senate control.
Team – this is one of the most important elections of our lifetime.
We know people say that all the time – but this time, it’s true.
Folks in Ohio and across the country know the system is rigged. They see that our government doesn’t work for working people, just for the rich and powerful. They’re frustrated why so many politicians in Washington don’t seem to give a damn.
**They’re right on all accounts, and that’s why Sherrod is in this fight.**
Right now, we’re making incredible progress to flip Ohio, take back the Senate, and give working people their voice back in Washington – but we’re facing an uphill battle.
While experts across the board say this race is a true toss-up, GOP dark-money groups are pouring $317 million into Ohio to defeat us. **That money is taking a toll, with the latest poll showing Sherrod 2 points down.**
The only way we can fight back and surge ahead is with your grassroots support. And, this is our shot to prove organized people are stronger than organized money.

body:

| | | | |

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Peter,
It's official: we are TWO WEEKS away from Election Day.
Fourteen days. That's all that stands between us and the most important decision of this year.
_This is the moment where we find out who's really in this fight._
**Because here's the choice in front of us:** We can keep building a stronger, safer, more prosperous country. Or we can hand the keys to leftists who will do everything in their power to OBSTRUCT President Trump's agenda, push socialism, drive up your energy bills, and drag America down a path we can't afford to go down.
I know which side I'm on. **I'm ALL IN.**
So I have to ask you directly, Peter.
Are you with me?
Will you take the pledge to SAVE TRUMP'S MAJORITY?
[**> > YES, I'M IN. I'LL TAKE THE PLEDGE <<**](https://us.list-manage.com/10g2fhOGsqc?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
The Left is pouring everything they have into these final two weeks. They're activating all of their most radical voters and they're hoping patriots like you to sit this one out.
Let's prove them wrong.
[Join me now to protect our majority, protect our agenda, and protect the future of this country.](https://us.list-manage.com/bjMtix7MW3l?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)

Let's win this.Kailee Buller

**Ivette DECODES**
The Heart of What Matters
**Who is protecting the ballot --and how?**
The Justice Department has charged 28 California residents, all lawful permanent residents (LPRs), with election-related crimes. Green-card holders are not U.S. citizens and cannot vote in federal elections. Prosecutors allege that some falsely claimed citizenship when registering and that some cast ballots. The charges are allegations, not convictions.
The administration says these cases support its claims about more than 20,000 people it considers likely noncitizens on California's voter rolls. California's Secretary of State says her office did not receive the list directly or the information needed to verify it. Los Angeles County received a USB drive but had not accessed it because of security concerns. California objected to the 48-hour deadline to act without adequate means to verify the data.
**When questioning voter-roll entries, what evidence should be produced?**
**And when security concerns prevent officials from examining evidence, what alternatives should they pursue?**
Enforce the law. Prove the claim. Protect the right.
**Ivette DECODES**

body:
We want to launch our biggest wave of GOTV programs yet

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141817145/654840399/777330224?refcode=email-logo&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDcvMS8xMDU4MjciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmZlZWEwMzAtYThjYy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=cNoqUv9FLiHaFFheatq7uD-lbBXRFDKV0JynZcnrXUg=) I know my team and I talk a lot about why this election matters — and honestly, we give a good deal of attention to the bad stuff: Rampant corruption in Washington. The freedom to vote under attack by an unaccountable Supreme Court. Our most basic Constitutional rights, chipped away one-by-one by a wannabe tyrant in the White House. And yes, we absolutely need to fight back against the President and his agenda. But I didn't get into public service just to oppose bad ideas. I got into it because I believe the government can actually make people's lives better. As a dad and a former teacher, I'm much more interested in what we can get done than in how many times we can argue about who's to blame. **But I’ve gotta tell you: We’d get a heck of a lot more done with a Democratic majority in charge.** **[I’ll be honest: We’ve spent the last two years fighting against the bad stuff. One in nine. That is the share of Americans who support building an AI data center in their community, according to a September University of Massachusetts poll. The other eight in nine are opposed -- and the opposition runs straight through the Republican base, which rejects a data center in its own backyard by nearly three to one, 52 percent to 18.
The GOP's leadership has taken the other side. Donald Trump's administration fast-tracked federal permitting for data centers over 100 megawatts by executive order in July 2025, and in December it ordered the Justice Department to sue states that regulate AI while drafting legislation to pre-empt state AI law. Washington is not on the county commission's side of this fight.
Meanwhile, Democrats are running the campaign Trump's own base is begging for. Florida is proving it.
**" Data Center Donalds"**
David Jolly -- the former Republican congressman now carrying the Democratic banner for Florida governor -- has made a data-center pause the spine of his campaign: "I'm calling for a stop to AI data centers until Florida has a responsible plan" to pay for the power and water first. He has rechristened his Trump-endorsed opponent, Byron Donalds, "Data Center Donalds."...

This year, the Swing Left community is supporting governor races in three categories: **Must-Flip, Must-Hold, and Reach**. clean_body: This is what we built together. | | Peter, Early voting opened yesterday, and what a day it was. Lines wrapped around the block at our local precinct. Supporters kept sending photos with their "I Voted" stickers, and every one of them put a bigger smile on my face. | Forgive me for getting sentimental, but this is everything we spent the past year building. All those doors in the summer heat, the town halls, the yard signs, the volunteer hours at food pantries, because service before self was never just a slogan. Every bit of it was for this, neighbors at the polls standing up for democracy. After 20 years in uniform defending this country, days like yesterday show me what all that service was for. Ordinary people lining up on an ordinary Monday to govern themselves. That line around the block is America keeping its oldest promise. We have two weeks left to bring it home, and this team will not slow down one inch before the finish. # [Treasury flags $270M in ghost student aid fraud schemes](https://substack.com/redirect/ffcd324d-871b-411f-922f-3832d8ded541?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Treasury's FinCEN identified **[roughly $270 million in suspicious transactions linked to federal student aid fraud,](https://substack.com/redirect/9fad663d-9f3f-49c7-8ee3-15756f902b05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/9fad663d-9f3f-49c7-8ee3-15756f902b05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)including ghost-student schemes using stolen identities, and referred the activity to investigators.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ffcd324d-871b-411f-922f-3832d8ded541?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **FinCEN alert volume:** Financial institutions filed nearly 100 suspicious activity reports after a July alert, covering more than 20,000 potentially suspicious transactions dating to February 2026.
* **Ghost student tactics:** Criminals use stolen personal data or synthetic identities created with AI tools to enroll fake students and divert aid refunds; victims, including minors, often learn of the debt later.
* **Straw student rings:** Fraud groups pay real people for personal information, enroll them, and keep the resulting refunds, sometimes with help from corrupt school employees who alter records.
* **Administration response:** Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the programs exist to expand opportunity, not enrich fraudsters, while Education Secretary Linda McMahon noted a new FAFSA tool has already saved more than $2 billion.

# [$32M United CEO demands near-100% inheritance tax](https://substack.com/redirect/ffcd324d-871b-411f-922f-3832d8ded541?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby, **[whose 2025 compensation totaled about $32.3 million,](https://substack.com/redirect/eafe36ca-3943-451d-ad38-39e48a9aa35c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** told The New York Times that wealth inequality threatens society and backed a national wealth tax plus near-100% inheritance taxes on some estates.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ffcd324d-871b-411f-922f-3832d8ded541?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Kirby 's exact stance:** He said a national wealth tax is needed because a state-level version would simply prompt the rich to move, and he personally would pay inheritance taxes approaching 100% at some unspecified level.
* **Interview context:** The remarks came in a Sunday Times interview about declining public trust in corporate executives amid broader debates over taxing high-net-worth Americans.
* **Current estate rules:** Federal estate tax currently tops out at 40% on taxable estates above a $15 million individual exemption in 2026, according to the IRS.
* **No rate specified:** Kirby did not name a preferred wealth-tax rate or the exact estate size that would trigger the near-100% inheritance levy he supports.

# [GM beats Q3, adds $20B buyback, but stock plunges 6%](https://substack.com/redirect/ffcd324d-871b-411f-922f-3832d8ded541?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
General Motors reported **[$50 billion in Q3 revenue](https://substack.com/redirect/df655a5f-4952-4440-9261-4fb6d6e1f41f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and $3.70 adjusted EPS, beating estimates, raised its auto free-cash-flow outlook to $11.5-12.5 billion, and authorized **[a new $20 billion buyback,](https://substack.com/redirect/1f240d3c-46bd-47f0-9e6a-93445f745ac2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** yet shares dropped about 6% early Tuesday.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b43a2423-bb16-45e5-81f2-9748ddd83d04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Earnings and cash:** Adjusted EBIT reached $4.1 billion, up nearly 22%, while automotive free cash flow jumped 40% to $5.9 billion; full-year adjusted EBIT guidance tightened to $14.5-15.5 billion.
* **Buyback scale:** The new multiyear authorization has no expiration date and follows nearly $30 billion in repurchases over the past five years; **[Barron's noted](https://substack.com/redirect/2d94a3b8-fe99-4829-9ffb-c1f4393e44ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/2d94a3b8-fe99-4829-9ffb-c1f4393e44ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)it could allow buying back more than 25% of the company.
* **Market reaction:** Shares fell more than 6% in premarket trading despite the beat, with investors focused on a weakening U.S. auto market, higher financing costs, and pressure on lower-priced models.
* **Volume and China:** U.S. sales fell 5.5% to 670,974 vehicles, EV volume dropped about 62%, and profit from China fell 60% year-over-year to $32 million.

# [U.S. bans DeepSeek from all civilian federal systems](https://substack.com/redirect/ffcd324d-871b-411f-922f-3832d8ded541?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Department of Homeland Security ordered federal civilian agencies[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/42ff54c9-de88-4180-a005-a6dd091a88f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[to remove DeepSeek technology, including third-party products built on it,](https://substack.com/redirect/42ff54c9-de88-4180-a005-a6dd091a88f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and to stop purchasing it, citing data-transfer and security risks.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ffcd324d-871b-411f-922f-3832d8ded541?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Order details:** Issued July 24 and made public October 20, the directive covers all federal civilian agencies but excludes the Defense Department; agencies may request exceptions with written justification within 60 days.
* **Security concerns:** DHS cited potential transfer of sensitive U.S. government data to China and vulnerabilities, including critical issues previously identified in DeepSeek's iOS app.
* **Prior restrictions:** Congress limited DeepSeek in intelligence systems in December 2025, Commerce bureaus banned it on government devices in March 2025, and the Defense Information Systems Agency blocked access in January 2025.
* **China response:** Beijing's foreign ministry said it would protect its companies' interests and opposed over-generalizing national security or politicizing technology and trade.

# [French bond yields near 24-year high as protests loom](https://substack.com/redirect/ffcd324d-871b-411f-922f-3832d8ded541?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
French 10-year OAT yields rose 3 basis points to 4.96% and the spread over German Bunds **[widened to 152.5 basis points after weekend riots,](https://substack.com/redirect/1e6a72e2-5f03-401b-a5f2-31c31b4aa087?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with fresh demonstrations planned for Saturday.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ffcd324d-871b-411f-922f-3832d8ded541?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Yield levels:** The 10-year OAT reached as high as 4.9937% earlier in October, its highest since July 2002, while the OAT-Bund spread touched 158.67 basis points, the widest since November 2011.
* **Protest impact:** Weekend riots added to investor caution about the government's ability to reduce the deficit, and new demonstrations are scheduled for this Saturday.
* **Broader spreads:** Italian spreads also widened, rising 4.5 basis points to 113.51 basis points on the same day.
* **Market caution:** Investors remain focused on fiscal challenges as yields sit near multi-decade highs.

Straw student rings: Fraud groups pay real people for personal information, enroll them, and keep the resulting refunds, sometimes with help from corrupt school employees who alter records. United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby, told The New York Times that wealth inequality threatens society and backed a national wealth tax plus near-100% inheritance taxes on some estates. | | ---|---|--- Kirby 's exact stance: He said a national wealth tax is needed because a state-level version would simply prompt the rich to move, and he personally would pay inheritance taxes approaching 100% at some unspecified level. Interview context: The remarks came in a Sunday Times interview about declining public trust in corporate executives amid broader debates over taxing high-net-worth Americans. Current estate rules: Federal estate tax currently tops out at 40% on taxable estates above a $15 million individual exemption in 2026, according to the IRS. No rate specified: Kirby did not name a preferred wealth-tax rate or the exact estate size that would trigger the near-100% inheritance levy he supports. Buyback scale: The new multiyear authorization has no expiration date and follows nearly $30 billion in repurchases over the past five years; could allow buying back more than 25% of the company. Market reaction: Shares fell more than 6% in premarket trading despite the beat, with investors focused on a weakening U.S. auto market, higher financing costs, and pressure on lower-priced models. # Fun Fact of the Month
---
Those odd, bulbous growths on redwoods are called burls, and they’re hiding a clever survival trick. If the parent tree dies, burls can send up genetically identical sprouts, giving the redwood another shot at life. It’s basically botanical life insurance.Learn more about these strange and [wonderful growths](https://click.everyaction.com/k/141819515/654848531/1230570026?utm_campaign=redwoodmatters&utm_medium=email&utm_source=ea-redwoodmatters&utm_term=rm-10-2026&sourceid=1171043&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImE1ZmRmYTNiLWFkY2MtZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMjI0ODI5Zjg2OSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=URD87SwYw_vtv2mE73U96-Z6N8kQZ4lwFwDh0Xy7Kgs=&emci=29f23dd9-2bc7-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=a5fdfa3b-adcc-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=1504551).

body:

Derek, In just _**14 days**_ , voters across the country will make critical choices that shape our future. That means right now is our crucial window to knock doors, make calls, and connect directly with voters in key battleground communities. There will be plenty of races this November that will be decided by a handful of votes. You don’t want to wake up the day after the election and wish you had done more. The easiest way to have a really, really big impact is to volunteer with your local Democratic Party to remind Democrats in your community that it’s time to VOTE. So we’re asking you to RSVP and attend an upcoming organizing event near you. | VOLUNTEER SHIFTS NEAR YOU

body:
Sign-Waving, Candidate Debates and Forums!

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/cziHclukfv_?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
|
---
| |
# Two Weeks Until the Election!
---
|
---
| | Only two weeks until Election Day!
Eastern Washington is paying attention, and the choice is clear. We need leadership that puts our district first, protects our freedoms, and keeps fighting for the values that make this place home.
We’ve built real momentum. Now we close it out.
Ballots landed in mailboxes across Eastern Washington late last week. If yours is sitting on the kitchen counter, fill it out and return it today. Don’t wait! You can drop it in the mail or find your nearest drop box [**here.**](https://us.list-manage.com/WICFkP91kGS?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
Between now and November 3rd, every conversation, every yard sign, every ballot returned, and every volunteer hour matters. Races are won in these final days and turnout will be so important.
I’m grateful to be in this fight with you. Let’s make these last two weeks count!
---
|
---
| |
# Join Us for a Sign-Wave!
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| | Join us for sign-waving in these final two weeks at busy intersections and overpasses! We are waving every weekday morning and afternoon. **Thank for all of the supportive honks and thumbs-ups - we appreciate it!**
Sign-waving is one of the most effective ways to show support, help voter turn-out, and put our message in front of thousands of drivers across the district. Bring a friend or the whole family, a lawn-chair if preferred, grab a sign, and help us wave where traffic is heaviest. It’s a fun, high-impact way to boost visibility, meet fellow supporters, and keep the energy strong. All ages and experience levels are welcome. Come out when you can! Email [**here** ](mailto:stephanie@votebaumgartner.com?subject=Sign-Waves...Sign%20Me%20Up!&body=)for details.
---
|
---
| |
# NAACP Candidate Forum
---
|
---
| | Last week I joined the NAACP Candidate Forum at the Spokane Downtown Library. It was a great event and I really appreciated all the work that went into putting it together. I appreciated the civility and the thoughtful questions, and it was good to be able to share my priorities for strengthening our community, supporting working families and protecting our American values and freedoms. I especially appreciated the chance to connect with people one-on-one and talk about representation, opportunities, and the work still ahead. Thank you to the NAACP for hosting the dialogue.
---
|
---
|
---
| |
# Chewelah Candidate Forum
---
|
---
| | I also appreciated the chance to join the Candidate Forum in Chewelah in Stevens County on Thursday evening. It was a great opportunity to answer questions directly from neighbors, talk about the issues that matter most to rural communities in our district, and connect with people face-to-face. In those conversations I was pleased to highlight my co-sponsorship of the Secure Rural Schools reauthorization important for Stevens County, and my work on the federal funding for the major expansion of NEW Health rural healthcare services. Thank you to the Chewelah Chamber of Commerce and The Independent for hosting this event.
---
|
---
| |
# Lunch Debate at Rotary 21
---
|
---
| | I was glad to take part in the Rotary 21 lunch debate last week. It was a robust discussion with thoughtful questions from Rotarians and a great opportunity to lay out my priorities for the district: the economy, public safety, and keep Eastern Washington strong. I appreciated connecting with community leaders who care deeply about our region. Meanwhile, my opponent repeated her support for higher taxes including the Washington state income tax, and her plan for releasing illegal immigrants from detention to help pay for Social Security. Conversations like these are valuable, and I’m grateful to Rotary 21 for hosting the debate and to KXLY for the livestream.
---
|
---
| |
# Letter to the Editor-
# The Spokesman Review
---
| | Thank you to Janet Peterson for her letter published in the Spokesman-Review last week:
_“Have you forgotten what the Biden administration put this country through? Carmela Conroy, Mayor Lisa Brown and Gov. Ferguson all come from the same school of thought, as do most of Spokane’s City Council. We need to turn this train wreck around! Vote Baumgartner! ”_ Janet Peterson, Spokane
---
|
---
| |
# Christmas Came Early in Spokane
---
|
---
| | Our team brought some holiday spirit to a sign blitz in Spokane this week. Yard signs are going up across the district, and every one of them helps. Let’s keep this momentum going! Ask for your [**yard sign**](https://us.list-manage.com/y3_vKJAnptG?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)[****](https://us.list-manage.com/GDY9luZK21U?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238) today!
---
|
---
| | Only 2 weeks until the General Election! _**Will you host a yard sign? **_Click [**here**](https://us.list-manage.com/BqMFzm_kWUn?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238) to sign up now, or just send an email reply!We need volunteers! If you have a couple of hours to spare, please reach out to us! Visit our [**website**](https://us.list-manage.com/MFV0lmtDzGj?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)**** to sign up now for opportunities, from sign-waving or knocking on doors, or writing letters. **Upcoming Events** Team Baumgartner is on the move across Eastern Washington, focusing on encouraging turnout ahead of the November 3 General Election. Here is where you can find us next:
**Weekday mornings/afternoons:** Sign-waves: Email [here](mailto:stephanie@votebaumgartner.com?subject=Sign-Waves!&body=)[ ](mailto:stephanie@votebaumgartner.com?subject=Sign-Waves!&body=)for details!**Saturday October 24:** Door-knocking Super Saturday: [Join us](https://us.list-manage.com/VdNpUIxr6Ho?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238) as we talk to our neighbors and hear about their concerns!
**Saturday October 31:** Door-knocking Super Saturday: [Join us](https://us.list-manage.com/14KEdkq5tYs?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238) as we talk to our neighbors and hear about their concerns!Thank you for all your help.-Michael
