In those conversations I was pleased to highlight my co-sponsorship of the Secure Rural Schools reauthorization important for Stevens County, and my work on the federal funding for the major expansion of NEW Health rural healthcare services. Thank you to the Chewelah Chamber of Commerce and The Independent for hosting this event. | | | Lunch Debate at Rotary 21 | | | I was glad to take part in the Rotary 21 lunch debate last week. It was a robust discussion with thoughtful questions from Rotarians and a great opportunity to lay out my priorities for the district: the economy, public safety, and keep Eastern Washington strong. I appreciated connecting with community leaders who care deeply about our region. Meanwhile, my opponent repeated her support for higher taxes including the Washington state income tax, and her plan for releasing illegal immigrants from detention to help pay for Social Security. Conversations like these are valuable, and I’m grateful to Rotary 21 for hosting the debate and to KXLY for the livestream. | | | Letter to the Editor- The Spokesman Review | | Thank you to Janet Peterson for her letter published in the Spokesman-Review last week: “Have you forgotten what the Biden administration put this country through? **Peter, it’s John James. **
We're less than 3 weeks away from Election Day. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. _I promise I will not waste your time._
I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted.
I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, _**I would live it.**_
[**Eventually, this led me to apply to West Point, and my decision to serve my country would make me the man I am today.**](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=7e9649d8b65240bfb1e9da8530683989&_e=Ro8XDKxGK_eCr6rIi_PIyN5oAm0zcW6zbRtypbe97sAprK2Ij1R3FuQ9G2K0oi3-u_SZqXtor0h05R6MIqnrlFZDzEPHpMf3yD-ZRp3T6MeNF11OQtbuLr9-V3MaCW4TFuQFLHUIMWlGRy-L2oC3t186r2zPUeLjreAmvtTF32PkcQjPumBjh9HImE9jbMqQyz8fHNhIbh8jAMiw-K7XfuCc-eNXmz8Yd-sF_yPjmwzDtI6oODnXL_EA9ij28MECCfe6nuisidbrv9serVHMrJwQnuzukKlnEpxrsZOjjBhxQ1CdgDu9hy515VNzCFhHcJ_XUFKAWdjNZ7z4R5v_xR46HGc-aOGxisrOGJsvjwEaj7DdoUM8M2Di3rCY0G2tCvzwxiKVmw_fGbwvjCIOc2H7u0g-XlmBUoT8o6tjjA7iDV07-UTbfIS2E-RUGhlEHpHPZFZcw_HcBYQ6tFHbwdBFOSu3V8Ad32Yvi0T6j0W8dmVfrlnICK6xQCwuaozUsKc6QKHRbMoXo64BmAizYG1ekCiO9YjS5D3XtjQg8PsnNy19FQDH-uiu35DaLcy7vTGAD47K5A5O8rXXvY0Mw4NivBopFXPf08GlIyCnUiGjkMV2a7DR6lzgAZkzJ-mwTit4LsazUREUJ_XKUDJJlKcVVSZ7pxUHE4PUariC1qu8cGHlaqzCRXJQ0ypNjXQIq5mDawYIbCdT3kgpg4JVf3ht0FLchHr9OcaENydPKLjNWUPQFQuWVQKB-5R-iSLz6-z88CRMvMFuxsRT1Lp_b4YmqPU8z9vNSofvngygmoM%3D)

Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army.
During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. **Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. **
**I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and _I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud._**

After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, **_I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. _**
I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician...
[**But there comes a point in your life when you stop looking at the issues surrounding you and start thinking about what you can do to fix them.**](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=7e9649d8b65240bfb1e9da8530683989&_e=Ro8XDKxGK_eCr6rIi_PIyN5oAm0zcW6zbRtypbe97sAprK2Ij1R3FuQ9G2K0oi3-u_SZqXtor0h05R6MIqnrlFZDzEPHpMf3yD-ZRp3T6MeNF11OQtbuLr9-V3MaCW4TFuQFLHUIMWlGRy-L2oC3t186r2zPUeLjreAmvtTF32PkcQjPumBjh9HImE9jbMqQyz8fHNhIbh8jAMiw-K7XfuCc-eNXmz8Yd-sF_yPjmwzDtI6oODnXL_EA9ij28MECCfe6nuisidbrv9serVHMrJwQnuzukKlnEpxrsZOjjBi-LUWLpH2iFJAM5wbByB1F9p7aMa0iorcTejgh5tbmR1msjGJAIKuwOmsDWN1LLzeOgLXlT4kXo-J4SQoq14mxHos028KuDBXV8IvneeBUECiKW6aeaiXH9FHfffSXjBp3YbywrYELcaZp3mM5XnQDjgbgJjeOIoyZ3UfxzHfNgVr1-BNcO-FiiDNxqdTX8qg4mMjiJF4iT0lGhJRBJ7rN2zTOVWALh6yQzQvigYzHl9rK8-jO5Lpy7c-kRQiCD__CK0-VuZbEz4MVJCJL8L_g1B_KiDMCrZk1NEcE6y3nZE1PNg_oVzeY8dsMosTcajTTcPYhnIQgqKH0D2UHaLVcdhfa5P5d16vr0kTWQ7ujbmyetAh6c_D2qdcMLO9cUqjxARidrgo3aUJOPhf_IT3bhovLIaMYXTpDMGqhpZ6dehWAYNdtMJkOm2KZpMlS0Q2wgvbuXXe6LZkJUH-US6MYc-bMqDzbV48hvttDgLjAXMz3uEdldvTW850W_WGaP0w%3D)

clean_body: Will you have my back on November 3rd?| | | | | Peter, it’s John James. We're less than 3 weeks away from Election Day. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. I promise I will not waste your time. I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted. I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, I would live it. Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army. During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud. After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician... I saw the Democrats destroying our country, and I knew my service to this great nation wasn’t over yet. Everybody told me running for office isn’t easy, but my heart was telling me it was the right thing to do. I won my election, with the help of President Trump, and started delivering results for my new constituents. Then, in 2023, when the Establishment tried to move on from Trump and being MAGA was seen as risky or politically inconvenient, I was among the first in Michigan to endorse President Trump for 2024. Loyalty isn’t a talking point to me; it’s the only way I know how to operate. My dedication to this country, my loyalty towards my constituents, and my desire to see the greatest nation on earth excel are part of the reasons why I’m now emailing you, but they’re not my #1 reason why... These three kids are the reason why I’m sending this message to you, as a TRUMP-ENDORSED Republican and father running to be the next governor of Michigan Having my own family taught me more lessons than I could list, and it was the one thing being in the U.S. Army didn’t prepare me for. But it also awoke in me a desire to do EVERYTHING and ANYTHING I can to ensure my kids have bright futures. My family means everything to me, and Michigan is our home; that’s why I will fight like my life depends on it to save this state and win this November. I’m under no illusions; I know this election will be one of the toughest challenges I’ve faced in my entire life, but after everything I’ve done in my service, it’s nothing I can’t handle. Unfortunately, the one thing I can’t directly control is spending, and the Democrats will do everything in their power to stop my campaign from making it to the ballot box this November. Nothing can stop us from saving this country if we stand together. Today, I’m asking you to make a small-dollar gift of $10, $25, $50 or ANYTHING you can spare to fuel my campaign’s fight as we approach our upcoming November 3rd election. Thank you for taking the time to read my message. I hope to hear from you in the days to come. In California, voters aren’t waiting for November 3rd. |

Hi there – it’s Senator Adam Schiff. Derek Tran’s first ad of the general election is on the airwaves. It’s called “Many Lives,” and I think the title gets him exactly right. Let me tell you why: Long before Congress, Derek spent his afternoons after school working at his parents’ store. He joined the Army because this country gave his refugee family a chance, and he wanted to give something back. Later, as a workers’ rights attorney, he stood up for immigrants and working families who didn’t have anyone else in their corner. That’s who CA-45 sent to Washington. With two weeks until Election Day, a lot of voters there are meeting him through this ad for the first time. In California, ballots are _already_ on kitchen tables, and voters are mailing them back now. National Republicans have made CA-45 one of their top flip targets, and they’d like nothing more than to define Derek before those voters cast their ballots. We’re two weeks out from Election Day, and House races across the country are entering their final stretch. To help Democrats win, I'm highlighting Frontline Members and Red to Blue candidates in competitive districts who need all the help they can get.
---
_**The current House members in key races:**_ Republicans know that **[Susie Lee (NV-03)](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141821665/654855037/-1911020574?refcode=ga&nvep=&hmac=&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjY2YWE5ZjMtYjBjYy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=w_3am0NO7XroeSF4clT3UHwwElFWznH3drH74eaPAnM=)** , **[Tom Suozzi (NY-03)](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141821666/654855038/-1911020574?refcode=ga&nvep=&hmac=&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjY2YWE5ZjMtYjBjYy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=w_3am0NO7XroeSF4clT3UHwwElFWznH3drH74eaPAnM=)** , and **[Marcy Kaptur (OH-09)](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141821667/654855039/-1911020574?refcode=ga&nvep=&hmac=&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjY2YWE5ZjMtYjBjYy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=w_3am0NO7XroeSF4clT3UHwwElFWznH3drH74eaPAnM=)** won’t be easy to beat. That is why Donald Trump and Republican super PACs are pouring millions of dollars to take them out. They need the resources to continue fighting back and communicating with voters in their districts.
---
**_The candidates for seats we need to flip from Republican to Democratic control_**
---
That’s why I’m highlighting another group of DCCC Red Alert candidates for whom we need to surge resources to win the races that will make the Democratic majority in the House.
---
**_The current House members in key races:_**
---
**[Chris Jones (AR-02)](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141821668/654855040/-1911020574?refcode=ga&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjY2YWE5ZjMtYjBjYy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=w_3am0NO7XroeSF4clT3UHwwElFWznH3drH74eaPAnM=)** is a 7th-generation Arkansan, physicist, ordained minister, and former executive director of the Arkansas Regional Innovation Hub.
---
**[Dr. Amish Shah (AZ-01)](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141821669/654855041/-1911020574?refcode=ga&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjY2YWE5ZjMtYjBjYy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=w_3am0NO7XroeSF4clT3UHwwElFWznH3drH74eaPAnM=) **is an emergency room physician running for Congress after previously coming within four points of winning the district.
---
**[Manny Rutinel (CO-08)](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141821670/654855042/-1911020574?refcode=ga&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjY2YWE5ZjMtYjBjYy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=w_3am0NO7XroeSF4clT3UHwwElFWznH3drH74eaPAnM=) **is the son of a single mother who immigrated from Latin America. He worked at McDonald’s and tutored kids as a teenager, put himself through college, and later served in the Army Corps of Engineers.
---

subject: A pickup truck reminded me of Washington

body:
I'd written down a few thoughts I wanted to share with y'all.

| [](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.-O68Rw)
---
Peter,
This morning I was sitting in traffic watching a fella haul what appeared to be an entire hardware store in the back of a pickup truck.
Somehow that got me thinking about Washington.
Don't ask me how. My brain works in ways I can't even explain.
By the time I got home, I'd scribbled down a few thoughts I wanted to share with y'all.
No out-of-touch DC consultants touched it. No pollsters approved it. No intern cleaned it up.
Just me.
[Give it a read when you've got a minute!](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.)

**Peter, it’s John James. **
We're less than 3 weeks away from Election Day. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. _I promise I will not waste your time._
I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted.
I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, _**I would live it.**_
[**Eventually, this led me to apply to West Point, and my decision to serve my country would make me the man I am today.**](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=30b2ca9f1b9f47b68a8ca53f01e408eb&_e=BIgtrPQrIuFUKyPVt2IWojQIvK06NFM96ekm2FvrJnY2daOi9cVmBNtxPrmdelSmiCbOnxv2eJ9xSVIRmA5b0FCj2V_1n4wJ9hGVyPkBO_EKCkOjufs9b5iXTXlpNXWRbUYhklqWnRgmwIaUYG69mJfPhTvXbq96ppmW4e7qFRx4pnR9dFXe2c4k-mLKvcDDq7nMbu5rY3ndZWgdq8ywJDSVv8laFohI0EvfYfk3H8Kq7NXFGXbAz1ChPSxRJQ1IgkUD0-Ga4DK_euwZon5kDMitB7aUUoZkuRzuP58zpOSVW3xPOpTMiaw55m-NcDWci8vHTN4ozk6lLzDEZs2kAbjhD11SdM47eu1Cc7Wa_7qlLTb8DO2v5QQbeMGMecQADecHdtQnZ_HfehbNP8oSmh_aLz8xmsyB_M63wvxpSXZp9gWhtiQr6gBVi2WXsEEEexk4lrtoORECiLojNMjlucT74SdBBD-PFNP-Y6g2pndxsZ2fq1pexc96bZW72SrcsvbeEAfaJmxyMvdTU48V1P7YJqictB6HMeEhlm18b2Zxvucm9RAohsdtvt21jBngRbxlleL8RkfeD18jQuo0YhpjYyYbFirFiwv53sc2QdQ1NafcXSiGzJVLvwlkWi614yZnJPYoHF3yUiu23Tyj9gMN5wVDYtaEpYZ8cO2vJaR1V7PUnzXvyYTRHKxRT2XQbQSllZfuSctXSwdMKa0gOJt2K4jmaflw6hDsEGo9M5cjAtWdnY50NZuhRJ9jAO20L6_HuEUjKxOkYxn8ruaRwg%3D%3D)

Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army.
During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. **Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. **
**I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and _I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud._**

After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, **_I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. _**
I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician...
[**But there comes a point in your life when you stop looking at the issues surrounding you and start thinking about what you can do to fix them.**](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=30b2ca9f1b9f47b68a8ca53f01e408eb&_e=BIgtrPQrIuFUKyPVt2IWojQIvK06NFM96ekm2FvrJnY2daOi9cVmBNtxPrmdelSmiCbOnxv2eJ9xSVIRmA5b0FCj2V_1n4wJ9hGVyPkBO_EKCkOjufs9b5iXTXlpNXWRbUYhklqWnRgmwIaUYG69mJfPhTvXbq96ppmW4e7qFRx4pnR9dFXe2c4k-mLKvcDDq7nMbu5rY3ndZWgdq8ywJDSVv8laFohI0EvfYfk3H8Kq7NXFGXbAz1ChPSxRJQ1IgkUD0-Ga4DK_euwZon5kDMitB7aUUoZkuRzuP58zpOQfWPugRRghjX1bZIozd3y-v09tygX3J72yfaVMhCVYp8wREPC30BUdm2EN92HhjpqgNBrIsd26yGicA2lYP_7upybqYTzdd7e5Tqkr8XDXq7ogvX8GhakEeOuijtYpJfFQsT5ee7Um17Eq-rQaXT17CPzXBnSq4YmIkEaRgIhigXjPkPTuV3PRm7oitoKWn_yOAHDHyORC0mWYlyCemesy-KRRmVvlnU3rIg1UVPQAupOfUwvV7_8gVcYmaow7gbsvzKu4AxdOid8iIAuD_Zmksj0hztZFzIfyeDhqbw8Cq2TFie9rpTRTSb4AxZLrzN1HjvU-pvhLallHg7cWO4UllgJK6IodnQL4m82DyxfE7l3zuIxwtZI2GWPMC_weexrOcN9zeujuP8mzAmJ7fkTc2BNeUQzl8B7K8syekpXwcBi8RTEfOZ27jnMG9pYBzlhwjGLRWmwCHFJjRkXyv1yuCH81EAz_xXzlfPvKwYUo0caQGAcIPzhmHqnKoL3Nh2c%3D)

clean_body: My story as a black Republican combat veteran| | | | | Peter, it’s John James. We're less than 3 weeks away from Election Day. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. I promise I will not waste your time. I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted. I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, I would live it. Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army. During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud. After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician... I saw the Democrats destroying our country, and I knew my service to this great nation wasn’t over yet. Everybody told me running for office isn’t easy, but my heart was telling me it was the right thing to do. I won my election, with the help of President Trump, and started delivering results for my new constituents. Then, in 2023, when the Establishment tried to move on from Trump and being MAGA was seen as risky or politically inconvenient, I was among the first in Michigan to endorse President Trump for 2024. Loyalty isn’t a talking point to me; it’s the only way I know how to operate. My dedication to this country, my loyalty towards my constituents, and my desire to see the greatest nation on earth excel are part of the reasons why I’m now emailing you, but they’re not my #1 reason why... These three kids are the reason why I’m sending this message to you, as a TRUMP-ENDORSED Republican and father running to be the next governor of Michigan Having my own family taught me more lessons than I could list, and it was the one thing being in the U.S. Army didn’t prepare me for. But it also awoke in me a desire to do EVERYTHING and ANYTHING I can to ensure my kids have bright futures. My family means everything to me, and Michigan is our home; that’s why I will fight like my life depends on it to save this state and win this November. I’m under no illusions; I know this election will be one of the toughest challenges I’ve faced in my entire life, but after everything I’ve done in my service, it’s nothing I can’t handle. Unfortunately, the one thing I can’t directly control is spending, and the Democrats will do everything in their power to stop my campaign from making it to the ballot box this November. Nothing can stop us from saving this country if we stand together. I sat down with Ken Boddie on KOIN this week, two weeks out from Election Day, to talk about where Oregon's elections stand. If you missed it, here's the short version. Ken asked how secure the system really is. So I walked him through it:
* Every voter gets a paper ballot, and every envelope that comes back is checked against the signature county clerks have on file.
* The machines that count those ballots are never connected to the internet, every step is audited, and every ballot is available to be recounted.
* Drop boxes have cameras and fire suppression, and we're adding 20 more boxes statewide before Election Day.

**Then he asked the question I knew was coming: the Supreme Court blocked the president's executive order against vote-by-mail. Are we out of the woods?** **No.** The Court was clear that the order can't touch this election. But that fight will likely continue after the election, and **I told Ken what I've learned the hard way: trying to predict what this president is going to do next is not a smart plan.** What I can tell you is this. clean_body: | | | = | | | Did you see my latest interview? = I sat down with Ken Boddie on KOIN this week, two weeks out from Election Day, to talk about where Oregon's elections stand. If you missed it, here's the short version. Ken asked how secure the system really is. So I walked him through it: Every voter gets a paper ballot, and every envelope that comes back is checked against the signature county clerks have on file. The machines that count those ballots are never connected to the internet, every step is audited, and every ballot is available to be recounted. Drop boxes have cameras and fire suppression, and we're adding 20 more boxes statewide before Election Day. Then he asked the question I knew was coming: the Supreme Court blocked the president's executive order against vote-by-mail. Are we out of the woods? No. The Court was clear that the order can't touch this election. But that fight will likely continue after the election, and I told Ken what I've learned the hard way: trying to predict what this president is going to do next is not a smart plan. What I can tell you is this. The Constitution gives states the job of running elections. The president doesn't have a role in it. And we're going to use every legal tool we have to keep it that way. But I need you with me. =** = Thank you.— Tobias = | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Friends of Tobias Read (5208) PO Box 42307 Portland, OR 97242 United States If you believe you received this message in error or wish to no longer receive email from us, please .

Urgent: Vote NO on 3 Extreme Amendments
---
| |

| VIRGINIA IS FOR PATRIOTS!

| Friends,It is an honor to represent James Madison's district in the House of Delegates. Madison helped write our founding documents, and I take seriously what's at stake when anyone tries to rewrite ours.On Tuesday, November 3, that's exactly what's on your ballot. Richmond Democrats want to rewrite the Constitution of Virginia three times in one election. My answer is simple: Vote NO on ALL 3 Amendments.❌❌❌
Please read past the short ballot questions. The real language goes much further than the summary tells you. ❌ Question 1: The "Reproductive Freedom" Amendment
This is not a modest change. It writes a new "fundamental right to reproductive freedom" into our Bill of Rights, and it reaches far beyond abortion. The Family Foundation of Virginia has gone through the full text line by line. Here's what they're warning:
* Parents get cut out. The right belongs to "every individual," with no exception for minors. The Foundation warns this could wipe out a parent's right to know about, or consent to, their minor child's abortion. This leaves young girls wide open to human traffickers and abusers who want it kept quiet.
* Abortion up to the moment of birth. Virginia law currently permits third-trimester abortion when THREE physicians agree that the woman's health may be irremediably harmed if the pregnancy continued. This amendment allows it whenever a SINGLE physician (the abortionist) says it is needed for the woman's "physical or mental health." One signature. Zero regard for viability.
* Weaker health and safety standards for women. Eliminates the state's ability to penalize or regulate individuals "aiding" reproductive freedom. The Foundation warns this reduces oversight, accountability, and liability for harm done to the woman.
* Our children and "fertility care." Because "fertility care" is a right with no age limit, minors could get sterilizing or gender-transition procedures. Confused children making permanent, life-threatening decisions, without Mom and Dad knowing.

I will always stand for life. Vote NO. ❌❌ Question 2: The Marriage Amendment
This amendment strikes the definition of marriage as the union of one man and one woman from our Constitution. In its place it puts a right to marry "regardless of the sex, gender, or race" of the two people. This bizarre wording deserves a closer look.
* Gender ideology written into our Constitution. By naming "sex" and "gender" as two separate things, the amendment could pressure schools, businesses, and government to adopt policies that conflict with biological reality.
* Our girls' sports and private spaces. Legal experts warn this could open girls' sports, locker rooms, and shelters to biological males. Our daughters shouldn't have to fight this battle.
* Zero protection for conscience. There is no religious or conscience exemption. Not for pastors, not for churches, not for faith-based organizations, not for small businesses. The earlier draft had protections for religious liberty; the final draft removed them. If it is not the intent to compel people of faith to violate their beliefs, why remove them?
* Destruction of the nuclear family. Marriage reduced to personal happiness. The amendment drops the language that recognizes marriage's role in raising children and building strong, stable families.

❌ Question 3: Automatic Voting Rights for Felons
Question 3 would automatically restore voting and other political rights (jury, notary, holding public office and potentially gun rights) to every felon the moment he walks out of prison. That includes violent offenders. He would not have to finish probation or pay restitution to his victims first. Criminals before victims, again.
It also adds a right to vote that "shall not be abridged by law," and critics warn that phrase could be used to challenge common-sense election-integrity laws. Restoration should come after a sentence is finished. Period.Question 3 Also Rewrites Who Counts as "Able" to Vote
There's a second change buried in Question 3 that almost no one is talking about.
* Mental capacity. Our Constitution has long said a person found mentally incompetent cannot vote until that is restored. Question 3 replaces it with a much narrower rule: the vote stays live unless a judge makes a second, specific ruling that the person can't "understand the act of voting." Governor Youngkin vetoed this change in 2025 for good reason.
* An open door for ballot abuse. Think about who this covers: seniors with advanced dementia in nursing homes and memory-care units. Every one of those ballots is a ballot someone else can fill out, steer, or harvest. And who's checking? This is an election integrity problem, hiding behind the veil of compassion and "democracy." And once it's in our Constitution, Richmond can't fix it.

Our elections should be secure, and every legitimate vote should count. Vote NO. ❌🗳️ Your Vote Matters. Use It!
Please vote NO on Questions 1, 2, and 3, and share this with your family, your friends, and your church. Early voting is open now, and Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Vote Doug Ollivant for 7th District Congress and Bert Mizusawa for US Senate! We can't do this without every patriot showing up. I'll continue to defend life, liberty, and common sense here in Virginia. Thank you for standing with me. God bless,
KarenDelegate Karen Hamilton
Virginia House of Delegates, District 62

clean_body: Urgent: Vote NO on 3 Extreme Amendments | | | VIRGINIA IS FOR PATRIOTS! | Friends,It is an honor to represent James Madison's district in the House of Delegates. Madison helped write our founding documents, and I take seriously what's at stake when anyone tries to rewrite ours.On Tuesday, November 3, that's exactly what's on your ballot. Richmond Democrats want to rewrite the Constitution of Virginia three times in one election. My answer is simple: Vote NO on ALL 3 Amendments.❌❌❌ Please read past the short ballot questions. The real language goes much further than the summary tells you. ❌ Question 1: The "Reproductive Freedom" Amendment This is not a modest change. It writes a new "fundamental right to reproductive freedom" into our Bill of Rights, and it reaches far beyond abortion. The Family Foundation of Virginia has gone through the full text line by line. Here's what they're warning: Parents get cut out. The right belongs to "every individual," with no exception for minors. The Foundation warns this could wipe out a parent's right to know about, or consent to, their minor child's abortion. This leaves young girls wide open to human traffickers and abusers who want it kept quiet. Abortion up to the moment of birth. Virginia law currently permits third-trimester abortion when THREE physicians agree that the woman's health may be irremediably harmed if the pregnancy continued. This amendment allows it whenever a SINGLE physician (the abortionist) says it is needed for the woman's "physical or mental health." One signature. Zero regard for viability. Weaker health and safety standards for women. Eliminates the state's ability to penalize or regulate individuals "aiding" reproductive freedom. The Foundation warns this reduces oversight, accountability, and liability for harm done to the woman. Our children and "fertility care." Because "fertility care" is a right with no age limit, minors could get sterilizing or gender-transition procedures. Confused children making permanent, life-threatening decisions, without Mom and Dad knowing. I will always stand for life. Vote NO. ❌❌ Question 2: The Marriage Amendment This amendment strikes the definition of marriage as the union of one man and one woman from our Constitution. In its place it puts a right to marry "regardless of the sex, gender, or race" of the two people. This bizarre wording deserves a closer look. Gender ideology written into our Constitution. By naming "sex" and "gender" as two separate things, the amendment could pressure schools, businesses, and government to adopt policies that conflict with biological reality. Our girls' sports and private spaces. Legal experts warn this could open girls' sports, locker rooms, and shelters to biological males. Our daughters shouldn't have to fight this battle. Zero protection for conscience. There is no religious or conscience exemption. Not for pastors, not for churches, not for faith-based organizations, not for small businesses. The earlier draft had protections for religious liberty; the final draft removed them. If it is not the intent to compel people of faith to violate their beliefs, why remove them? Destruction of the nuclear family. Marriage reduced to personal happiness. The amendment drops the language that recognizes marriage's role in raising children and building strong, stable families. ❌ Question 3: Automatic Voting Rights for Felons Question 3 would automatically restore voting and other political rights (jury, notary, holding public office and potentially gun rights) to every felon the moment he walks out of prison. That includes violent offenders. He would not have to finish probation or pay restitution to his victims first. Criminals before victims, again. It also adds a right to vote that "shall not be abridged by law," and critics warn that phrase could be used to challenge common-sense election-integrity laws. Restoration should come after a sentence is finished. Period.Question 3 Also Rewrites Who Counts as "Able" to Vote There's a second change buried in Question 3 that almost no one is talking about. Mental capacity. Our Constitution has long said a person found mentally incompetent cannot vote until that is restored. Question 3 replaces it with a much narrower rule: the vote stays live unless a judge makes a second, specific ruling that the person can't "understand the act of voting." Governor Youngkin vetoed this change in 2025 for good reason. An open door for ballot abuse. Think about who this covers: seniors with advanced dementia in nursing homes and memory-care units. Every one of those ballots is a ballot someone else can fill out, steer, or harvest. And who's checking? This is an election integrity problem, hiding behind the veil of compassion and "democracy." And once it's in our Constitution, Richmond can't fix it. Our elections should be secure, and every legitimate vote should count. Vote NO. ❌🗳️ Your Vote Matters. Use It! Please vote NO on Questions 1, 2, and 3, and share this with your family, your friends, and your church. Early voting is open now, and Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Greg Abbott and Gina Hinojosa are in a statistical dead heat.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)

Peter, it’s Jane Fonda.
I’ve dedicated my life to fighting corruption when and where I see it. So you can imagine how I felt when I learned about Gina Hinojosa.
In 2021, Gina and her fellow Texas Democrats walked out of the legislature and broke quorum to block a bill that would have made it _harder_ to vote.
Now, Gina is running for governor against Greg Abbott, and this race is neck and neck.
**That’s my kind of fighter. 💪**
Nothing changes at the scale we need until we change the people in power. Electing Gina Hinojosa is how we do that in Texas.
**[But we need a whole lot of us coming together in these final 14 days to defeat one of the most powerful incumbents in the country. Peter, will you join me and chip in $5 or anything you can to elect Gina as the next Governor of Texas?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261020_2_janefonda.bwWUm2&refcode=em20261020-2490&amount=5&t=2&akid=2490%2E299639%2EqNMrRu)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261020_2_janefonda.bwWUm2&amount=5&refcode=em20261020-2490&t=3&akid=2490%2E299639%2EqNMrRu)
Imagine waking up on November 4 to the news that Greg Abbott lost.
A three-term incumbent, with his oil executive donors and a _MASSIVE_ war chest, beaten by a grassroots movement of folks ready to take back Texas.
That’s not a fantasy.
**Gina has shocked the country. At the beginning of the year, almost nobody expected Texas to be this competitive. But her campaign is proving that organized people can beat organized money.**
If the many can beat the money in Texas — in a state where one party has held the governor’s mansion for over 30 years — I believe they can beat it _anywhere_.
Gina’s campaign has momentum. Poll after poll show her beating Abbott. But she does not have the resources to match that momentum, and we’re running out of time to help her out.

subject: I rock my ribbon skirt to honor my ancestors:
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/1102?refcode=jtk1612-fr-nd&t=1&akid=13317%2E400544%2EZZ7-9X)
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17482?refcode=jtk1612-fr-nd&t=2&akid=13317%2E400544%2EZZ7-9X)
Hi friend, it's Deb Haaland. I am the daughter of Pueblo women, a single mother, a former small business owner, a former Congresswoman, and the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in U.S. history. **And thanks to your support, I am the official Democratic nominee for Governor of New Mexico.**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17482?refcode=jtk1612-fr-nd&t=3&akid=13317%2E400544%2EZZ7-9X)

Last night, I stood in front of Kentucky for the single debate my opponent dared to join me for. After seeing his performance, it became pretty clear why.

If you missed it, it's not too late - here's the link to watch: [watch the debate](https://substack.com/redirect/4f72a85c-0be6-4345-83ab-1a02c640118a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

---|---|---
Barr parroted Trump's failed playbook to a T, all while claiming to be the "common sense" candidate.
Whether it was ramblings about the "necessary" Iran War, blaming Joe Biden for rising costs, or his blatant hypocrisy claiming to support term limits while serving five terms, Andy was anything but common sense.
He wants to call himself the America-first candidate. But when the spotlight is on him, his priorities look a lot more like Trump first, Kentucky second.
If you're still not convinced, follow the money. MAGA-aligned Super PAC "Keep America Great PAC" has spent $5 million backing him - talk about handouts!
He can't stand on his own two feet without the MAGA machine's support. And as long as Trump & friends line his pockets, the priorities of real Kentuckians will always be pushed to the sidelines.
**Andy is ready to carry on Mitch McConnell 's legacy of putting wealthy donors and President Trump's agenda first. I'm fighting for a Kentucky where this Senate seat belongs to the people -- not the special interests trying to buy it.**
Early voting starts in just 9 days, mail-in ballots are already being sent out, and Andy and I are tied. I need to pull ahead, and there's no room for error at this late stage.
Can you chip in today to help us make sure every single undecided Kentucky voter hears our message?

Kentucky deserves better. Let's deliver a brighter future, together.
Thanks for tuning in.
Charles Booker.

**Derek, I’m inviting you on an all-expenses paid trip to meet me in Boston or DC.**[**Chip in $7, or any amount, to the DNC and you’ll be entered to win a free trip to meet me for you and a friend.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-warren-sweepstakes-2026.k_RvmO&refcode=em_20261020_9979_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=9979%2E22930333%2EBss1xM)

I’ve been doing everything I can to make sure Democrats win back majorities in the House and Senate this November, and as a member of the DNC’s Grassroots team, I know you have been, too. That’s why I want to meet you to say _thank you_ for all that you do.
**If Democrats win back our majorities, we can stop congressional Republicans from enabling the president.**
**We can block any far-right, extremist judge that Trump nominates to the Supreme Court.**
**And, critically, we can use those majorities to actually pass policies that you will _feel_ in your day-to-day life.**
I’ve done my homework: there is a narrow path to retake our majorities in Congress, but it can be done. We need to flip four seats to take back the Senate, which means we need to put up a strong defense in Michigan and Georgia, AND a strong offense in Maine, North Carolina, Iowa, Ohio, Texas, and Alaska.

It's Karl Rove.I've spent decades in and around politics - advising presidents, running national campaigns, and watching hundreds of Senate races unfold from the inside. In all that time, I've learned to be careful about where I put my name and my energy. I don't back just anyone.But Susan Collins is different, Peter.I've watched her operate in the Senate for years, and what strikes me most isn't just her experience - it's her independence. She doesn't vote with a party out of habit. She studies the issue, talks to the people it affects, and makes the call she believes is right for Maine. That's rare in Washington today, and it's exactly why she's earned the trust of voters again and again.Right now, that independence and grit are being tested like never before. Troy Jackson and the Far-left machine behind him are pouring everything they have into flipping this seat because they know that if they take Maine, they take the Senate majority with it.Let me be blunt: this race will be one of the closest and most consequential in the country. It won't be decided by Maine alone. It will be decided by whether supporters in all 50 states step up the way they did for the races that mattered most in past cycles.That's why I'm writing to you directly today.Susan doesn't need a miracle. She needs steady, committed support from people like you who understand what's at stake - not just for Maine, but for the direction of the entire United States Senate. One seat can be the difference between a Senate that holds the line and one that hands total control to the Far-Left.I've seen races like this before. The ones who show up in these final, critical stretches are the ones who decide the outcome.[Can you join me and chip in today to help Susan finish strong?](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.)

I want to be direct with you about something I am watching closely.

Democrats are not just playing defense this cycle. They are on offense - targeting red states they have no business competing in, flooding them with outside money, and running candidates specifically designed to fool voters into thinking they are getting a moderate when they are actually getting another loyal Schumer vote.

**Montana is one of those states. But I refuse to let it slip away without a fight.**

I refuse to let that happen here.

Kurt Alme is exactly the kind of candidate Montana needs - a Trump-nominated federal prosecutor with a real record of results. He took on cartels, drug traffickers, and violent criminals as U.S. attorney. He cut Montana's income tax rate. He helped make Montana debt-free. **_He has President Trump's complete and total endorsement, and mine._**

clean_body: Democrats are flooding red states with outside money. Montana cannot be the one that slips away. | FROM THE DESK OF SENATOR JOHN THUNE: I want to be direct with you about something I am watching closely. Democrats are not just playing defense this cycle. They are on offense - targeting red states they have no business competing in, flooding them with outside money, and running candidates specifically designed to fool voters into thinking they are getting a moderate when they are actually getting another loyal Schumer vote. Montana is one of those states. But I refuse to let it slip away without a fight. I have served in the Senate long enough to know how these races unfold. Democrats identify a target, recruit a candidate, and pour in millions of dollars before the Republican side has had time to build. By the time conservatives see what is happening, the gap is already significant. I refuse to let that happen here. Kurt Alme is exactly the kind of candidate Montana needs - a Trump-nominated federal prosecutor with a real record of results. He took on cartels, drug traffickers, and violent criminals as U.S. attorney. He cut Montana's income tax rate. He helped make Montana debt-free. He has President Trump's complete and total endorsement, and mine. But here is the reality. Schumer has two candidates in this race, both funded by out-of-state money, both running the same bait-and-switch playbook we have seen in state after state. They are not running to represent Montana. They are running to give the Senate back to Chuck Schumer. Fellow Conservative, maintaining our Senate Republican Majority is not just about this seat - it is about our ability to confirm conservative judges, advance President Trump's agenda, and provide a check on Washington's excesses. Every seat matters. This one especially. I hope we can count on you. Thank you, - John Thune P.S. Democrats are targeting Montana because they think they can flip it. A new 60-second radio ad aimed at Troy Jackson doesn't bother needling Jackson for not knowing the difference between Medicare and Medicaid. Instead, the ad targets issues that, in modern American democracy, might just matter more.
"Troy Jackson is weird," SLF's fake country singer belts, closing with a line you don't often hear: "If he'll f--- his own family, he'll f--- yours too."
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack.com/redirect/bde0ebd1-054d-4263-920a-ebcb586165b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The spot is called "Yours Too" and it was produced by the Republican Senate Leadership Fund, one of the many Washington, D.C.-based political committees backing U.S. Sen. Susan Collins. SLF is the GOP super PAC long tied to Mitch McConnell (may he rest in peace) and now aligned with Majority Leader John Thune.
Here is what the ad says and what the PAC offers to back each line.
**" He has two kids with his cousin. If he'll screw his own family, he'll screw yours too."**
The source is my July 30 story, [RELATIVE ATTRACTION: Troy Jackson's Longtime Lover Is His Second Cousin](https://substack.com/redirect/6d198cb2-eada-4569-b473-8a2a7e5fbaf1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which used genealogical records to trace Jackson and Lana Pelletier, the mother of his two adult sons, to shared great-grandparents, Thomas Pelletier and Edith Thibodeau.
Jackson has addressed the cousin issue before. In September he said Collins was "attacking my personal life, my children, stuff like that, because her record sucks," [per the Washington Examiner](https://substack.com/redirect/753e1830-f62a-42cb-9c8e-9cf4a9adb1cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

subject: This firefighter has Trump nervous
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Working Families Party PAC (77 Sands St
body:
| | | Peter — **Donald Trump’s super PAC just dropped nearly $50,000 more into Pennsylvania’s 7th district to stop Bob Brooks, the WFP-endorsed firefighter running for Congress. 1 **That’s on top of the $295,000 they _already_ threw at this race last month.2 Trump is worried, and for good reason. **Earlier this month, the Cook Political Report moved Bob’s race from “Toss-up” to “Lean Democrat.” 3** This race is now a national priority for Republicans. If they lose seats like this one, they could lose control of the House, and that’s a risk Trump can’t afford. So his super PAC is flooding the district with ads to stop Bob’s momentum and drag his opponent, Ryan Mackenzie, across the finish line. **But the numbers are on our side, Peter. Last time, Republicans only won this seat by _4,000_ votes, which means a strong final push could flip it blue. **[**Can you split a donation between WFP and Bob Brooks’ campaign to help us get Bob’s message in front of every voter who could help us win?**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T96dd_312ZULeNpPvEkGMo4N40BCKWb3GevKPKwEASRoL2Dr398e_kaDQRKZ2IMnAG4GZOPyDahSiCRuL2o7KqKdbFJXixtXVxFDIib-xmxCoWRqImyV5D_Vh3LcH0P46JUtRL6aw2oFuSBAzCSonSZT_LEpDjH9o3ZPnQ6ms1ZBoyQ51XDRDsCbSricZ8zZiXYtz5lLXNc0DbHPoY-4IGmv_M_uvleK8HJeaPTh-rmaPFsxIEYqrbEKIEEXC9nWw4qc_v6z3w5Sc6UdHu0mHUPDa9JD8opNQmLKkJMgoxIkxt063-TCKMNqhPJlbqA8LjOGpG-KzzlQkQAP7YcAvwbg/4v1/7Cp7GUqISpeTTi8tu7RjaA/h0/h001.6SOZ6pgGJ0T4V3fZncxzT452fmxH6j9q5b3yxvlYTFY) **[Donate $10 »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T96dd_312ZULeNpPvEkGMo4N40BCKWb3GevKPKwEASRoIst61SMuyDdxIMKVHl9HMvRjcb-yp2aAAIrKoswa6snuESFo48fNFFEzppcEjrF9fS2-3nIR--DjULetRCpy2_A75KifMP9PifEbPfewUA4SUvnKUlwsF6t8NHsMdL2bIJqnCTWwPO4HvldqEapZyEBUllud5H20aPmepLcr-qHHOYap6V6XpDqzV5iARX30thwXhLLf5jLfoFBjHzf9PB1sf1yxlPiJGNgNjGNl3_fNnceAo2compLlOWV4wDrMM5p2h1ab55Br0SV2SgZy1sAVZ5Ujm_AnHgfSXaU8XGGPUZVZGPGR6YGWMCdu-YFw8/4v1/7Cp7GUqISpeTTi8tu7RjaA/h1/h001.S2HNYawnM9hRUly8bGREPWffSeBezFuuuAI2PAtD5M0)** Bob has been very clear about what’s at stake: “Ryan Mackenzie got to D.C. and spent two years pouring fuel on the fire. He and Donald Trump promised to bring costs down and end endless wars. Instead, prices keep climbing, and they dragged us into a reckless war of choice in Iran.”4 Bob’s not exaggerating. Mackenzie voted _eight_ times to protect Trump’s tariffs and _six_ times to keep the war in Iran going,5 while families in his district paid more for groceries, gas, rent, and health care. As Bob put it, “It’s about time we sent a working person to D.C. who knows how to put out a fire.” **Bob is _literally_ that person, Peter. **He spent 20 years as a firefighter, then went on to lead the union representing more than 8,000 firefighters across Pennsylvania, where he fought for better wages, health care, and safer working conditions. Now, he’s taking that fight to Congress. And unlike Mackenzie, Bob doesn’t take a dime of corporate PAC money, so he answers only to the working people who elect him. **His agenda shows it: banning corporate money from politics, guaranteeing health care through Medicare for All, lowering the cost of housing, child care, and groceries, and making billionaires finally pay their fair share.** So the choice in PA-07 comes down to this, Peter: a firefighter who answers to working people, or a puppet who answers to whoever’s pulling his strings. **With two weeks left, this race is only going to heat up, and Trump’s super PAC will keep throwing money on the fire. clean_body: | | | Peter — Donald Trump’s super PAC just dropped nearly $50,000 more into Pennsylvania’s 7th district to stop Bob Brooks, the WFP-endorsed firefighter running for Congress. 1 That’s on top of the $295,000 they already threw at this race last month.2 Trump is worried, and for good reason. Earlier this month, the Cook Political Report moved Bob’s race from “Toss-up” to “Lean Democrat.” 3 This race is now a national priority for Republicans. If they lose seats like this one, they could lose control of the House, and that’s a risk Trump can’t afford. So his super PAC is flooding the district with ads to stop Bob’s momentum and drag his opponent, Ryan Mackenzie, across the finish line. But the numbers are on our side, Peter. Last time, Republicans only won this seat by 4,000 votes, which means a strong final push could flip it blue. Bob has been very clear about what’s at stake: “Ryan Mackenzie got to D.C. and spent two years pouring fuel on the fire. He and Donald Trump promised to bring costs down and end endless wars. Instead, prices keep climbing, and they dragged us into a reckless war of choice in Iran.”4 Bob’s not exaggerating. Mackenzie voted eight times to protect Trump’s tariffs and six times to keep the war in Iran going,5 while families in his district paid more for groceries, gas, rent, and health care. As Bob put it, “It’s about time we sent a working person to D.C. who knows how to put out a fire.” Bob is literally that person, Peter. He spent 20 years as a firefighter, then went on to lead the union representing more than 8,000 firefighters across Pennsylvania, where he fought for better wages, health care, and safer working conditions. Now, he’s taking that fight to Congress. And unlike Mackenzie, Bob doesn’t take a dime of corporate PAC money, so he answers only to the working people who elect him. His agenda shows it: banning corporate money from politics, guaranteeing health care through Medicare for All, lowering the cost of housing, child care, and groceries, and making billionaires finally pay their fair share. So the choice in PA-07 comes down to this, Peter: a firefighter who answers to working people, or a puppet who answers to whoever’s pulling his strings. With two weeks left, this race is only going to heat up, and Trump’s super PAC will keep throwing money on the fire. Bob will be outspent, but with your help, he won’t be out-organized. In solidarity, (and ready to put out a MAGA dumpster fire), Working Families Party Sources: 1\. , Federal Election Commission (FEC), October 14, 2026. 2\. , The New York Times, September 15, 2026. 3\. , The Philadelphia Inquirer, October 9, 2026. 4\. , Lehigh Valley Live, October 19, 2026. Dear Friend, There are just two weeks until Election Day, and the choice could not be clearer in the race for Rhode Island Attorney General.
I have spent my career standing up for Rhode Islanders as a frontline prosecutor under three AG's, a policy advisor to two governors, and the head of a state agency. As Attorney General, I'll defend Rhode Islanders' fundamental rights and create a new unit dedicated to protecting the right to choose - a right currently under attack by the Trump administration.
Meanwhile, my Republican opponent has made clear that he opposes abortion under any circumstance. He has been charged with dozens of crimes - including a capital offense. **And he is not even licensed to practice law in Rhode Island.**
This election should be a landslide, and yet a recent poll shows that my opponent already has the support of a third of Rhode Island voters. **In a state where Donald Trump received 42% of the vote, we cannot take anything for granted.**
There is too much at stake in this election to take any chances, and we need your help to make sure my opponent cannot come within striking distance of the Attorney General's Office.

subject: What the closing stretch looks like
body:
It's all hands on deck on the ground right now

| |

Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army.
During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. **Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. **
**I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and _I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud._**

clean_body: Will you have my back on November 3rd?| | | | | Patriot, it’s John James. We're less than 3 weeks away from Election Day. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. I promise I will not waste your time. I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted. I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, I would live it. Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army. During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud. After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician... I saw the Democrats destroying our country, and I knew my service to this great nation wasn’t over yet. Everybody told me running for office isn’t easy, but my heart was telling me it was the right thing to do. I won my election, with the help of President Trump, and started delivering results for my new constituents. Then, in 2023, when the Establishment tried to move on from Trump and being MAGA was seen as risky or politically inconvenient, I was among the first in Michigan to endorse President Trump for 2024. Loyalty isn’t a talking point to me; it’s the only way I know how to operate. My dedication to this country, my loyalty towards my constituents, and my desire to see the greatest nation on earth excel are part of the reasons why I’m now emailing you, but they’re not my #1 reason why... These three kids are the reason why I’m sending this message to you, as a TRUMP-ENDORSED Republican and father running to be the next governor of Michigan Having my own family taught me more lessons than I could list, and it was the one thing being in the U.S. Army didn’t prepare me for. But it also awoke in me a desire to do EVERYTHING and ANYTHING I can to ensure my kids have bright futures. My family means everything to me, and Michigan is our home; that’s why I will fight like my life depends on it to save this state and win this November. I’m under no illusions; I know this election will be one of the toughest challenges I’ve faced in my entire life, but after everything I’ve done in my service, it’s nothing I can’t handle. Unfortunately, the one thing I can’t directly control is spending, and the Democrats will do everything in their power to stop my campaign from making it to the ballot box this November. Nothing can stop us from saving this country if we stand together. Today, I’m asking you to make a small-dollar gift of $10, $25, $50 or ANYTHING you can spare to fuel my campaign’s fight as we approach our upcoming November 3rd election. Thank you for taking the time to read my message. I hope to hear from you in the days to come. | **IN CASE YOU MISSED IT**

**UVM Economics Professor, Dr. Art Woolf Says:**
**Janoo’s economic ideas are “ _way outside the mainstream of economics_.”******
In a new report by Vermont Public’s Peter Hirschfeld, retired University of Vermont economics professor Dr. Art Woolf raised very big red flags about the feasibility and costs of Amanda Janoo’s economic proposals.*

Dr. Woolf, who also previously served as the State Economist under Democratic Governor Madeleine Kunin, described Janoo’s platform as “way outside the mainstream of economics.”

**This is particularly newsworthy because Dr. Woolf is an _actual_ economist.**

Dr. Woolf warns that Janoo’s programs appear unworkable; drive high-income households out of Vermont; and increase healthcare costs.

Here’s what Professor Woolf told Vermont Public:
* Janoo’s platform is **“way outside the mainstream of economics.”**
* _He sees no plans to translate her theories into practice._
* **“There so much in there of these grandiose schemes that it’s really hard to figure out how you would do them in terms of actually setting them out,** ” he said. **“And I doubt most of them would work.”**
* Janoo’s healthcare proposal also has the potential to increase the costs of primary care, not lower them.

_**by David Shuster**_
Over the last ten years, there has been a tradition in MAGA economics of measuring prosperity not by a worker's earnings, grocery prices, or even what remains in somebody's pocket after paying for gas, housing, and health care, but by what Donald Trump says. Under this system, most of the public may be growing poorer, the cost of living may be climbing, and the family budget may be coming apart at the seams. But none of that matters. Trump declares economic greatness and anybody who declares otherwise is a traitor and/or fake news.
Now, less than two weeks until the midterm elections, Trump and his administration deputies are leaning into the top issue for voters--the economy--and lying with an enthusiasm and intensity unknown to humankind.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/224cf529-f4c2-4782-9ccc-4b36230a4f67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
At the White House Rose Garden, where Dementia Don announced a women's health care task force chaired by RFK Jr. (oh the ironies), Trump also declared that consumer prices are, "coming way down. I'm seeing. Down, down, down."
One almost has to admire the simplicity. There is no need for elaborate economic theory, no tiresome consultation with the Bureau of Labor Statistics, no investigation of the typical family finances. The President has seen it. Down, down, down. The case is closed.
Unfortunately for Trump and the GOP, the business of prices is conducted in the vulgar world of arithmetic, where Trumpian delusions have never been recognized as a unit of measurement.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/224cf529-f4c2-4782-9ccc-4b36230a4f67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
According to Trump's own Bureau of Labor Statistics, inflation was 3.0% when Joe Biden left office and Trump took over in January 2025. Now, inflation stands at 3.7%.
That does not mean every price is rising at the same rate, nor does it mean that the price level itself has jumped by that amount. It means that the pace of inflation has increased. The distinction is elementary, but elementary distinctions have a way of becoming inconvenient for the Trump buffoonery squad.
Trump's defenders could reasonably argue that inflation is affected by many forces, that some prices fall while others rise, and that no administration controls every fluctuation in the market. All true.
But this is precisely why a President who makes wild claims about falling prices should be prepared to show his or her work. Otherwise, we are left with an administration demanding credit for the economy while treating unwelcome data as subversive threats.
At the same White House Rose Garden event, Trump said that China's President Xi Jinping was at the White House a week earlier, when the visit had occurred about a month before. Does this confusion signify Trump has dementia? Add it to the list. But whether you believe or not that Trump's brain is rotting, this incident does beg a more ordinary question: why must the public so often be asked to reconcile Trump's pronouncements with the plain record of events and basic facts?

Prices are up, wages are behind, and the White House says you're reading it wrong | | and | Oct 20| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Cliff 's Note: Inflation just hit 3.7%. Donald Trump stood in the Rose Garden and said prices are going "down, down, down." David Shuster did the arithmetic so you don't have to. Behind the paywall: David rips apart how Trump explains away his own numbers: a "blip" that won't end, a hotel-lobby theory of prosperity, a jobs "record" that's just population growth. Then there 's what Trump brags about instead. Insane. ! -- Cliff | | ---|---|--- by David Shuster** Over the last ten years, there has been a tradition in MAGA economics of measuring prosperity not by a worker's earnings, grocery prices, or even what remains in somebody's pocket after paying for gas, housing, and health care, but by what Donald Trump says. Under this system, most of the public may be growing poorer, the cost of living may be climbing, and the family budget may be coming apart at the seams. But none of that matters. Trump declares economic greatness and anybody who declares otherwise is a traitor and/or fake news. Now, less than two weeks until the midterm elections, Trump and his administration deputies are leaning into the top issue for voters--the economy--and lying with an enthusiasm and intensity unknown to humankind. | | ---|---|--- At the White House Rose Garden, where Dementia Don announced a women's health care task force chaired by RFK Jr. (oh the ironies), Trump also declared that consumer prices are, "coming way down. I'm seeing. Down, down, down." One almost has to admire the simplicity. There is no need for elaborate economic theory, no tiresome consultation with the Bureau of Labor Statistics, no investigation of the typical family finances. The President has seen it. Down, down, down. The case is closed. Unfortunately for Trump and the GOP, the business of prices is conducted in the vulgar world of arithmetic, where Trumpian delusions have never been recognized as a unit of measurement. | | ---|---|--- According to Trump's own Bureau of Labor Statistics, inflation was 3.0% when Joe Biden left office and Trump took over in January 2025. Now, inflation stands at 3.7%. That does not mean every price is rising at the same rate, nor does it mean that the price level itself has jumped by that amount. It means that the pace of inflation has increased. The distinction is elementary, but elementary distinctions have a way of becoming inconvenient for the Trump buffoonery squad. Trump's defenders could reasonably argue that inflation is affected by many forces, that some prices fall while others rise, and that no administration controls every fluctuation in the market. All true. But this is precisely why a President who makes wild claims about falling prices should be prepared to show his or her work. Otherwise, we are left with an administration demanding credit for the economy while treating unwelcome data as subversive threats. At the same White House Rose Garden event, Trump said that China's President Xi Jinping was at the White House a week earlier, when the visit had occurred about a month before. Does this confusion signify Trump has dementia? Add it to the list. But whether you believe or not that Trump's brain is rotting, this incident does beg a more ordinary question: why must the public so often be asked to reconcile Trump's pronouncements with the plain record of events and basic facts? | | ---|---|--- Continue reading this post for free in the Substack app | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Cliff Schecter PO Box 8384, Cincinnati, OH 45208 ? ?

| | | | | | Let me tell you about Marie Perez's record in Congress, because it won't take long.
In the last nearly four years in Congress, she has gotten exactly one bill signed into law: a bill renaming the post office in Bucoda.
One bill. A post office.
Meanwhile, families across Southwest Washington are paying more for groceries, gas, and housing, our communities are dealing with the consequences of failed policies from Olympia and Washington, D.C., and what has our congresswoman delivered? A post office naming and a reelection campaign built on attack ads.
There's a reason she's running against my character instead of running on her record: there is no record.
I've spent my career doing the work. I built a business in Chehalis that employs our neighbors, people whose kids go to school with your kids. I've served in the State Senate, where I've fought for balanced budgets, lower taxes, and the working families the political class keeps forgetting. And before all of that, I served my country in the United States Navy.
That's the contrast in this race: a career of service and results, against a congresswoman whose single accomplishment is naming a post office and whose closing argument is a false attack ad exploiting a tragedy.
We're 14 days out. Voters are already returning ballots, and every dollar we raise now goes directly to reaching them with the truth before it's too late.

We’re in the home stretch of the election.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=9652%2E582294%2EdJLhpd)
Hi, it’s Chris.
**_Can I get a few moments to reintroduce myself —[and explain why I’m asking for your $5 donation today?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261020_3.-vxVfW&refcode=em20261020-3&t=2&akid=9652%2E582294%2EdJLhpd)_**
Over 100 years ago, my great-grandfather came here from Greece and opened our family restaurant that became a beloved local spot. That’s where I learned how to work hard and show up for my community – lessons I carried with me into the State House, Congress, and now my run for Senate.
I’m running against John Sununu, the son of a political dynasty family with deep pockets. He said he’d like to “send me back to bussing tables,” as if that’s an insult.
John Sununu doesn’t know a thing about hard work.
I’m proud to be running this race the right way – no corporate PACs, just a grassroots team built by people like you, chipping in what they can, when they can.
But with just 14 days until the election, recent polls show Sununu is surging into the lead, **and this race has officially shifted to a Toss Up.**
I know what it takes to win in a swing state like New Hampshire – and we can’t flip the Senate if we don’t win this open seat.
**[That’s why I need you to stand with me today. Please chip in $5 to help my campaign win this seat and give Democrats a shot at taking back the Senate.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261020_3.-vxVfW&refcode=em20261020-3&t=3&akid=9652%2E582294%2EdJLhpd)**

body:
[ https://act.robsand.com/go/11762?t=1013&amount=25&akid=1594%2E412644%2E8hOF3M ][IMG]

Folks, we’re just 2 weeks away from Election Day, and the polls
are painfully close. This really is anyone’s race.

Between Zach Lahn’s $1M/week attack ad blitz and the fact that Iowans have
already started voting early, the stakes couldn’t be higher this week.

Bottom line? We’re running out of time to reach voters before they cast
their ballots, and I need your help to maximize our efforts over the final
couple weeks of this neck-and-neck race.

We’ve got to raise $100k before tomorrow at midnight to bolster our ads
through the home stretch, and we’re cutting things way too close. [ https://act.robsand.com/go/11762?t=1014&amount=25&akid=1594%2E412644%2E8hOF3M ]Will
you please chip in a quick grassroots donation toward our Ads Fund goal to
help get my campaign message in front of folks?

[ https://act.robsand.com/go/11762?t=1015&amount=25&akid=1594%2E412644%2E8hOF3M ]DONATE

I want to give you fair warning that this email is longer than usual, but
I do hope you’re able to spare a couple of minutes to read the whole
thing.

Election Day is just 2 weeks away, and my team and I have outlined our
game plan for the remainder of this neck-and-neck race.

But if you’re in a hurry and you don’t have time to read it all, my
feelings won’t be hurt (too badly 😂). [ https://act.robsand.com/go/11762?t=1016&amount=25&akid=1594%2E412644%2E8hOF3M ]But if you’re able to chip in a
quick grassroots donation toward our $100k Ads Fund goal, that would
really make my day.

[ https://act.robsand.com/go/11762?t=1017&amount=25&akid=1594%2E412644%2E8hOF3M ]DONATE

If you’ve made it this far — hey 👋 thanks for being here.

Right, so this is obviously oversimplifying things a bit, but in the
spirit of not emailing you an entire novel, I did my best to distill our
campaign’s plan into three BIG action items:

Everything, Everywhere, All at Once

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

The most important thing we can do to set ourselves up for success is talk
to as many people as possible, in as many places as possible.

Look, people get their news and consume media differently. While I’ve
already spoken to loads of people in person, some folks probably first
heard about my campaign on social media, while others might have learned
about it through TV, their newspaper, or the radio.

The point here is that there are still a TON of people who’ve yet to hear
from us, and others still who might not even know much about the election
or my background.

Zach Lahn is spending $1 million every week on ads to attack me and smear
my record, and it’s mission-critical that we’re able to cut through the
noise so folks hear from us, too.

Because we know that once folks hear about my vision for a better, more
equitable Iowa that puts people over politics, they’re very, very likely
to support our campaign.

That’s why even though we’ve already wrapped up my 100 Town Hall Tour,
we’re still pulling every lever we can to talk to Iowans and expand our
outreach.

Focus on the Issues that Matter

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Everywhere I go, Iowans — regardless of their political leanings — tell me
they’re sick of partisan talking points and a government that doesn’t work
for them.

They understand that partisan insiders and special interests are pulling
the strings, gaming the system, and putting politics over people — all
while pitting communities against one another.

They’re concerned about rising costs, farm foreclosures, and losing
opportunities to neighboring states as our economy continues to decline.

That’s why we’re talking about bringing jobs back to Iowa and making sure
our kids have the same opportunities we did. We’ve got a plan to bring
opportunity and innovation back to our state, and make it a place where
folks want to stay and raise a family, or start a small business.

Build the Biggest Grassroots Coalition in Iowa History

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Traveling the state, meeting with voters, having important conversations,
holding town halls and other community events... It's a lot.

But it’s 100% necessary, and it’s how we’re going to win.

Taking on the powers that be and the insiders isn’t easy, and Zach Lahn
has already gotten more than $15 million from his partisan backers at the
Republican Governors Association.

But we’ve got something they don’t: This grassroots team.

It’s growing bigger by the day as more folks hear from us, but we can’t
afford to slow down now. We need to continue growing our grassroots
network and laying the groundwork for victory, and empowering people to
have conversations about the importance of this race.

We’ve got a plan to win this thing, and I’m confident that if we can
execute on all three of these action items, we’ll be in good shape.

[ https://act.robsand.com/go/11762?t=1018&amount=20&akid=1594%2E412644%2E8hOF3M ]Our campaign coffers are running low, and this race is getting tighter
by the day, which makes replenishing our ads fund that much more
important. Can I count on you to fuel our efforts through the final weeks
of this race by chipping in
$20
toward our $100k goal today?

[ https://act.robsand.com/go/11762?t=1019&amount=20&akid=1594%2E412644%2E8hOF3M ]Donate
$20

[ https://act.robsand.com/go/11762?t=1020&amount=25&akid=1594%2E412644%2E8hOF3M ]Other Amount

I really appreciate you taking the time to read all this!

—Rob Sand

[ https://act.robsand.com/go/918?t=1001&akid=1594%2E412644%2E8hOF3M ][IMG]

Rob has built a coalition of support that crosses party lines because he
knows we can only move Iowa forward together. If you’re able to support
his campaign today you can chip in here:
[ https://act.robsand.com/go/918?t=1002&akid=1594%2E412644%2E8hOF3M ]Chip in a one-time donation
[ https://act.robsand.com/go/919?t=1003&akid=1594%2E412644%2E8hOF3M ]Chip in a weekly recurring donation!

We believe that emails are the best way for our organization to stay in
touch with supporters like you. But if you'd like to receive fewer emails,
[ https://act.robsand.com/signup/fewer_emails/?t=1004&akid=1594%2E412644%2E8hOF3M ]click here.

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

name: Dave Beckwith for Congress
subject: What the 1st Constitutional Amendment REALLY says
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Dave Beckwith For Congress_
body:
You won't see this on the ballot...
| | | | Hi Friend,
On November 3rd, Virginians will vote on a constitutional amendment that is being described as a simple protection for reproductive freedom. I read the full text. It is much broader than the ballot summary suggests, and I want you to know what is in it before you vote.
---
[](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
_Click the image to watch Dave's recent post on this.
_

**It applies to “every individual.”**
The amendment does not say adult, and it does not say woman. It says “every individual.” **That wording would include minors** , and nothing in the text mentions parents, parental notification, or parental consent.

**It bars the state from acting against anyone who helps.**
The amendment prohibits the Commonwealth from penalizing, prosecuting, or “otherwise tak[ing] adverse action against any individual for aiding or assisting” another person’s abortion, as long as that person consents. Its supporters may argue this was written for friends and family. _**I believe it could also be argued to cover an individual who helps a minor get an abortion without her parents ever knowing.**_

**It leaves the third trimester up to _one_ physician’s opinion.** In the third trimester, the state “may regulate,” but it can never prohibit an abortion that “in the professional judgment of a physician” is needed to protect “physical or mental health.” In plain language, all it takes is the opinion of one physician, with no second opinion required. It could be the same doctor who is profiting from a woman going through with the procedure. And nothing in the text sets a cutoff, so that exception can apply right up to the day of birth.
|
---
**Once language like this is in the Constitution, it is nearly impossible to change.**
Voters would have to pass another amendment, a process that takes years. Any parental rights law the legislature wrote afterward could face a constitutional challenge.
I don’t think any parent in Virginia wants our Constitution to legally create this kind of division within our families, especially when a difficult decision is involved. **If we want to protect women and girls, erasing parents from the picture is the wrong way to do it.**
I’m a dad who homeschooled my kids from kindergarten through high school. I believe it’s a parent’s right to raise their children and to be there for them through the hardest moments of their lives. A decision like this is one of those moments.
**Parents deserve to know what an amendment this broad could do to that role.**
I am voting **no** , and I am asking you to read the text yourself and consider the same. Early voting runs through October 31st, and Election Day is November 3rd.
_**Vote Dave Beckwith for Congress and Vote NO on the Amendments!**_
| | | God Bless, Dave Beckwith
