The amendment prohibits the Commonwealth from penalizing, prosecuting, or “otherwise tak[ing] adverse action against any individual for aiding or assisting” another person’s abortion, as long as that person consents. Its supporters may argue this was written for friends and family. I believe it could also be argued to cover an individual who helps a minor get an abortion without her parents ever knowing. It leaves the third trimester up to one physician’s opinion. In the third trimester, the state “may regulate,” but it can never prohibit an abortion that “in the professional judgment of a physician” is needed to protect “physical or mental health.” In plain language, all it takes is the opinion of one physician, with no second opinion required. It could be the same doctor who is profiting from a woman going through with the procedure. And nothing in the text sets a cutoff, so that exception can apply right up to the day of birth. | Once language like this is in the Constitution, it is nearly impossible to change. Voters would have to pass another amendment, a process that takes years. Any parental rights law the legislature wrote afterward could face a constitutional challenge. I don’t think any parent in Virginia wants our Constitution to legally create this kind of division within our families, especially when a difficult decision is involved. If we want to protect women and girls, erasing parents from the picture is the wrong way to do it. I’m a dad who homeschooled my kids from kindergarten through high school. I believe it’s a parent’s right to raise their children and to be there for them through the hardest moments of their lives. A decision like this is one of those moments. Parents deserve to know what an amendment this broad could do to that role. I am voting no , and I am asking you to read the text yourself and consider the same. Early voting runs through October 31st, and Election Day is November 3rd. Thank you,
John Bisognano
President
National Democratic Redistricting Committee
To: Interested Parties
From: John Bisognano, President, National Democratic Redistricting Committee (NDRC)
Date: October 2026
Subject: Democrats Stopped Trump’s Effort to Rig the 2026 Midterms
The mid-decade gerrymandering crisis that Donald Trump started has failed. It began in Texas, continued into North Carolina, Missouri, Ohio, Tennessee, Louisiana, Alabama, and Florida, and redraws were thwarted in Indiana, Kansas, Nebraska, New Hampshire, South Carolina, and Georgia. Despite all their effort to cheat the American people, Republicans will lose the House majority in the 2026 midterms.
This plot failed, not only because they underestimated the intense dissatisfaction of Americans across the country, but also because Attorney General Eric Holder’s leadership, in coordination with an aggressive, unified, multi-pronged Democratic response, played a central role in beating back Republicans’ attempt to rig the 2026 midterms, ensuring the will of the people can prevail this November.
Republicans Sought to Gain 21 New Congressional Seats from Redistricting, Instead They’ll Lose the Majority and Net Very Few Seats:
Originally, Republicans set out to draw themselves as many as 21 new seats in at least fourteen states. Instead, eight Republican states enacted new, mid-decade gerrymanders to give themselves 12 new seats—or so they hoped—and Democrats successfully responded in three states to take back seven seats. The result is that, based on redistricting, Republicans could net just five seats—and given the level of opposition they are facing from the voters, that number could go down to two or as low as zero—while wasting tens of millions of dollars and showing the American people they care more about holding onto power than the principles of our democracy.
The White House and its Republican allies wasted an incredible amount of time and resources to weaken the voting power of the American people—and it has backfired, with opposition among voters only increasing. Over the past year, they concocted legal briefs from the Department of Justice to justify stealing power, spent countless hours of White House attention and travel, including multiple trips to Indiana by the Vice President, and made an untold number of phone calls to governors and state legislators attempting to browbeat them into submission through threats, potential bribes, and other nefarious means. The result will likely be the Republican Party taking on more political baggage than an airplane carousel with few net seats and no House majority.
Overwhelming Opposition from Voters Could Overcome Republican Mid-decade Gerrymanders in the 2026 Midterms:
Republicans overplayed their hand in a number of states where they enacted egregious mid-decade gerrymanders and are unlikely to gain the number of seats they claim they will in the midterms. In fact, given strong opposition amongst voters to Republican policies, they could see very little to no gains in the following states where they enacted mid-decade gerrymanders at the direction of Donald Trump and against the will of their own constituents:
* Texas: Texas Republicans enacted a mid-decade gerrymander that relied heavily on 2024 data and claimed it would deliver five new seats. Given voting trends, Republicans overplayed their hand and will likely only net two to three seats.
* North Carolina: In the Tar Heel State, Republicans enacted a mid-decade gerrymander that aimed to dismantle NC-01, a Black opportunity district, making the 50-50 state’s congressional map an 11-3 gerrymander. However, Republicans have possibly drawn a dummymander where Democrats not only maintain NC-01, but have put the adjacent NC-03 in play.
* Ohio: Ohio Democratic state legislators successfully fended off the most extreme scenario gerrymander, with the likely result that Republicans will not gain a single new seat on the Buckeye State’s new congressional map in November.
* Alabama: When Alabama Republicans moved quickly after the Supreme Court’s disastrous Callais decision to dismantle the state’s newest Black opportunity district, AL-02, they underestimated the fire they would ignite amongst voters. Given the level of outrage among Black voters in the South, Republicans could see no gains from their new egregious racial gerrymander.
* Florida: Governor DeSantis pushed a map that aimed to net Republicans four additional congressional seats, but voter trends make it likely Republicans will net only one or two seats.

Democrats’ Multi-Pronged Strategy Played Key Role to Stop Republicans from Rigging the 2026 Midterms:
For nearly a decade, at the direction of Attorney General Holder, the National Democratic Redistricting Committee (NDRC) and its affiliates had been preparing to fight the threat of mid-decade gerrymandering in Republican states. When the potential threat became a dangerous reality, Attorney General Holder immediately galvanized support for an aggressive Democratic response. Under his leadership, NDRC and its affiliates quickly deployed a multi-pronged strategy to fight back by sounding the alarm to the public about Republicans’ attempt to rig the elections, utilizing its top-tier mapping team, coordinating with national and local partners, and empowering a growing grassroots network to get involved in the fight back. That strategy thwarted mid-decade redraws in several red states and reduced Republicans’ net seat advantage from 12 seats to a ceiling of five.
This was foundational to ensuring the will of the people could prevail on the national congressional map in November. Without this success in the redistricting fight, Republicans could have achieved their initial goal of enacting as many as 21 new seats in at least fourteen states—an amount that would have made it exceedingly difficult for the will of the people to prevail on the national congressional map. The path to success in the redistricting fight ahead of the 2026 midterms was defined by six key moments:
1. Democrats Quickly United Behind an Aggressive Response: In the days after Donald Trump publicly confirmed his push for mid-decade gerrymandering, Attorney General Holder took to the airwaves to sound the alarm about Republicans’ mid-decade gerrymandering scheme and issued a statement outlining Democrats' path forward, stating “We must preserve our democracy now in order to ultimately heal it.” Across the party’s ideological spectrum, Democratic leaders quickly united behind the principles Attorney General Holder spelled out, paving the way for a strong response from voters in California and for strong bipartisan opposition to build against mid-decade gerrymanders in red states.
2. California Voters Strongly Backed a Countermeasure: While the White House pushed a top-down approach, the opposition responded from the bottom up, with California voters passing Proposition 50 with over 60 percent of the vote. The Proposition 50 election results in California, alongside the broad bipartisan opposition to the redraws in Texas, Missouri, and elsewhere, demonstrated the incredible breadth and depth of the opposition. It also showed the rest of the country that blue states would not leave Trump’s mid-decade gerrymanders unchallenged.
3. Democrats Fended Off Most Extreme Gerrymander in Ohio: In 2025, Ohio was legally required to redraw its congressional map, and Republicans pushed for the consideration of a more extreme gerrymander—but they did not get it. The threat of overwhelming public opposition and a referendum on a legislatively-passed map in November pushed Republicans on the state’s bipartisan redistricting commission to negotiate with their Democratic counterparts. Democrats came out of those negotiations with a new map that, although far from fair, could allow all Democratic incumbents to compete for and win their districts.
4. Overwhelming Bipartisan Opposition in Red States Made Politicians Think Twice: In Indiana, Hoosiers of all stripes opposed a mid-decade gerrymander, including major in-state Republican figures like Mitch Daniels. The White House threw everything it could into pressuring Republican state legislators and the governor, including threatening federal funding for the state, sending the Vice President to travel multiple times to the state, calling legislators, and threatening primaries. Republican legislators faced threats of violence to themselves and their families. Yet, they stood up for the constituents, abandoning the effort to pass a mid-decade gerrymander. State legislators and governors in other red states—Nebraska, Kansas, New Hampshire, South Carolina, Georgia—followed suit by backing away from aggressive mid-decade gerrymanders, demonstrating the power of an engaged citizenry.
5. Utahns Won Years-Long Fight to Enforce Redistricting Reforms: For years, Utahns fought in court to enforce Proposition 4, a ballot measure enacted in 2018 that aimed to reform the state’s redistricting process and mapping parameters to ensure fairness. Leading up to the 2021 redistricting cycle, the Republican-led Utah legislature usurped the newly enacted ballot measure, replaced it with significantly watered-down reforms, and used that mechanism to enact an egregious congressional gerrymander. Utahns then took the fight to court. Finally, in 2025, Utah state courts ruled to fully reinstate Proposition 4 and strike down the state’s gerrymandered map. This resulted in a new, fairer map that allows Democrats to compete in at least one district.
6. Missourians Took the Fight to Court and the Ballot Box: After Missouri Republicans ignored overwhelming opposition from their constituents to enact an egregious mid-decade gerrymander, Missourians immediately pursued a ballot measure that would allow citizens to veto the state’s mid-decade gerrymander. State leaders did all they could to block Missourians’ ability to have the ultimate say, and Missourians took the fight to the Missouri Supreme Court, which invalidated the state’s mid-decade gerrymander and ordered the use of the 2022 congressional map in the 2026 midterms, while also allowing Missourians to have a chance to veto the state’s mid-decade gerrymander at the ballot box in November. Republicans did all they could to circumvent this clear decision, but Missourians took the fight up to the U.S. Supreme Court and won three times.

What Happens Next:
Republicans will not stop pursuing mid-decade gerrymanders; in fact, we anticipate they will immediately double down, pushing our country even further into a gerrymandering crisis in response to losing the House majority. The redistricting fight ahead of 2028 will begin on November 4th this year, with states like Georgia and Mississippi potentially using lame-duck legislative sessions to enact even more egregious gerrymanders. If Republicans’ mid-decade gerrymanders are left unchallenged and unresponded to, they could achieve a 25-seat advantage in the 2028 House elections by the middle of 2027. Any Democratic state with an ability to counter Republican gerrymanders should be prepared to do their part—quickly—to ensure the will of the American people can prevail again in the 2028 House elections.
Our goal remains the same: we want Congress to pass a federal ban on partisan gerrymandering and mid-decade redistricting as soon as possible to end this gerrymandering crisis. To get there, we must ensure the national congressional map remains responsive to the will of the American people. The immediate fight ahead will require everyone to do their part—just as the fight leading into the 2026 midterms required.
| | Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President.

This was foundational to ensuring the will of the people could prevail on the national congressional map in November. Without this success in the redistricting fight, Republicans could have achieved their initial goal of enacting as many as 21 new seats in at least fourteen states—an amount that would have made it exceedingly difficult for the will of the people to prevail on the national congressional map. The path to success in the redistricting fight ahead of the 2026 midterms was defined by six key moments: 1. Democrats Quickly United Behind an Aggressive Response: In the days after Donald Trump publicly confirmed his push for mid-decade gerrymandering, Attorney General Holder took to the airwaves to sound the alarm about Republicans’ mid-decade gerrymandering scheme and issued a statement outlining Democrats' path forward, stating “We must preserve our democracy now in order to ultimately heal it.” Across the party’s ideological spectrum, Democratic leaders quickly united behind the principles Attorney General Holder spelled out, paving the way for a strong response from voters in California and for strong bipartisan opposition to build against mid-decade gerrymanders in red states. 2. California Voters Strongly Backed a Countermeasure: While the White House pushed a top-down approach, the opposition responded from the bottom up, with California voters passing Proposition 50 with over 60 percent of the vote. The Proposition 50 election results in California, alongside the broad bipartisan opposition to the redraws in Texas, Missouri, and elsewhere, demonstrated the incredible breadth and depth of the opposition. It also showed the rest of the country that blue states would not leave Trump’s mid-decade gerrymanders unchallenged. 3. Democrats Fended Off Most Extreme Gerrymander in Ohio: In 2025, Ohio was legally required to redraw its congressional map, and Republicans pushed for the consideration of a more extreme gerrymander—but they did not get it. The threat of overwhelming public opposition and a referendum on a legislatively-passed map in November pushed Republicans on the state’s bipartisan redistricting commission to negotiate with their Democratic counterparts. Democrats came out of those negotiations with a new map that, although far from fair, could allow all Democratic incumbents to compete for and win their districts. 4. Overwhelming Bipartisan Opposition in Red States Made Politicians Think Twice: In Indiana, Hoosiers of all stripes opposed a mid-decade gerrymander, including major in-state Republican figures like Mitch Daniels. The White House threw everything it could into pressuring Republican state legislators and the governor, including threatening federal funding for the state, sending the Vice President to travel multiple times to the state, calling legislators, and threatening primaries. Republican legislators faced threats of violence to themselves and their families. Yet, they stood up for the constituents, abandoning the effort to pass a mid-decade gerrymander. State legislators and governors in other red states—Nebraska, Kansas, New Hampshire, South Carolina, Georgia—followed suit by backing away from aggressive mid-decade gerrymanders, demonstrating the power of an engaged citizenry. 5. Utahns Won Years-Long Fight to Enforce Redistricting Reforms: For years, Utahns fought in court to enforce Proposition 4, a ballot measure enacted in 2018 that aimed to reform the state’s redistricting process and mapping parameters to ensure fairness. Leading up to the 2021 redistricting cycle, the Republican-led Utah legislature usurped the newly enacted ballot measure, replaced it with significantly watered-down reforms, and used that mechanism to enact an egregious congressional gerrymander. Utahns then took the fight to court. Finally, in 2025, Utah state courts ruled to fully reinstate Proposition 4 and strike down the state’s gerrymandered map. This resulted in a new, fairer map that allows Democrats to compete in at least one district. 6. Missourians Took the Fight to Court and the Ballot Box: After Missouri Republicans ignored overwhelming opposition from their constituents to enact an egregious mid-decade gerrymander, Missourians immediately pursued a ballot measure that would allow citizens to veto the state’s mid-decade gerrymander. State leaders did all they could to block Missourians’ ability to have the ultimate say, and Missourians took the fight to the Missouri Supreme Court, which invalidated the state’s mid-decade gerrymander and ordered the use of the 2022 congressional map in the 2026 midterms, while also allowing Missourians to have a chance to veto the state’s mid-decade gerrymander at the ballot box in November. Republicans did all they could to circumvent this clear decision, but Missourians took the fight up to the U.S. Supreme Court and won three times. What Happens Next: Republicans will not stop pursuing mid-decade gerrymanders; in fact, we anticipate they will immediately double down, pushing our country even further into a gerrymandering crisis in response to losing the House majority. The redistricting fight ahead of 2028 will begin on November 4th this year, with states like Georgia and Mississippi potentially using lame-duck legislative sessions to enact even more egregious gerrymanders. If Republicans’ mid-decade gerrymanders are left unchallenged and unresponded to, they could achieve a 25-seat advantage in the 2028 House elections by the middle of 2027. Any Democratic state with an ability to counter Republican gerrymanders should be prepared to do their part—quickly—to ensure the will of the American people can prevail again in the 2028 House elections. Our goal remains the same: we want Congress to pass a federal ban on partisan gerrymandering and mid-decade redistricting as soon as possible to end this gerrymandering crisis. To get there, we must ensure the national congressional map remains responsive to the will of the American people. The immediate fight ahead will require everyone to do their part—just as the fight leading into the 2026 midterms required. | | Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President. | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|--- National Democratic Redistricting Committee 712 H St NE, #25 Washington, DC 20002 United States if you'd like to receive fewer emails from the NDRC. One of the things I’ve learned in public service is that some of the best leaders are people who were doing the work long before they ever thought about running for office.
As a pediatrician, Annie has spent her career caring for children and sitting with families through some of the hardest moments of their lives. She has also seen up close what happens when decisions made in Washington collide with the realities facing families – from the cost and availability of health care to the need for access to evidence-based care.
That experience is part of what led her to step forward. And it’s just the kind of perspective we need more of in the United States Senate.
Annie isn’t a career politician. She’s a doctor, a mom, and a public servant who understands that politics is supposed to be about making people’s lives better.

I’ve seen a lot of races. One thing that experience teaches you is to pay attention when the political ground begins to move. The momentum in South Carolina holds real potential, but Annie needs the grassroots support to match.

If you want to unsubscribe from Annie's email list please . = Hi friend, it’s Pete Buttigieg. I'm proud to endorse Dr. Annie Andrews for the United States Senate in South Carolina. Some people have written off the chance for a win in South Carolina and what that could mean for the Senate, but people doing the work on the ground there have a different story to tell. And Annie Andrews is exactly the kind of candidate who changes what's possible in a place like this. = | = One of the things I’ve learned in public service is that some of the best leaders are people who were doing the work long before they ever thought about running for office. As a pediatrician, Annie has spent her career caring for children and sitting with families through some of the hardest moments of their lives. She has also seen up close what happens when decisions made in Washington collide with the realities facing families – from the cost and availability of health care to the need for access to evidence-based care. That experience is part of what led her to step forward. And it’s just the kind of perspective we need more of in the United States Senate. Annie isn’t a career politician. She’s a doctor, a mom, and a public servant who understands that politics is supposed to be about making people’s lives better. Now, she has an extraordinary opportunity in an open Senate race – and what happens next will depend on whether her campaign has the resources to compete everywhere and make sure South Carolinians hear what she has to offer. I’ve seen a lot of races. One thing that experience teaches you is to pay attention when the political ground begins to move. clean_body: Today marks two weeks until Election Day. The clock is ticking. | Fellow Patriot, Today, we are officially two weeks out from November 3rd. It's crunch time, and we're falling behind. My opponent, Annie Andrews, has now raised over $20 million. And she's speeding up: she doubled her campaign's entire haul in just the last three months. Meanwhile, we have had to run multiple statewide campaigns in a matter of weeks. The money gap is real, and it's getting wider. Here's what I know. This race isn't decided by the size of any one check. It's decided by how many South Carolinians step up together. Will you make a "Two Week Donation" right now? Here's what your gift does with two weeks on the clock: Every dollar we raise between now and November 3rd helps rebuild our campaign after grueling Special and Runoff campaigns. It will help us run ads, mail voters, and train volunteers to get our message out on the ground here in South Carolina. The clock is not on our side, but I hope you are, Fellow Patriot. Thanks, Darline Graham P.S. Annie Andrews has raised over $20 million, and half of it came in just the last three months. My decision to email you today wasn't an easy one – but I don't want to wake up on November 4th wondering if one more email could have tipped the scales.
Because that's how close this race is.
**Experts have said our race for governor is one of the most competitive in the entire country.**
Right now, we're facing a significant budget gap – and it means we're at risk of having to pull the plug on some of our TV ads, just 14 days before the election...
**My finance team pulled the numbers, and if everyone reading this email chipped in $8 or more – we'd be able to keep our ads on air. **

Hey folks,
Donald Trump cannot stop talking about Barack Obama.
He's threatening investigations. He's ranting about Obama at rallies. He's even obsessing over his golf game. But Obama isn't staying quiet anymore, and his decision to speak out against the Trump administration's treatment of Ilhan Omar gets at something much bigger about political power, fear, and what Democrats need to do right now.
* [**00:01:13**] Barack Obama speaks out against the Trump administration's targeting of Ilhan Omar, and calls out what he sees as a fundamental abuse of government power.
* [**00:04:48**] Why Obama understands this playbook personally: Trump built his political rise in part on the racist birther conspiracy that targeted him for years.
* [**00:08:16**] The White House responds to Obama, and I explain why Trump's obsession with using government power against his perceived enemies should be taken seriously.
* [**00:10:04**] Trump is still ranting about Obama during his marathon speeches, but even his own crowds don't seem nearly as interested anymore.
* [**00:13:52**] Trump is entering lame-duck territory, and Democrats have an opportunity to build something new, not by recreating the Obama years, but by remembering what leadership can actually look like.

This isn't about nostalgia. Barack Obama isn't coming back, and Democrats need something new for the future. But there's a reason Trump remains so consumed by him. Obama is back on the campaign trail, he's speaking out, and he's reminding people what it feels like to have a president who sees the job as bigger than himself. **If you value independent media that calls out abuses of power and fights for something better, help me keep doing it.**

🚨 **Peter, Florida Democrats are showing up!** 🚨 Early voting is underway, and Day 1 in my home of Orange County was INCREDIBLE. We more than doubled Republican turnout! We won 26 out of 27 early voting sites, and the one we missed we lost by just 10 votes. Ten! [ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
No kidding, Derek:
Today, I’m asking you to pitch in one dollar to my campaign for
reelection. [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19215?t=1001&akid=689%2E245147%2EMYkngk ]Yes, really: Just $1!

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19215?t=1002&akid=689%2E245147%2EMYkngk ]Donate →

I know $1 doesn’t sound like a ton of money in a battleground state like
Pennsylvania. But take it from a guy who won by just under 3 percentage
points in his first statewide run:

Those $1 donations aren’t some extra, unnecessary luxury. They’re the
difference between winning and losing.

While the far-right blankets Pennsylvania’s airwaves with attack ads, your
$1 allows us to set the record straight.

While Donald Trump and his Mar-a-Lago allies try to spread their lies
across the Commonwealth, your $1 will help us spread the truth.

While the far-right pulls every trick in the book to defeat our campaign
and take full control of Pennsylvania, your $1 will help us take down
Donald Trump’s movement here in the most competitive battleground state in
the country.

I know $1 doesn’t sound like a lot. But for a people-powered campaign like
ours? It’s everything. So I’m humbly asking: [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19215?t=1003&akid=689%2E245147%2EMYkngk ]Will you rush $1 (or
more!) ahead of our next major fundraising deadline? We just set a goal to
bring in 300 individual donations before the end of the day — but we can’t
reach it unless our most dedicated supporters (like you!) step up and chip
in.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19215?t=1004&akid=689%2E245147%2EMYkngk ]Donate →

Appreciate your help!

Josh Shapiro

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a critical way we communicate with supporters like you.

Hi Peter,

As election day nears, James Talarico is letting his "moderate" mask slip.

When asked at a recent campaign event who his favorite drag queen was, he didn't miss a beat - instantly rattling "their" name off like he'd been asked his favorite color.

That video has gone viral online, racking up millions of views on social media.

Talarico has spent this entire campaign trying to sell Texas voters on a moderate, Bible-quoting version of himself, and videos like this are the LAST thing Talarico's campaign wants getting out to Texas voters.

Texas voters outside Austin won't buy his facade, not once they see the real Talarico instead of the campaign-trail version.

And right now in Michigan, Democrat U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is running the same playbook, holding town halls in Lansing, Grand Rapids, Detroit, Flint, and Macomb, hoping moderate suburban voters forget he wants abortion legal through all nine months.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement.

Peter, here's my problem.

You and I can't rely on the national media to tell the truth about these politicians' abortion extremism.

So it's up to grassroots folks like you and me to hold them accountable.
That's exactly what I want to do with my rapid response counter-protests at as many candidate events as possible in our targeted races.

[Will you please chip in right now to keep our rapid response team ready to move the moment we get word of the next public event](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=3ffd5a214150470aa91f24097dd65fd7&_e=4wxpww8Eg_eKKOfjt7xhJJYPtBJaGVRln294ctH5Gijd7_ahpbj2kMRz834a7pPIO6zReCWlkJrDAqBYAa71AL23e6tDJn4Bq1qNYMFVHwY9eUZkWgQ8MtuE7oa2Fowvx3OUqLzPMHLxJa26MfXyyGyqwXDz4zoHD_zkGMdSZe85y7s4AhwQ-3aoCpIWmR5pae4CTjWpchRgaQIIjOiHYat9tURSMNaNSAZPq9xs8xr2qTOhv4Q5elipRiNDmMK5Xhypa677QQ-nKNKMHaIElum7Yq3AhbQ6RHwmuqC3lFUx8N1-UIhjUZtoag6YkjBfpY1buLOW2eYdUH2KbiVfK9iRe1WgNc8Lz59YcNay3rYPmcQpES96ZKhzlAmXqLH-TTCBxJB06qXvk5YEY-plOiKWbivLg4wuzh_6-kommUc-lWApTua8PXS_6pEx_diWPD9BFox1BZT3CtFGK0ilOY-aAdFB3WHXw4v9fkJ3pzeapixdPfq4nunIjMDz18IpArObI0Gajcb8cbwt4U6DaQtw2NAeRhaYXna5j7JkAH51K3b0XStrb1JrSi439KgKThrb8y_BvdsMvq4gvESkColZAZ6L2kqwyU3pdFhIFZhZFr_3sqr11OQNKPut1-jJwOm2-vxvjTNSm65Y5aewMQ%3D%3D)**?**

Last month, our Pro-Life Generation activists launched the first stop of a 100-church flyering campaign at a church right in Talarico's back yard.

Then, when he spoke at Baylor University - a Baptist school - our team was on the ground to ensure attendees heard the truth about his anti-Biblical, pro-abortion stance.

Do you remember, back in 2024, when our students walked into a Kamala Harris rally in Wisconsin, held up a cross, and got mocked from the stage for it?

A video went viral of Kamala on stage, talking about abortion "rights" and overturning Roe v. Wade, denouncing Christians who said "Christ is King," and responding to our students with "You guys are at the wrong rally."

I've seen it time and time again.

These are exactly the moments on the campaign trail that can swing an entire election.

One month from today, on Tuesday, November 3rd, voters across the nation will decide who controls Congress for the next two years - and who has the momentum heading into the critical 2028 presidential cycle.

Talarico, El-Sayed, and all pro-abortion politicians know a camera catching them off-script is worth more than any ad buy. That's exactly why they're not publishing their schedules more than a day or two out.

So my team has to be ready before they announce, not after.

That means canvassers who can redirect on short notice and students who'll show up with signs and cameras of their own.

clean_body: Hi Peter, As election day nears, James Talarico is letting his "moderate" mask slip. When asked at a recent campaign event who his favorite drag queen was, he didn't miss a beat - instantly rattling "their" name off like he'd been asked his favorite color. That video has gone viral online, racking up millions of views on social media. Talarico has spent this entire campaign trying to sell Texas voters on a moderate, Bible-quoting version of himself, and videos like this are the LAST thing Talarico's campaign wants getting out to Texas voters. Texas voters outside Austin won't buy his facade, not once they see the real Talarico instead of the campaign-trail version. And right now in Michigan, Democrat U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is running the same playbook, holding town halls in Lansing, Grand Rapids, Detroit, Flint, and Macomb, hoping moderate suburban voters forget he wants abortion legal through all nine months. My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement. Peter, here's my problem. You and I can't rely on the national media to tell the truth about these politicians' abortion extremism. So it's up to grassroots folks like you and me to hold them accountable. That's exactly what I want to do with my rapid response counter-protests at as many candidate events as possible in our targeted races. ? Last month, our Pro-Life Generation activists launched the first stop of a 100-church flyering campaign at a church right in Talarico's back yard. Then, when he spoke at Baylor University - a Baptist school - our team was on the ground to ensure attendees heard the truth about his anti-Biblical, pro-abortion stance. Do you remember, back in 2024, when our students walked into a Kamala Harris rally in Wisconsin, held up a cross, and got mocked from the stage for it? A video went viral of Kamala on stage, talking about abortion "rights" and overturning Roe v. Wade, denouncing Christians who said "Christ is King," and responding to our students with "You guys are at the wrong rally." I've seen it time and time again. These are exactly the moments on the campaign trail that can swing an entire election. One month from today, on Tuesday, November 3rd, voters across the nation will decide who controls Congress for the next two years - and who has the momentum heading into the critical 2028 presidential cycle. Talarico, El-Sayed, and all pro-abortion politicians know a camera catching them off-script is worth more than any ad buy. That's exactly why they're not publishing their schedules more than a day or two out. So my team has to be ready before they announce, not after. That means canvassers who can redirect on short notice and students who'll show up with signs and cameras of their own. None of that comes free, and none of it waits for a fundraising deadline. ? President Trump came to Kansas yesterday -- and we're already seeing more attacks coming our way.
Last night, the president invited Roger Marshall to join him on stage -- a powerful platform he used to spread more lies about me and our grassroots movement. It's a deliberate attempt to turn the narrative against us, slow our momentum and bail out his flailing campaign.
Here's the honest truth: **Washington insiders are panicking.** They know we have what it takes to win this race. That's why a major GOP super PAC already spent $15 million against us. That's why JD Vance came to Kansas and why President Trump was here yesterday.
But here's what we didn't hear Roger Marshall talking about on that stage:
* $6 diesel squeezing Kansas farmers
* Harmful tariffs hurting small businesses
* Endless wars raising the costs of everyday goods for families
* The decision to slash SNAP benefits and Medicaid that Kansans rely on

_These are the issues on the minds of hardworking Kansans -- which Sen. Marshall would know if he ever bothered to listen._ Instead, he has been a yes-man for his party and the president, failing to do the No. 1 job of a senator: to be a champion for the people you represent.
**Now, he asked the president to swoop in to try and save his campaign -- and the visit gives a green light to outside groups to spend even more against me in this race.**
If we don't immediately respond, we risk persuadable voters being misled by our opponents at the most critical time. _Voting is already underway -- we don't have a second to waste._

body:
We won’t sugarcoat it. This could spell doom for Democrats.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001gIrBhcC-boNfQvUxWp3RpRjHhFXTfSfa6BDeSUkK5KI2i1iYfLHZed7ZZ6TnRY89-qwFvPP2wkR9Dp7kjDTUCLVAIzz_2mcRsiCrwRRUqKxShdzEFJGQW-o7UAgHBvTpDsiXK1pMOKu6haz64ZPFR8_FIOfYLO3rUEDv0Cj_H2-USadV_cUgDPpOeL7P0EZqJScB5BcpAwLCsStYZKz5n5zl4lXZX8FjrOb1hOgfklCFuEX9D2kXTw==&c=7y_TJcbjWy_h8VFNhFXt8Stx6gpBFdeg3Hnys3qiD9LE96mhFU-gKQ==&ch=5EEUCz6TX9Uj0ptJrUWTcvV56IOQ4tc0cwQ_Ufci9dtmZjs7twfy_A==)
---
|
Peter,
We have troubling news out of Michigan, where Democrats face critical elections this fall, chief among them the U.S. Senate race and the race for the state Supreme Court.
In the MI Supreme Court race, two pro-democracy justices, Megan Cavanagh and Noah Hood, are up for reelection. Both are facing competitive races against MAGA-backed challengers.
Democrats cannot afford to lose these races.
But voter turnout in traditionally Trump dominated territory has surged in the state, narrowing Democrat's projected early vote lead with only 2 weeks left until election day.
---
---
| | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001gIrBhcC-boNfQvUxWp3RpRjHhFXTfSfa6BDeSUkK5KI2i1iYfLHZed7ZZ6TnRY89-qwFvPP2wkR9Dp7kjDTUCLVAIzz_2mcRsiCrwRRUqKxShdzEFJGQW-o7UAgHBvTpDsiXK1pMOKu6haz64ZPFR8_FIOfYLO3rUEDv0Cj_H2-USadV_cUgDPpOeL7P0EZqJScB5BcpAwLCsStYZKz5n5zl4lXZX8FjUM2_kEhO3pmaXxkEWVLbaw==&c=7y_TJcbjWy_h8VFNhFXt8Stx6gpBFdeg3Hnys3qiD9LE96mhFU-gKQ==&ch=5EEUCz6TX9Uj0ptJrUWTcvV56IOQ4tc0cwQ_Ufci9dtmZjs7twfy_A==)
---
We won't sugarcoat it. This could spell doom for Democrats.
Just last week, Defend Our Courts began contacting thousands of Democratic voters in Michigan. And the conversations we've been having with voters have also been concerning.
While many of the voters we reached are fired up about voting for Dems, a lot of them do not know who the Dem endorsed Supreme Court candidates are, or that a Supreme Court election is even happening.
That's terrible news. Michigan's Supreme Court elections are nonpartisan. There will be no party affiliation listed next to the names on the ballot. If voters don't know who to vote for, they could inadvertently vote for MAGA's candidates.
All of this is creating a perfect storm that could capsize the Dem's blue wave in November. At a time when Dem voter turnout in Michigan needs to increase substantially to stave off MAGA's surge, these voters don't know who to vote for.
This is the exact scenario that cost Democrats in Georgia's nonpartisan Supreme Court races earlier this year. A last-minute surge in turnout produced an electorate that leaned Democratic by eight points. Yet the Democrat-backed candidates still lost, because too many Dems voted for the wrong candidates.
We can't let that happen in Michigan. Right now, our team has identified over 400,000 Democrats we need to contact between now and election day. We've reached less than a quarter of them so far.

Peter, In 2024, Elon Musk spent more money in NY-17 than in any other Congressional district. Billionaires and special interest groups were able to drag Mike Lawler across the finish line, even while Kamala won. So when I saw this headline, my alarm bells went off. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqiBIysd_1t7dQL51NYrcynj_UHKTnEbFJuXRbcU0RusMeK8Uw0hMFlhZHdKfCOjwCtsJFJuffBzcUvFl70wDDeChN1Iq8H4V69jkzTP_B7wsErrzGRB2IoPP4vVry9KqCwTKywZ2vFWT66xCyIC_HmX0wrbsvJhNJ8bfO3hu6czNtVgyVRcKwsYzNkimiPk17zSwDz7vtoamhVgW0xnw1xcCpGM8jD-DqjsOVuYGbpcbiliXig9bgCvNNblLBIo8LOQoETx6i65QG7igqLBQnAe4JELfnt_wAyXdGEYQRdA/4v1/cMqX5ptrQnSP0ja41PSbeA/h1/h001.cuhCLDhaG2JU4DxclMxEr9uhbLZvXqtP0S10LWBVeyQ) **The richest man in the world has spent a quarter of a billion dollars trying to buy our democracy—and a huge chunk of that money is being spent right here in NY-17.** Polling shows we have a path to victory, even in the face of all that spending. But we are in the fight of our lives. The fact that people like Musk are able to just drop this type of cash into our elections is a loss for anyone who cares about making sure everyday Americans have a voice in government. # **You're invited!**
---
---
I know this isn't exactly my normal newsletter, but I wanted to take a minute to invite you all to an Oregon Conservative Caucus event that you won't want to miss. Attorney Ray Hacke will update us on all the civil rights case victories his group has won in Oregon and nationally. There are far more than you realize. Brad Dacus, founder of the Pacific Justice Institute will follow as our keynote with a faith-based message on political activism that is incredibly inspiring to those of us in a blue state.

# The book is out!
---
---
On July 4 to celebrate America's 250th birthday, Solomon and I released his new book, COUNTERSCRIPT.
“... riveting, heartwarming, and most of all—inspiring. America is strong because it welcomes those who know the enduring value of freedom.”
—Gordon G. Chang, Political Analyst

“... a blend of two great missions—love of all that makes America great and a warrior’s charge to defeat the evil he escaped.”
—Steve Yates, White House Deputy National Security Advisor (2001-2005)

“Solomon is a good friend of mine and of _freedom_. What he writes is important and true. Please read this and _hear _it.”
—Tommy Hicks, Former RNC Co-Chair; National Finance Co-Chair of Donald J. Trump for President, Inc.

"Gripping, deeply personal ... this book is impossible to ignore and difficult to put down.”

I'm NOT looking for some gargantuan check from a millionaire, just a small ask of my most loyal grassroots patriots...

Fellow American, it's Michele.

And just like that, in the blink of an eye, the Election is almost HERE.I've got to speak candidly for a moment because it feels like we've been moving a million miles a minute just to keep up.

We've been on the ground meeting with voters everywhere, from door-knocking day trips to meet-and-greets to phone calls around the clock with donors and more.

When my head hits the pillow at night, I'm EXHAUSTED, but YOU keep me going day after day.If it wasn't for people like you who keep motivating me to keep pushing on, and graciously support this movement by any means necessary, we would've been lost in the dust LONG ago.

But we're right in the thick of it.
With only days until the Election, we're trying to find ways to pull ahead of my radical opponent before the buzzer and set ourselves up for the best chance at success when voters go to the polls.

That's why I'm reaching out to you today with ONE final ask of my most loyal patriots.

[Just $15.](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=270dcc9bad0f4d08bc734b6d13f150b4&_e=oUf9VwrMl5jghw-aJGGNda9RZyLJmeR-Vig98J8aFBG-m6vFLpctrPxWyd_d08Rvrx9WYnDLSt6sTha40po7xNTcUeBu9WqKbQn5Iv0Iz2XpNkYKwRfsNBwWNJLNcFZ0B9ux9Tflo0NA0MEj3v3AZSSjsyJlMqXzEuOVUiLA_ohnvCb4JaOC0xdUvHMloeuMRRr8vdo8wt07S4Hr0kPhIPP5fYdXhPhip7Rl4DZF7cRmOGkl2KRdbuEHt_qo3d4vro0nAU4KN894VgS__Dq36BYjZgqF2BTJKsl7LiaqnoK3sklEz6LhPHH7Q4M8ovmJ2QZiBora3rt3yBcT0gNqW-m8klydAKOWOIUs8onfb75M_vlvrcLWbcLrqWiYPxD5cBTl_9yDgNTVjXWlWjIli_G1ZRNVE38_s3ks2iYzMDvqpSoND25fQcL65ykx_QQy4UslYyKC7b0zdXJlW65tGGjxaaXOfaEc091ySuaxAeVEhEcYDwB1h2OYyPE-aeXOTZx1nDKWHg_NTeX6sYbch4oAbWPuj6qvO4vbX1JmmEI0Y61_o2jgqLUmXYrTxjquYr_K94YUPEPz3tH6LCs19OC8dy_BSn5fiEUoIaN-ESBWAWGQFOA3Q1n6jYlOrPHDF9PiHFufglh6LpLQqJFRHKF5VkiuMDSlM9li1qiK9iy_yy1ymdSwd6k6Ebm5AHhfoPrOiemOFXYydJpbOJ-JaoHkcgfoJ9XRMNLbQVY1CRWVSU03flZPaxz4UEFoMeOT0YsSbvbju_gnG31iiKd75WZLEAiF6K4z4GP6slvfufQvHPy12giNt6qy70UpsxfzuHMyloSuJP5hYKQ4Zj9k8ORBZ2tHtiRjVB9dyBPnhCy-WeMJvYpX0KmkxxodnQCQiJKgSHsc6zhQR-vtu69yYDrvw4oTsBphkpFidGRialzbiHsR8Kt2ellj0-C733L6)

Rear Admiral Nancy Lacore served our nation for 35 years in the Navy. She started as a helicopter pilot and rose to a three-star admiral and the chief of the Navy Reserve, where she led more than 60,000 sailors around the globe before Pete Hegseth fired her without cause in 2025.
Now, Nancy is stepping up to serve again — this time at home. She’s running for SC-01 against Republican Jenny Costa Honeycutt.
At the start of this cycle, race raters didn’t think Democrats stood a chance to take back this seat. But Nancy’s experience and message have deeply connected with voters, and now this race is a toss up. The polls are tightening and Nancy has a real shot to take back this critical seat and help Democrats flip the U.S. House.
Dr. Annie Andrews is running for the Senate against Republican Darline Graham, who was handpicked by Donald Trump to finish the remainder of her brother’s term.
For two decades, Annie has been on the front lines of the healthcare system as a pediatrician, watching how Washington’s political decisions land in hospital rooms across South Carolina. She knows that if Darline Graham wins, Republicans will continue to threaten Medicaid, cut food assistance, and hand out tax breaks to billionaires while families struggle to afford food and medicine. And she knows what the human consequences of those decisions look like when they land in the emergency room.
This is our best opportunity yet to flip seats in South Carolina and take back Congress. That’s why EMILYs List is all in for Nancy and Annie — and why we need this team with us to get it done.

clean_body: South Carolina is turning up the heat in 2026 | = Peter, South Carolina is one of the hottest states on our 2026 map — with two critical races that could help decide control of Congress. Nancy Lacore is running to FLIP South Carolina’s 1st Congressional District, and Dr. Annie Andrews is taking on Darline Graham in South Carolina’s U.S. Senate race. The state of these races make one thing clear: South Carolina is in play, and these women could help Democrats take back control of Congress. = | = Rear Admiral Nancy Lacore served our nation for 35 years in the Navy. She started as a helicopter pilot and rose to a three-star admiral and the chief of the Navy Reserve, where she led more than 60,000 sailors around the globe before Pete Hegseth fired her without cause in 2025. Now, Nancy is stepping up to serve again — this time at home. She’s running for SC-01 against Republican Jenny Costa Honeycutt. At the start of this cycle, race raters didn’t think Democrats stood a chance to take back this seat. But Nancy’s experience and message have deeply connected with voters, and now this race is a toss up. The polls are tightening and Nancy has a real shot to take back this critical seat and help Democrats flip the U.S. House. Dr. Annie Andrews is running for the Senate against Republican Darline Graham, who was handpicked by Donald Trump to finish the remainder of her brother’s term. For two decades, Annie has been on the front lines of the healthcare system as a pediatrician, watching how Washington’s political decisions land in hospital rooms across South Carolina. She knows that if Darline Graham wins, Republicans will continue to threaten Medicaid, cut food assistance, and hand out tax breaks to billionaires while families struggle to afford food and medicine. And she knows what the human consequences of those decisions look like when they land in the emergency room. This is our best opportunity yet to flip seats in South Carolina and take back Congress. | | | | Peter, Is there _anything_ we can say to convince you to chip in today to help us topple anti-public lands politicians this November? **What if we told you** that the administration gutted Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante by over 90%—wiping out protections for nearly three million acres of pristine backcountry so mining executives could immediately stake uranium claims? **What if we told you** that the Chief of the U.S. Forest Service is a former timber lobbyist who is now moving to repeal the 25-year-old Roadless Rule, opening up 45 million acres of untouched national forests to corporate clear-cutting? **And what if we told you** that in Minnesota, politicians like Pete Stauber are trying to hand the Boundary Waters over to a toxic sulfide-ore mining company owned by a Chilean billionaire who provides a luxury rental home to the President’s daughter? They are coming at our public lands from every direction at once, betting that the American people are too exhausted to notice and too divided to fight back. They think their billionaire extraction donors have bought them complete immunity. The single best answer to that arrogance is a surgical, inescapable digital ad blitz right in their home districts—putting their dirty voting records in front of every hunter, angler, hiker, and voter before they cast a ballot. They are coming at our public lands from every direction at once, betting that the American people are too exhausted to notice and too divided to fight back. | Election Day is November 3rd, Virginia's future is on the line.
John McGuire proudly voted to condemn socialism in all its forms.
Socialism is not just the government providing services. It is the seizure of private property, state control of the means of production, and the systematic destruction of incentives.
Venezuela was once one of the wealthiest countries in the Western Hemisphere. Under socialism it collapsed: the productive fled, hyperinflation and shortages followed, and ordinary people were reduced to scavenging trash or turning to prostitution simply to survive. Socialism has never worked.
When the Berlin Wall fell, people ran to the freedom side. Combined with Marxism, socialism produced the deaths of tens of millions in the 20th century. In practice it means bigger, more intrusive government; open borders; weakened law enforcement and military; stifled innovation; and widespread poverty.
I'm sure most agree: if Kamala Harris had been president, her radical policies would have left American cities looking like Paris, burning streets, lawlessness, and disorder. That is not the America we want. Socialism has no place in Virginia or in our country.
As Margaret Thatcher said: "The problem with socialism is that you eventually run out of other people's money."

Vote to re-elect John McGuire
Vote for Bert Mizusawa for U.S. Senate - Virginia.
Vote NO on all three constitutional amendments.

**Patriot, it’s John James. **
We're less than 3 weeks away from Election Day. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. _I promise I will not waste your time._
I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted.
I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, _**I would live it.**_

Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army.
During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. **Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. **
**I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and _I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud._**

After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, **_I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. _**
I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician...

clean_body: Will you have my back on November 3rd?| | | | | Patriot, it’s John James. We're less than 3 weeks away from Election Day. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. I promise I will not waste your time. I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted. I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, I would live it. Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army. During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud. After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician... I saw the Democrats destroying our country, and I knew my service to this great nation wasn’t over yet. Everybody told me running for office isn’t easy, but my heart was telling me it was the right thing to do. I won my election, with the help of President Trump, and started delivering results for my new constituents. Then, in 2023, when the Establishment tried to move on from Trump and being MAGA was seen as risky or politically inconvenient, I was among the first in Michigan to endorse President Trump for 2024. Loyalty isn’t a talking point to me; it’s the only way I know how to operate. My dedication to this country, my loyalty towards my constituents, and my desire to see the greatest nation on earth excel are part of the reasons why I’m now emailing you, but they’re not my #1 reason why... These three kids are the reason why I’m sending this message to you, as a TRUMP-ENDORSED Republican and father running to be the next governor of Michigan Having my own family taught me more lessons than I could list, and it was the one thing being in the U.S. Army didn’t prepare me for. But it also awoke in me a desire to do EVERYTHING and ANYTHING I can to ensure my kids have bright futures. My family means everything to me, and Michigan is our home; that’s why I will fight like my life depends on it to save this state and win this November. I’m under no illusions; I know this election will be one of the toughest challenges I’ve faced in my entire life, but after everything I’ve done in my service, it’s nothing I can’t handle. Unfortunately, the one thing I can’t directly control is spending, and the Democrats will do everything in their power to stop my campaign from making it to the ballot box this November. Nothing can stop us from saving this country if we stand together. Today, I’m asking you to make a small-dollar gift of $10, $25, $50 or ANYTHING you can spare to fuel my campaign’s fight as we approach our upcoming November 3rd election. Thank you for taking the time to read my message. I hope to hear from you in the days to come. Here's the short version. When Donald was two and a half, my grandmother was hospitalized and unavailable to her children for almost a year. **More than 60% of the money Michael raised last quarter came from political action committees.** It didn’t come from folks in Superior or Wausau or Rice Lake. It came from PACs from all over the country.

Here’s a sample of who’s writing the checks to Michael Alfonso:

**Koch Industries’ PAC: $5,000** , the most a PAC can legally give per election. **Boeing’s PAC: another $5,000**. **The American Bankers Association. The trucking industry’s PAC. Jim Jordan’s campaign committee.** Tom Emmer’s campaign and his leadership PAC.

You can see the tracks of all that PAC money here - bankers, airlines, trucking companies, and dozens of PACs with obscure names that only the insiders know about.

This is how Washington works. Insiders move money to each other through committees most voters have never heard of, and the person on the receiving end owes them a phone call.

**Northern Wisconsin deserves a congressman who answers to the people who live here.**

I made a different choice. I’ve refused corporate PAC money from day one. More than 98% of our support has come from Wisconsin residents. That’s the campaign I’m proud to run, and it’s the only way I know how to do this.

**[I won’t pretend it’s an even fight. Michael Alfonso's Washington friends are going to keep the money flowing right up to November 3rd. **I. The school with four names**
In 1926 the Communist International opened a training school in Moscow so secretive that, a century on, nobody can settle on its name. The Comintern's own files say International Lenin School. The memoirs say university, academy, institute, college -- the full vocabulary of respectability applied to an institution whose students crossed borders on forged papers, under names that weren't theirs. The naming wasn't confusion. It was cover.
The school ran from May 1926 until mid-1938, first under the Marxist theorist Nikolai Bukharin, and by the standard count trained some 3,500 communists from 59 countries. Europe and North America supplied most of them; students from the colonial world were routed to a sister institution, the Communist University of the Toilers of the East. What the ILS taught was not, in the main, book communism. The curriculum ran from dialectical materialism and political economy to party history and "party technique" -- the unglamorous tradecraft of cells, propaganda presses and false identities. Students lived in national sections, learned Russian, and studied the very parties they were expected to lead home.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/163f5810-74d6-4eeb-94c2-5844b2bc105a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Minutes of the Second Congress of the Communist International
By that measure -- alumni -- the school was the most successful educational experiment of the century. Ana Pauker of Romania became one of the first women in the world to hold a foreign ministry. Walter Ulbricht went from its lecture halls to building the German Democratic Republic, which he then ran for sixteen years. Luis Carlos Prestes led Brazil's Communist Party through decades of prison and exile. Pak Hon-yong led Korea's communists; Teng Daiyuan became a general of China's Red Army. When the Great Purge finally closed the school in 1938, it swallowed some of its own teachers and students along the way. The lesson was already written: an idea with a school behind it outlives the men who taught it.
**II. The fifties: the method survives the school**
Stalin died in 1953. In February 1956 Khrushchev read his secret speech, and by November Soviet tanks were in Budapest. The Comintern's monopoly on the communist imagination died that year too: Palmiro Togliatti, chief of the Italian party, produced his "Yalta memorandum" arguing for "polycentrism" -- communism would no longer march in step. Yet the school itself was not abandoned; other Lenin Schools were established after Stalin's death. The fifties confirmed what the purge had taught: you can close a school, but you cannot close the *idea* of the school -- the conviction that revolutions are not merely made but manufactured, in classrooms, out of selected people.
**III. Eurocommunism: the heresy of the grandchildren**
By the 1970s the grandchildren of those Moscow students ran the great Western parties, and they renounced the landlord. Eurocommunism -- the name usually credited to the Yugoslav journalist Frane Barbieri -- named their claim, as the parties put it, that they had developed a theory and practice of social transformation more relevant for Western Europe: pluralism accepted, Moscow distanced, revolution by ballot box.
The high-water marks came fast. On a visit to Washington in June 1976, Enrico Berlinguer declared Italy's NATO membership secure even as his party headed toward its best result ever -- 34.4 percent of the Italian vote, the largest communist party in the West. Santiago Carrillo published *Eurocommunism and the State* in 1977, the year Spain's Communist Party was finally legalized after four decades underground; the French party signed on, then watched its 1978 campaign collapse. Berlinguer's "historic compromise" with Italy's Christian Democrats died with Aldo Moro in 1978, murdered by the Red Brigades. Carrillo was pushed out in 1982 and expelled in 1985. The term itself was dead by the mid-1980s, and in 1991 the Italian party -- the great hope of the tendency -- dissolved into something that no longer called itself communist.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b0f228ef-2fd6-4403-bb12-a02f52c1de2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
# Enrico Berlinguer, the leader of the PCI (Partito Comunista Italiano/Italian Communist Party)
Scorecard. As a strategy for power: a total failure -- no Eurocommunist party ever governed a Western European state. As a theory: a success that outlived its authors. It normalized a communism of the ballot, moved the movement's ambition from seizing the state to staffing it, and left its vocabulary in every subsequent European left. And staffing is a question of training. Which brings us, of all places, to Chicago.
**IV. The Chicago question**
Here is the claim: that Barack Obama, Fiona Hill and Abdul El-Sayed are linked through the University of Chicago -- through its "Pritzker Fellows" and its "Obama Foundation Scholars Program," housed across the Booth School of Business, the Crown Family School of Social Work, Policy, and Practice, and the Harris School of Public Policy -- and that this apparatus is, functionally, a Lenin School for the age of foundations.
The institutions are real. The University of Chicago's Institute of Politics, founded in 2013, has hosted hundreds of Pritzker Fellows -- the Institute's own roster runs from Jennifer Granholm and Antony Blinken to Beto O'Rourke, Michael Steele and New Hampshire's Kelly Ayotte, and includes, strikingly, Vladimir Kara-Murza, the Russian oppositionist the Kremlin poisoned twice. El-Sayed is on its rolls; Hill appears on the Institute's former-fellows page. The Obama Foundation Scholars Program at UChicago was announced in February 2018: a Master of Arts in International Development and Policy, run jointly with Booth, Crown and Harris under director Adrian Talbott, drawing a global cohort -- eighteen students in 2025-26\. (A parallel program at Columbia just concluded.) Obama himself taught constitutional law at the university for a dozen years, 1992 to 2004 -- a teacher, not a trainee -- and in June 2026 the Obama Presidential Center opened in Jackson Park, a mile east of the gothic quadrangles.
So the pipeline exists, exactly as advertised: promising young people, largely from elsewhere, brought to the South Side for a year of formation, funding and networks, then returned to run things. The claim fails, though, on the two words that matter: *furthering communism*.
If any American university furthered communism in the second half of the twentieth century, Chicago's fingerprints are in the opposite file. Milton Friedman built the monetarist counterrevolution there; Friedrich Hayek settled into the Committee on Social Thought in 1950; the "Chicago Boys" -- Chilean economists brought to Hyde Park under an exchange with the Catholic University of Chile -- went home to run Augusto Pinochet's economy from 1975. The most effective anti-communist revolution of the age was administered, in its economic chapter, from the same campus now accused of running a communist one.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2c9e796e-8bf0-4919-a0f0-94cc5d62c804?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
# Obama Presidential Center opens, offering an art-filled, hopeful view of US history
And the three names? Hill is a coal miner's daughter from Bishop Auckland who took a Harvard doctorate in Soviet history, spent her career studying the very system the Lenin School served, served a Republican president as his Russia director, and testified against him under oath. El-Sayed -- Rhodes Scholar, Oxford PhD, Columbia-trained physician, Detroit's health director, now running for Senate in Michigan -- is a product of nearly every elite formation pipeline in the West, and of the Comintern's pedagogy he is not. And Obama, the community organizer from the South Side, is best understood not as a student of the old school but as its great imitator in form: he built a pipeline.
**V. The scorecard, 1950s to today**
The Lenin School succeeded enormously and failed completely: its alumni built the states that fell between 1989 and 1991, while the method -- identify promising twenty-year-olds, fund their formation, install them in the machinery -- outlived every one of those states. Eurocommunism rebranded revolution into administration and lost both the revolution and the administration. The pipeline is the durable technology, and it is now bipartisan: the same Institute that hosts the Obama Foundation's scholars hosts Pritzker Fellows drawn from Republican administrations and from the ranks of Kremlin-poisoned dissidents.
The question beneath all of it is the one this newsletter keeps returning to: who decided? The Lenin School decided, in a building in Moscow, whose twenties would be spent learning revolution. Foundations decide now, in glass buildings on the lakefront, and their decisions are public if anyone cares to read the class lists. The difference between the Comintern and the twenty-first century isn't the pipeline. It's whether you can see the syllabus. The Lenin School, at least, had the decency to hide.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/62effedf-0048-4d03-abda-dc9192337121?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

clean_body: From the Lenin School to Obama's Chicago | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? From the Lenin School to Obama's Chicago | | | Oct 20 | | | | | | | | | | | | I. The school with four names In 1926 the Communist International opened a training school in Moscow so secretive that, a century on, nobody can settle on its name. The Comintern's own files say International Lenin School. The memoirs say university, academy, institute, college -- the full vocabulary of respectability applied to an institution whose students crossed borders on forged papers, under names that weren't theirs. The naming wasn't confusion. It was cover. The school ran from May 1926 until mid-1938, first under the Marxist theorist Nikolai Bukharin, and by the standard count trained some 3,500 communists from 59 countries. Europe and North America supplied most of them; students from the colonial world were routed to a sister institution, the Communist University of the Toilers of the East. What the ILS taught was not, in the main, book communism. The curriculum ran from dialectical materialism and political economy to party history and "party technique" -- the unglamorous tradecraft of cells, propaganda presses and false identities. Students lived in national sections, learned Russian, and studied the very parties they were expected to lead home. | | ---|---|--- Minutes of the Second Congress of the Communist International By that measure -- alumni -- the school was the most successful educational experiment of the century. Ana Pauker of Romania became one of the first women in the world to hold a foreign ministry. Walter Ulbricht went from its lecture halls to building the German Democratic Republic, which he then ran for sixteen years. Luis Carlos Prestes led Brazil's Communist Party through decades of prison and exile. Pak Hon-yong led Korea's communists; Teng Daiyuan became a general of China's Red Army. When the Great Purge finally closed the school in 1938, it swallowed some of its own teachers and students along the way. The lesson was already written: an idea with a school behind it outlives the men who taught it. II. The fifties: the method survives the school Stalin died in 1953. In February 1956 Khrushchev read his secret speech, and by November Soviet tanks were in Budapest. The Comintern's monopoly on the communist imagination died that year too: Palmiro Togliatti, chief of the Italian party, produced his "Yalta memorandum" arguing for "polycentrism" -- communism would no longer march in step. Yet the school itself was not abandoned; other Lenin Schools were established after Stalin's death. The fifties confirmed what the purge had taught: you can close a school, but you cannot close the idea of the school -- the conviction that revolutions are not merely made but manufactured, in classrooms, out of selected people. III. Eurocommunism: the heresy of the grandchildren By the 1970s the grandchildren of those Moscow students ran the great Western parties, and they renounced the landlord. Eurocommunism -- the name usually credited to the Yugoslav journalist Frane Barbieri -- named their claim, as the parties put it, that they had developed a theory and practice of social transformation more relevant for Western Europe: pluralism accepted, Moscow distanced, revolution by ballot box. The high-water marks came fast. On a visit to Washington in June 1976, Enrico Berlinguer declared Italy's NATO membership secure even as his party headed toward its best result ever -- 34.4 percent of the Italian vote, the largest communist party in the West. Santiago Carrillo published Eurocommunism and the State in 1977, the year Spain's Communist Party was finally legalized after four decades underground; the French party signed on, then watched its 1978 campaign collapse. Berlinguer's "historic compromise" with Italy's Christian Democrats died with Aldo Moro in 1978, murdered by the Red Brigades. Carrillo was pushed out in 1982 and expelled in 1985. The term itself was dead by the mid-1980s, and in 1991 the Italian party -- the great hope of the tendency -- dissolved into something that no longer called itself communist. | | ---|---|--- Enrico Berlinguer, the leader of the PCI (Partito Comunista Italiano/Italian Communist Party) Scorecard. As a strategy for power: a total failure -- no Eurocommunist party ever governed a Western European state. As a theory: a success that outlived its authors. It normalized a communism of the ballot, moved the movement's ambition from seizing the state to staffing it, and left its vocabulary in every subsequent European left. And staffing is a question of training. Which brings us, of all places, to Chicago. IV. The Chicago question Here is the claim: that Barack Obama, Fiona Hill and Abdul El-Sayed are linked through the University of Chicago -- through its "Pritzker Fellows" and its "Obama Foundation Scholars Program," housed across the Booth School of Business, the Crown Family School of Social Work, Policy, and Practice, and the Harris School of Public Policy -- and that this apparatus is, functionally, a Lenin School for the age of foundations. The institutions are real. The University of Chicago's Institute of Politics, founded in 2013, has hosted hundreds of Pritzker Fellows -- the Institute's own roster runs from Jennifer Granholm and Antony Blinken to Beto O'Rourke, Michael Steele and New Hampshire's Kelly Ayotte, and includes, strikingly, Vladimir Kara-Murza, the Russian oppositionist the Kremlin poisoned twice. El-Sayed is on its rolls; Hill appears on the Institute's former-fellows page. The Obama Foundation Scholars Program at UChicago was announced in February 2018: a Master of Arts in International Development and Policy, run jointly with Booth, Crown and Harris under director Adrian Talbott, drawing a global cohort -- eighteen students in 2025-26\. (A parallel program at Columbia just concluded.) Obama himself taught constitutional law at the university for a dozen years, 1992 to 2004 -- a teacher, not a trainee -- and in June 2026 the Obama Presidential Center opened in Jackson Park, a mile east of the gothic quadrangles. So the pipeline exists, exactly as advertised: promising young people, largely from elsewhere, brought to the South Side for a year of formation, funding and networks, then returned to run things. The claim fails, though, on the two words that matter: furthering communism. If any American university furthered communism in the second half of the twentieth century, Chicago's fingerprints are in the opposite file. Milton Friedman built the monetarist counterrevolution there; Friedrich Hayek settled into the Committee on Social Thought in 1950; the "Chicago Boys" -- Chilean economists brought to Hyde Park under an exchange with the Catholic University of Chile -- went home to run Augusto Pinochet's economy from 1975. The most effective anti-communist revolution of the age was administered, in its economic chapter, from the same campus now accused of running a communist one. | | ---|---|--- Obama Presidential Center opens, offering an art-filled, hopeful view of US history And the three names? Hill is a coal miner's daughter from Bishop Auckland who took a Harvard doctorate in Soviet history, spent her career studying the very system the Lenin School served, served a Republican president as his Russia director, and testified against him under oath. El-Sayed -- Rhodes Scholar, Oxford PhD, Columbia-trained physician, Detroit's health director, now running for Senate in Michigan -- is a product of nearly every elite formation pipeline in the West, and of the Comintern's pedagogy he is not. And Obama, the community organizer from the South Side, is best understood not as a student of the old school but as its great imitator in form: he built a pipeline. V. The scorecard, 1950s to today The Lenin School succeeded enormously and failed completely: its alumni built the states that fell between 1989 and 1991, while the method -- identify promising twenty-year-olds, fund their formation, install them in the machinery -- outlived every one of those states. Eurocommunism rebranded revolution into administration and lost both the revolution and the administration. The pipeline is the durable technology, and it is now bipartisan: the same Institute that hosts the Obama Foundation's scholars hosts Pritzker Fellows drawn from Republican administrations and from the ranks of Kremlin-poisoned dissidents. The question beneath all of it is the one this newsletter keeps returning to: who decided? The Lenin School decided, in a building in Moscow, whose twenties would be spent learning revolution. Foundations decide now, in glass buildings on the lakefront, and their decisions are public if anyone cares to read the class lists. The difference between the Comintern and the twenty-first century isn't the pipeline. It's whether you can see the syllabus. The Lenin School, at least, had the decency to hide. | | ---|---|--- Invite your friends and earn rewards If you enjoy Heartland Journal ®, share it with your friends and earn rewards when they subscribe. | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Heartland Journal 99 E. Peter,
A year ago, we built the **Defending Our Neighbors Fund** to close a dangerous gap in our immigration system: people facing deportation without a lawyer by their side. We’ve been rushing resources to trusted organizations that provide legal representation and bond support ever since.
_Neighbors like you have helped raise more than**$15 million** and fund **56 grants** to frontline organizations._ 🙌🏾
When a loved one is detained, legal support becomes a family’s most urgent need. Access to a lawyer can be the difference between a family staying together or being separated indefinitely.
More than 425,000 children with pending removal cases have no lawyer.1 Up to 67% of all people facing deportation must defend themselves in court without counsel.2
ACLU Executive Director Anthony D. Romero, our partner in the Defending Our Neighbors Fund, put it like this: _“We’ve heard too many harrowing stories of children—some as young as 2 years old—being forced to face deportation hearings with nobody by their side.”_
He’s right. This should never happen. That's where neighbors like you come in, Peter.
Lawyers in courtrooms. Bonds paid. Families back together.
But the work is far from finished. Immigration arrests have more than quadrupled over the past year,3 and new barriers to safety and stability for our immigrant neighbors are emerging every day.
This is neighbors helping neighbors. It’s what we, the people, do best.
**[Donate $10, $25, or more to the Defending Our Neighbors Fund today to make sure no one faces this system alone.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.yjJN_MEbNx94PLaWzZ6hWzadU9N9RNMkN_aPwx_gUWMyhrdkC01LWf7qDIV-X_SfNT1mpyRhipiKDWZuKh9G2xnm3a8Q_ZTLc3CbCqOIqOM9suTNZ7kdKsLzK9jMMBkVTCpujjMQaGEatVTdGHA7NZItVjgS4G06Pr0IaqPAimxwxfiyJmT3agdOYVzD0rfagxmm8O1UsFsizON5y3bxDGqKpZ-TUo4j7z3uJYUc8edMNfEbi3YwWqWGShs_ziaSY6WHC9NnTiAEKfQm4XwX8pTDkPUrKlObur_gVjEtCU0CI5GWqZc8wtwMnqlH-d6sxY9vhUtA7lvAY99f7CmA_yX1-9284726eeBazf1ySBTNr95s9UPxDtg2czSRT2XRiZXeVOKp1S-QON-6L2uLg5qDpjZwIYSeb1imjGskQNk/4v1/vdquFPLaTAKtlOkOPCcHhQ/h2/h001.IrQO4jc0Xv0KGMDaajfksAOWRzuKBnsljVXPf8P80tk)**

Access to a lawyer can be the difference between a family staying together or being separated indefinitely. More than 425,000 children with pending removal cases have no lawyer.1 Up to 67% of all people facing deportation must defend themselves in court without counsel.2 ACLU Executive Director Anthony D. Romero, our partner in the Defending Our Neighbors Fund, put it like this: “We’ve heard too many harrowing stories of children—some as young as 2 years old—being forced to face deportation hearings with nobody by their side.” He’s right. This should never happen. That's where neighbors like you come in, Peter. Lawyers in courtrooms. Bonds paid. Families back together. But the work is far from finished. Immigration arrests have more than quadrupled over the past year,3 and new barriers to safety and stability for our immigrant neighbors are emerging every day. This is neighbors helping neighbors. It’s what we, the people, do best. | Year one proved what’s possible when we come together. Year two starts with you. — Greisa, United We Dream * 1. "Over 425,000 Kids in U.S. Face Deportation Hearings Without Lawyers." Drop Site News. June 26, 2026. 2. "Immigration Court Legal Representation Dashboard." Vera Institute. 3. “Immigration Enforcement: First Year.” Deportation Data Project. Follow us on: | | | | |
